description: B42.1.0 update: Sandbox options now includes a control for discomfort that will affect the maximum discomfort you will experience from your clothing. This mod affects the rate at which you reach the maximum discomfort level of your clothing, and still works in B42.1.0. If you just want to reduce/disable the total discomfort from clothing then use sandbox settings, if you want to keep the eventual discomfort but have a longer amount of time before it bothers your character then use this mod. Ever thought "wearing a respirator isn't nice, but it doesn't send me into a spiral of depression within five minutes" or perhaps "wearing a bulletproof vest all day would suck, but surely it takes more than ten minutes before I'm screaming in agony"? This mod slows the rate of discomfort increase, meaning you can wear protective gear for longer before you see the discomfort moodle and associated sadness increase. By default discomfort will go up at 10% but drop back down at 100% speed after removing gear, but these values can be adjusted in sandbox settings. This mod does not affect the maximum discomfort value reached, just how long it takes to get there. FAQ Can this be added to/removed from an existing save? Yes. Can this safely be added to/removed from an existing save? Also yes. Will this mod work in multiplayer? Yes, but due to poor coding there will be performance issues because the main loop will run playerCount^2 times. Which is fine when there is only one player, and I'll fix it before B42 multiplayer. What does the "Ticks between checks" sandbox option do? For performance reasons this mod doesn't correct discomfort every frame. If you're using a mod that showa the discomfort meter directly this will result in it raising and lowering every X frames, which can be distracting. Either turn off the discomfort meter and just wait for moodles to show up, or lower the number of ticks in this setting. A value of 1 will run on every frame update and completely eliminate any flicker, and while I can't notice any performance issue like this it does seem excessive. Main menu Background Framework supports Single image (no more need to split image by tiles) Images will resize, fit and center perfectly at any resolution Any resolution (like ultrawide 3440x1440 or even 4k too) Bonus vanilla image for ultrawide resolution (select it from mods options) Optional lightning image Vanilla like lightning transition (optional, active only if second image provided) Mod menu drop list to select background on the fly (select + apply = done) Image resolution details on drop list items (easy select by your resolution) Possibility to use mulltiple addons to select a background from Select logo: default or none (hide logo) Optional backgrounds randomize (respects aspect ratio of selected background) Optional logo randomize Addons can add custom logos on a list Direct image feed from ProjectZomboid folder (details below) Direct image feed Open ProjectZomboid game folder, create folder named "direct" and copy images into it so framework will find them. background1, background2) (optional) Name background lightning files with accordingly and number after "background" but before "_lightning" (example: background1_lightning, background2_lightning) (optional) Name logo files with number at the end (example: logo1, logo2) Note that files are checked by number one by one ...1,...2,...3 if you skip this order by 10 or more further files won't be read (example with names logo1, logo5, logo16: only logo16 won't be found by framework) Example: Full path example: D:/Steam/steamapps/common/ProjectZomboid/direct/background.png Addons (for content creators) Here is an example mod how to add one or multible backgrounds via lua Background Framework Example If you copy an example make sure that: You changed folders name You changed required item on a steam page Put images into media/ui/backgrounds/ Use unique file names like ModId_something The lua part for background addons is simple Backgroundspictures should be on This mod automatically adjusts and sorts all vehicles into three distinct categories to emphasize the gameplay specific use The goal is to make every vehicle class feel good to have Quiet - The explorers choice, so quiet that barely anyone will know about your presence. Can reach good speeds, though avoid towing other vehicles and leaving the paved roads. (mostly Standard vehicles) Strong - The loot goblin delight, tow whatever wherever. Loud, sluggish and relatively slow. (mostly Heavy Duty vehicles) Fast - Fun and versatile vehicles, on the road they can tow other vehicles on par with Strong class while being quieter. (mostly Sports vehicles) General rules inside each class The heavier the vehicle, the more horse power it will have. This is static and not affected by installed parts or cargo More horse power == more speed == more noise Mod Compatibility Load it after other vehicle mods By default supports KI5 vehicles including Bikes and ATA Jaap Wrungel Should work well with other vehicle mods. You might need to add custom entries to Sandbox Options for example when Quiet (Standard) vehicle like Dash Rancher (OffRoad) is supposed to be Strong (Heavy Duty) follow the example of the default entries This is a direct successor to Offroad Go Brrr and is not meant to be used with it, especially in B42 Compatible with Effortless Towing Notes Should work well with everything Can be added/removed to/from existing saves. Works in Multiplayer When added to existing save the player might have to enter the vehicle or repair the engine for its mechanics UI to be updated with the new stats. Overview : Adds a feature to easily unset alarm settings on Digital Watches and Alarm Clocks. Confirmed to work with Build 41/42 and also work on MP. Features : These features are all enabled by default. You can toggle them enable or disable individually through the options. 1. Show Icon Displays an icon on items with an alarm set. Alarm is set Alarm is ringing If no alarm is set, the icon will not be displayed. 2. Show Unset Menu If an alarm is set, a menu to unset the alarm will be displayed. Executing this menu will unset the alarm without displaying the alarm settings panel. You can also unset alarms for multiple items at once by selecting them in bulk. 3. Auto Unset When an item with an alarm set is obtained, the alarm will automatically be unset. Automatic unsetting only occurs when the item is moved into your inventory or a container you are carrying. Options : These options are available with Mod Options in B41. Show Icon : Toggles the enable/disable setting for the "Show Icon" feature. Show Unset Menu : Toggles the enable/disable setting for the "Show Unset Menu" feature. Auto Unset : Toggles the enable/disable setting for the "Auto Unset" feature. Zombies, items, and objects can ride along as well Sandbox options can be set to change the travel time between floors and various power options -Bodies on the floor will not move in elevators this is being worked on. grappled bodies should be movable How it works Opening context on an elevator button will create an elevator in the room behind it, and set up any other rooms vertically. Once built you should get an option to call or open the door in the button context. If called the elevator will take anything on its floor and move it one floor at a time to you. Inside the elevator will be a panel that will have context to select the floor, when a floor is selected you will be transported to every floor in between until your destination. Context options for climbing and prying the doors will open anywhere inside the elevator Usage Notes The Top floor of the elevator needs power or the whole system will not work If there is no power then the doors can by pried with an option in the context menu The elevator has an emergency stop if you have the key, or sandbox option enabled for it The "Interact" key and left clicking will do things like call the elevator and shut the doors and climb the ladder. Movement keys will change your direction when climbing Building When placing a button the room that will be the shaft must be directly behind the wall the button is on A minimum of 2 buttons must be placed directly vertical with the same x,y coordinates The room must be enclosed by walls, limited to an 8x8 room, on each floor and the button within 2 tiles of 2 elevator doors Important If walls do not exist enclosing the elevator shaft when being created it will leak out and make floors outside of it part of the elevator. this is limited to a max of 8 squares from the panel creation point to not cause stack overflow Once a floor is chosen the elevator will go until it reaches that floor, any context on the panel is disabled,other than the emergency stop, until then because choosing floors while moving can cause issues. When reloading a game the elevator lights may turn off, opening context on the panel should fix this Utility Functions All with a wrench or screwdriver equipped opening context on a button will give a reset option that will delete the elevator reverting it to default state, floors will not be replaced opening context on or near the vanilla doors will give an option to place buttons this will place any buttons that were meant to spawn near these doors if i have them in the system I spend countless hours working on mods. If you enjoy my mods, and are able to, please donat, contributions are greatly appreciated and sometimes may keep my lights on Ko-Fi Check out my other mods Beds have blankets, Functional Clotheslines , Gun's Posters Workshop ID: 3411580812 Mod ID: Gelevator Mod ID: Gelevator

description: Add extra sandbox options to your Bandits experience Includes: NEW: Integrate modded weapons lists for NPCs using configurable weapons loadout options Prevent bandits from knowing your location without ever seeing you by disabling Raider AI type for all waves with a single option Rebalance bandit melee attacks by preventing them from cancelling their attack animations Global bandit spawn chance modifiers Random group sizes Random health, ammo, and loot amounts Prevent bandits from spawning near your base Adjust timer before bandits may occupy buildings you've visited Toggle gore/visible injuries on NPCs You can disable generators and vehicle sound effects for a years-later vibe Prevent duplication of weapons on dead NPCs Day 1: Randomise equipment of NPC groups, adjust starting companions,disable nuke Week 1: Randomise equipment of NPC groups, adjust time before you are attacked for trespassing, toggle air strikes Compatibility Notes For use with BANDITS, DAY ONE, WEEK ONE (B42) and WEEK ONE (B41) by Slayer As Bandits is still being developed by Slayer, compatibility issues may arise following updates to the main mod. Compatible weapon mods Brita's Weaponpack Firearms Firearms Revamped Vanilla Firearms Expansion CJ Firearms Rain's Firearms Real Firearms Guns of 93 Guns of 93 (B42) Post Soviet Armory If you encounter any issues please report them here. Credits Full credit to Slayer for his amazing creation, BANDITS! All functions of this mod are derived fromthe butchery ofhis code. Buy him a coffee! Thanks to Choko, Бен, VVentos and fleshka812 for translations! Thanks to DrStalker, Albion and Spongie for coding advice! Instructions If playing with Day One/Week One or weapon mods, you should ensure that all Extra Options mods are loaded afterwards in mod load order (bottom right of mods screen in B42) Most options are accessed from Sandbox settings. To customise, you'll need to start a new game, use Debug mode, or an appropriate mod Detailed options for the mod are found on the Bandits Extra Options sandbox page and are added to each Wave screen. Sandbox Options Allow "Raider" AI In the BANDITS release of 9/2/25 default Raider behaviour was turned off for most spawns. This setting still prevents Raider-type attacks in Day/Week One as well as random AI settings. New Melee Rebalance When a bandit engages the player from the zero distance, they perform a shove which knocks the player away or down, and start their next attack immediately, before the shove animation has played. This setting should prevent them from cancelling attack animations like this, making melee combat more intuitive. General spawn multiplier Percentage multiplier for NPC spawning chance, modifies base spawn chance for all waves, defender and camp spawn chances. Spawn chance in wrong terrain Chance for bandits to spawn in areas they avoid. World age for wave progression By default wave progression resets when you create a new character in the same world; this ties progression to world age instead. Random bandit group size Choose a minimum and maximum size for each bandit wave; invalidates the existing "Group Size" setting. Random bandit health Choose a minimum and maximum health for each bandit wave. Random bandit ammo Choose a minimum ammo count for each bandit wave. Mag count will be random between listed amount and minimum. Random bandit loot A multiplier that affects the chance for bandits to carry additional loot items. Player base minimum spawn radius Define a radius around player bases within which bandits cannot spawn. Days before visited building may be occupied Choose the number of days before defenders may occupy a building you have visited. For a building to count as "visited" you should remain inside for 10 game minutes. Occupied buildings have generators How often generators will spawn at bandit safehouses. Generator type will be randomly chosen. Allow sandbag roadblocks Sandbag roadblocks are a new option which can replace or complement the existing vehicle roadblocks. Vehicle sound effects on bandit spawning Large groups of bandits spawn with car or helicopter sound effects by default, which some players may prefer to disable. Allow gore Display injuries NPCs that take damage. Spawn icons do not show hostility Spawn marker icons will no longer show if NPCs are friendly or hostile. Who is there? You'll have to find out... Loadout and special weapons You can assign a weapons loadout of your choice for each bandit wave. You can also define the probability a bandit will spawn with a "special weapon" for that loadout type. Civilian: Handguns and single shot rifles. Police: Semi-automatic rifles and SMGs. Special weapons are automatic and sniper rifles. Military: US-type automatic rifles. Special weapons are sniper rifles and LMGs. Exotic: Weapons of rare and/or non-US origin. Special weapons include SMGs and sniper rifles. Looted: Lower quality weapons loadout for desperate bandits. Special weapons include automatics. Sandbox Options for Day One Starting equipment Start with some equipment to match your profession. Starting companions Start with a random family of NPCs, a group of co-workers, or nobody. Randomise groups NPC groups spawning during Day One will no longer carry identical weapons. Enable nuke Day One need not end with a bang. Sandbox Options for Week One Trespass grace period Choose how long it will take for inhabitants of buildings to attack, if you trespass. Randomise groups NPC groups spawning during Week One will no longer carry identical weapons. Enable bombing Toggle fire-bombing. Enable gas attacks Toggle gas bombing. Enable A10 attacks Toggle machine gun air attacks.

Electric Weapons Electric weapons work like regular weapons when inactive, but they can be switched into electric mode when they have battery power and their circuitry is still functional. When electric mode is active, each swing consumes battery charge. Battery consumption varies depending on the weapon, and stronger weapons usually consume more power. Electric mode also gives each weapon its own bonus. For example, spear-type weapons can gain extra attack range, while heavy blunt weapons can gain more damage and critical hit potential. By default, electric weapons also gain an increase to maximum attack targets while electric mode is active, but this only matters when multi-hit is enabled. Malfunction System Electric weapons are built from scrap parts, improvised wiring and unstable circuitry. Because of that, their circuits can degrade during combat. The higher the malfunction risk, the more likely the weapon is to break down and lose access to electric mode until repaired. The malfunction system is mainly affected by: Electrician Level — affects the base malfunction probability. Maintenance Level — affects how much malfunction risk is added with each swing. Note: malfunction risk and malfunction probability are not the same thing. Risk builds up over time, while probability determines whether the circuit actually fails. Electric Mode Toggle Electric mode can be configured in: Options → Mods → Mad Crafter You can also assign a hotkey for toggling electric mode. No hotkey is assigned by default. The G key is recommended. Scrap Weapons and Tools Mad Crafter also adds a collection of improvised scrap weapons and multi-purpose tools inspired by makeshift survival gear, movies, and games. Current scrap weapons and tools include: Cleaver Axe Dagger Trident Extinguisher Maul RailSpike Spear Nail-Spiked ShortSword Pipe Wrench Hatchet Saw Blade Claw Wrench Knife Zulu Short Spear Dagger Hatchet Saw Blade Bolt Cutters Keychain Screwdriver Yes, you can now hang a screwdriver on your keychain. Recipe Unlocks Electric Weapons To craft electric shock weapons, you must either: Find Electrician Maniac's Diary, or Have an Electrician level higher than the recipe requirement. Wild / Scrap Weapons To craft certain improvised weapons, you must either: Find Hollywood Weapons Encyclopedia, or Have the required skill level plus one extra level. Sandbox Options Mad Crafter includes sandbox settings so you can adjust the experience to your liking. You can configure: Electric weapon malfunction factor. Electric weapon battery consumption factor. This allows you to make electric weapons more reliable, more fragile, more efficient, or more battery-hungry depending on the type of playthrough you want. Translations The mod currently supports: Chinese English Russian French Russian translation thanks to ph0. French translation thanks to Bobitec. B42 Compatibility Update Mad Crafter has been updated for Project Zomboid Build 42. This version includes compatibility work for the newer B42 mod structure, item script changes, registered item tags, translation formats, and Lua loading paths. Supported builds: Build 42.12.3 Build 42.13.2 Build 42.14.1 Build 42.15.3 Build 42.16.3 Build 42.17.0 Build 42.18.0 Bug Reports If you encounter a bug, please report it in the discussion section. Useful information to include: Your Project Zomboid build number. Whether you are playing single-player or multiplayer. Any relevant console/log errors. A short description of what happened before the bug occurred. Your mod list, if the issue may be caused by a conflict. Future Update Ideas Possible future plans include: Reworking some weapon textures to reduce the use of very dark colors. Adding more electric shock weapons. Adding more scrap-based weapons. Adding more convenient tools. Adding more world items to support crafting and exploration. Exploring dual-mode weapons, such as weapons that can attack with different sides. Possibly experimenting with flame weapons once B42 becomes more stable. Suggestions and feedback are welcome. True Smoking This mod provides a more realistic and immersive smoking experience. Smoking is no longer a short action but now a tracked and passively handled mechanic where the stats and effects are distributed over time while smoking. There is also a optional Nicotine System that implements Addiction and Withdrawal Smoking Light a smoke as normal, any restrictive headgear will be taken off. After lighting, a moodle will appear tracking the progress of your smoke. You can take puffs manually or enable passive smoking and your character will take puffs when idle or when the smoke is about to go out! Dynamic Burn Rate The smoke will burn faster as you puff or move around, when idle it will slowly go out. If it goes out you can relight it to keep smoking. Smokes can be put out and saved for later, the amount left will be visible on the item tooltip. Cigars, pipes, and cigarillos are more effective than a single cigarette so you don't need to smoke the whole thing to get the same effects as a single cigarette! Freedom Lighting, puffing, and putting out the smoke are timed actions that your character performs, after a smoke has been lit you can now do whatever you like while smoking. Take puffs whenever you want but make sure your smoke doesn't go out or you will need to relight it or save it for later! Nicotine System The Nicotine system adds Nicotine, Addiction, and Withdrawal. This system allows the Smoker trait to be dynamically lost and gained based on Addiction levels. Nicotine is accumulated while smoking and leads to Addiction over time. Nicotine provides small amounts of fatigue and hunger reduction. Withdrawal causes small amounts of boredom and unhappyness gain. There are various traits that effect the metabolism rate of Nicotine on the player and your tolerance level varies based on Addiction. The more addicted you are the less effective smokes become at completely removing your stress. This system is completely optional and can be turned off in the Sandbox Options if desired. Features Save Game Compatible! Controller support Split-screen support Compatible with Smoker Trait and most mods Options and Settings configurable via Sandbox Options and Mod Options All vanilla smokes compatible with visual item displayed on face! Controls Default Keyboard K - Tap to take a short puff, hold to keep puffing. Will light a cigarette or unpack one. Relights the smoke when if it goes out. ; (semi colon) - Puts the smoke out. Re-equips headgear that was taken off. Controller Button prompts will appear when the corresponding action can be done. LB is a modifier key that when held changes the B action as follows below: LB + B = Get/Light Cigarette LB + B = Put Out Smoke / Re-equip headgear B = (Hold) Take Puff / Relight Configurable I have made most of the mod configurable through Sandbox Options and in-game Mod Options. Most features can be toggled, or tuned to your liking. All vanilla smoke items can have their properties changed to have different smoking times, burn characteristics and effectiveness. The Nicotine system which adds more depth to the Smoker trait can be tweaked or turned off completely if desired, this system also allows the Smoker Trait to be gained or lost over time. Moodles can be toggled off or on if desired. I review comments almost daily and add options and fix bugs as quickly as I can so feel free to leave feedback or requests. I would highly recommend checking the in-game Mod Options to help configure the behaviour of the mod to your liking as there are many options to help automate smoking or you can disable them to make it completely manual. I've also added a config system for modders to directly integrate into the True Smoking system, some mods may require their authors to add a config to fully support their OnEat methods Future Updates Custom Animations Mod support as requested and needed Further tweaks, options, etc Do not modify or redistribute my mod/code without consent, ask for permission. La idea surgio en el foro reddit cuando debatimos acerca de como afecta las temperaturas bajas a los zombies. Soy fanatico de los comics de Walking Dead por lo que siempre me gusto la idea de un invierno gelido en el cual la supervivencia pasa mas por sobrevivir a las duras condiciones junto a la falta de comida por lo que queria dejar a los zombies de lado por un tiempo. Si quieres este estilo de juego este mod es para vos. Los zombies se congelan cuando llegan a una temperatura baja indicada como pasa en los inviernos de TWD.. Nueva UPDATE con caracteristicas nuevas. Deberia ser totalmente compatible con B41. Ahora puedes elegir una fase previa a la congelación, haciendo de esta manera que la congelación sea más progresiva y natural, con el tiempo si es muy solicitado agregaré distintas fases, pero por ahora con una debería bastar. ¿Cómo funciona? En el menú sandbox podrás elegir si activar o no está característica y también podrás definir la temperatura necesaria para que eso ocurra. Intenta poner siempre una temperatura superior a la de congelación para que no pasen cosas raras, no fue testeado que pasaría si no lo haces. La temperatura de congelación y pre-congelacion son seleccionables en el menú sandbox así como también la cantidad de tiempo que la temperatura de congelacion debe permanecer para que el zombie finalmente se congele. En las opciones por defectos los parámetros se mantendrán en -5 °C para congelación, 0 °C para pre-congelacion y 30 minutos del juego para que los zombies pasen a estado sólido. Los zombies a su vez tienen un termómetro interno, si están cerca de un incendio y se calientan lo suficiente volverán a moverse, en los interiores los zombies no estarán congelados por que la temperatura es mucho mas alta. _______________________________________________________________ The idea came up on the Reddit forum when we discussed how low temperatures affect zombies. I'm a fan of The Walking Dead comics, so I always liked the idea of a harsh winter where survival is more about enduring the harsh conditions and lack of food, rather than just fighting zombies. If you want this type of gameplay, this mod is for you. Zombies freeze when they reach a low temperature, just like in The Walking Dead winters. New UPDATE with new features. Should be fully compatible with B41. Now you can choose a pre-freezing phase, making the freezing process more progressive and natural. If there's enough demand, I'll add more phases in the future, but for now, one should be enough. How does it work? In the sandbox menu, you can choose whether to enable or disable this feature and also define the temperature required for it to happen. Always try to set a temperature above freezing to avoid any issues, as it hasn't been tested what would happen if you don't. The freezing and pre-freezing temperatures are selectable in the sandbox menu, as well as the amount of time the freezing temperature must remain for the zombie to finally freeze. In the default options, the parameters will remain at -5°C for freezing, 0°C for pre-freezing, and 30 minutes of gameplay for zombies to become solid. Zombies also have an internal thermometer; if they are near a fire and heat up enough, they will move again. Inside buildings, zombies will not be frozen because the temperature is much higher. Does dismantling a functional car produce more raw materials than a wreck/burnt out car? Additional materials are generated based on the condition of the vehicle's parts. description: After much consideration and between being very busy with RL and other projects and also some major PZ burnout, I’m officially suspending development of this mod. It’s been a while since I’ve had a chance to even try to write an update and that doesn’t appear to be changing any time soon. While it is missing some requested features and will have incompatibilities with certain weapon mods that employ script swaps for things like bayonet use or stock folding (this mod already includes compatibility files with some major ones like Britas and VFE), it is very functional in its current form and has behaved well over 200+ hours of testing. As it stands, it should remain in good shape for B41, but may become increasingly less reliable as B42 continues development in its unstable branch. I may try to come back to it and polish it up once B42 is released into stable. So cheers! May your sprinters always stumble and your bags overflow with ammo! 🍺 The new and much improved version of Legend Craft - Melee Weapons and Guns & Grenades Available for B41 and B42, Legend Craft Evolved lets you take duplicates of the weapons you find and, with tools, materials, and skill levels, combine them into ever more powerful variants. Works with vanilla and many major weapon mods including Brita's, VFE, Scrap Guns, and more. The mod defaults to requiring a hammer and 5 nails for every upgrade, allows the first upgrade on level 1 of that weapon's combat skill, and an additional upgrade per level until the weapon has reached Mark 10. For those who are familiar with the original's shortcomings, Legend Craft Evolved now also retains all tool functionalities as well. This is achieved through the use of a script-less and recipe-less craftlike system that checks your inventory and prompts you with the option to upgrade in your right-click inventory menu. There is also a feedback system through character speech to inform you what is missing to proceed with an upgrade. The mod also has a ton of sandbox choices split between two menus - Options & Values. There, you can decide Which weapon attributes to allow for upgrade (damage is the only non-optional value) How much each upgrade increases those attributes What tool or tool type to use (B42 has up to three choices from 29 types to consider) What materials to use, with 5 different choices in B41 and 7 choices in B42 (to be expanded in updates) What skill level to check for progress - Combat, Maintenance, Carpentry, Electrical, or Metalworking The option to prevent upgraded weapons from breaking or from taking any condition loss at all And more! There is also a token system to preserve upgrades should a weapon fall to pieces in B42 or be accidentally consumed as a craft ingredient. Everything is explained in detail in a HOW-TO.txt file included in the mod folder. So upgrade the things! Get too overconfident! Die terribly! That's how I use it anyway. NOTE: When uninstaling the mod, upgrades are left as artifacts. So the mod includes a 'Reclaim Mode' which gives item refunds for all upgrades to be used before a mid-save uninstall. SPECIAL THANKS Taylor MH for the Spanish translation Hx for the Korean translation and info about correct encoding for it Vilespring - co-developer of Vanilla Firearms Expansion - for pointing out that VFE's folded stocks likely needed special attention kin1555 for identifying a critical bug where upgrades were losing some values on exiting and reloading the game CdrCantees for identifying a critical bug involving upgrade function not functioning properly when level and skill check requirements were removed NuEvE for finding a major bug where artifacts would remain in the player's hands if a secondary equipped weapon was used to upgrade a primary or unequipped weapon or a primary was used to upgrade a secondary Vasher for reporting a pair of bugs that could cause crashes under certain circumstances MUSIC Upgrade Jingle: Excerpt of Banjo opener by Simonays https://freesound.org/s/533545/ License: Attribution 4.0 Remixed by Marbo Dreadnought Workshop ID: 3432470769 Mod ID: LegendCraftEvolvedB41 Mod ID: LegendCraftEvolvedB42

description: Shoving and stomping now carries a risk of being counterattacked. Highly customizable. NOTE: Temp fix for b42.19. Traits have no effect in the mod with b42.19. Full repair is WIP. No change on b42 version. Ever wonder why zombies become helpless when they're knocked over? Or why you never get bitten when you're shoving away a horde and putting your limbs right in front of their gnashing faces? Or maybe you just feel too powerful curb stomping dozens of zombies and walking away without a scratch on the first day? The idea behind this mod is to simulate the risk of fighting zombies without any range advantage. In short, it introduces a small chance for any one shove or stomp to backfire and result in a wound on the attacker with the same consequences of a normal zombie attack. This change discourages fighting when unprepared, especially at the very beginning of the game. Any last-resort improvised weapon becomes safer than going unarmed. In this time it might be better to flee and break line of sight than to kill a threat with your bare hands. When you do get a weapon, it becomes very important to keep zombies outside the weapon's minimum range so your melee attacks aren't automatically swapped into shoves. Crowd control with low-knockback weapons should be more difficult. The practice of preserving weapon durability by using unarmed is now risky. By default it's safe to shove zombies who are unalerted, facing away from the player, or who have already counterattacked a player within the last couple seconds. The player also has a separate shorter grace period after being counterattacked. Wearing armor on your limbs can reduce or eliminate the danger from this mod. The strength and fitness skills affect the chance of being injured, as do the thick and thin skinned traits. Almost every part of the mod is customizable in sandbox options so you can use as much or as little of it as you want. For example, you could configure the mod to: - Simulate the roughness of unarmed combat without actually being "attacked" by zombies by disabling all wounds except non-infectious scratches on the hands and feet, ignoring defense and not causing holes in clothing. With this setup you might get blisters or abrasions on those parts but it shouldn't ever be directly lethal. - Enable shove safety when holding two-handed weapons, allowing you to safely push zombies away using brooms, planks, or other long weapons. You could even hold something like a pillow to protect yourself from being bitten if you set shove safety to recognize "any item" - Set shoving to only affect the forearms, and stomping to only affect the feet; that way the counterattacks from this mod can be absorbed by more easily accessible clothes. Assuming you aren't using mods that add armor for the hands and shins. - Set the cooldown very high to (in effect) prevent a zombie from counterattacking you more than once. In case you want the risk to still be significant but don't like the chance of being ripped to shreds because you won an unarmed fight. I personally play with low-pop vaulting runners and transmission off. If you play with high pop, shamblers, or transmission on, this mod might make less sense or feel excessively punishing. It was just bothering me that my character could 1v1 a rabid monster the size of a full grown human while bare-handed and at little to no personal risk. Note: I have not tested this in multiplayer or with most other mods. I don't see a reason why it wouldn't work, but let me know if it doesn't and I'll mention incompatibilities here. B41 version: -> military_burnt (burnt military vehiles; determined by the presence of "burnt" in the vehicle's script name) -> military_container (containers added by the mod Containers!; determined by the presence of "container" in the vehicle's script name) -> military_trailer (trailers; determined by the presence of "trailer" in the vehicle's script name) -> military_trailer_light (only small trailers; determined if offroad efficiency of trailer is less than or equal to 1) -> military_trailer_heavy (only huge heavy trailers; determined if offroad efficiency of trailer is more than 1) -> military_vehicle (military cars; remainder after sorting) -> military_vehicle_light (light military cars; determined if (mass*engineForce)/(maxSpeed*1000) is less than or equal 60) -> military_vehicle_heavy (heavy military cars; B42.13.0 update: after testing this mod is still working (NOTE: tested in single player only) Updated for 42.9.0! > Made vehicle headlights extend much farther. The latest update made headlights a lot better... but they could be even brighter! This mod has been updated using the new functionality in B42.9.0 for the best headlights ever, without any manual java file installation. Anyone using the main mod will have it automatically updated to version 3 if they are using Zomboid 42.9 or later (same modID, new code & name). The 2.0 WIP version has been removed, and the Java mod is now depreciated. Bonus update: you can now toggle high beams using the radial menu (this can be disabled in mod options) --- High Beams! Because driving at night needs more than 8 feet of visibility. This mod adds high-beams you can toggle on/off that give your headlights extra distance and (optionally) light up the immediate area around the car. Credits 十叁 for their mod BrighterHeadlights which showed me the final missing piece to make the first version of this mod Indie Stone for updating the headlight code to make more available via lua. Fkekexue for the radial menu icon FAQ How do I use this mod? First, you need to be playing B42 and you need a vehicle with working headlights. Then get in your car and toggle high-beam mode with the hotkey (set to '.' by default.) The headlight indicator will be blue when headlights are on and in high-beam mode. What do the options do? In Options -> Mods -> High Beams you can change a few settings: Keybind: The key to toggle high beams Always On: high beams are always on automatically Length multiplier: default length is 36 tiles, this lets you increase that distance Intensity Multiplier: allows you to blind other drivers with your aftermarket xenon bulbs Radial Menu: Adds a high beam toggle to the vehicle radial menu. Debug Mode: Prints extra info to console. After changing settings turn high beams off and on again for them to take effect. Does this mod work in B41? This mod is B42 only. description: Realistically harvest rain water from a building's roof by connecting a container to the gutter's drain. Tap into existing gutters or build your own custom gutter system using a variety of new craftable gutter pipes. FAQ Does this mod work in multiplayer (build 42.13+)? Yes, the mod has been updated with initial multiplayer support. Servers will use the default mod options (1.0 rain factor, pipe wrench required) until configurable sandbox values are added in a future update. Can this mod be safely added mid-save? Yes, but it will not change any already existing collectors that happen to be placed on a gutter tile. Can this mod be safely removed mid-save? Yes, but any existing collectors on a gutter tile will keep their increased rain factor. Do gutter collectors work indoors? No, currently they still require being outdoors without a covered overhead tile. What can I connect to the gutter All vanilla rain collectors, troughs, and the amphora are supported. Additionally, any modded entities that use the game's FluidContainer system should work out of the box such as the Useful Barrels mod. Does this work for build 41? This mod relies on systems introduced in build `42.4+` and will not function in build `41`. How To Use Build/place supported collector on the same tile as a gutter drain. Either tile works for multi-tile troughs. Open the context menu by right-clicking on the collector. Find the "Gutter Drain" submenu and select the "Connect" option. Requires a pipe wrench unless turned off in mod settings. Enjoy the benefits of a highly-efficient rain collector system. Pre-Existing Structures Pre-existing structures already have roof gutters meaning you won't have to build your own. To tap into these roof gutters, you will either need to find a building with an existing drain pipe or build a new drain pipe. On its own a drain pipe will reach the next level above. Additional vertical pipes can be built on top of the drain pipe to access roofs on higher floor levels. Player-Built Structures Unlike pre-existing structures, player-built structures will require horizontal gutter pipes to expand the size of the roof's area being covered by the drain pipe. Each gutter pipe can collect rain from up to 4 grid-squares from its attachment point in a line. A roof square will be considered valid if it has a floor, isn't covered by a roof, and isn't occupied by an item such as a rain collector. Use the "View Pipes" and "View Roof" buttons in the gutter ui panel to help visualize the connected pipes and covered roof area. Mod Settings Options -> Mods -> Functional Gutters Removing Mod from Multiplayer As of 42.13.1, there is an extra step required to properly remove the mod from multiplayer servers. This step is not specific Functional Gutters and will be required for any mods that add custom entities until a fix is added in the base game. Steps to remove the mod Remove any player-crafted gutters from the game world - not required but will prevent invisible asset warnings being logged Stop the server Backup the server files if not done automatically on server shutdown Remove the mod from the server settings Locate and delete the following server files: WorldDictionary.bin, WorldDictionaryLog, WorldDictionaryReadable - location may differ but for hosted files on windows will be Users/<user name>/Zomboid/Saves/Multiplayer/<server name> Start the server back up - this will automatically regenerate the WorldDictionary files and allow clients to connect without crashing But why do I need to do all of this? The client syncs its own local copy of the server's WorldDictionary when connecting to the server. Any custom entities will still exist in the server's WorldDictionary with the flag removed=True whenever a mod is removed. Unfortunately in the current version of project zomboid multiplayer, this flag appears to be ignored and the client will crash with a reference error since the referenced entity scripts no longer exist for it locally. Deleting the server's WorldDictionary files forces the server to recreate them from scratch and they will no longer contain any entities from the removed mod allowing the client to properly connect once again. View on github for more information Workshop ID: 3439305933 Mod ID: FunctionalGutters

description: The Best Lockpicking Old Mod, New Features! [p]"The Best Lockpicking" is a mod for Project Zomboid that adds realistic lockpicking mechanics and vehicle hijacking, expanding your survival options in the zombie apocalypse world. Forget about simply finding keys — now you’ll need to use your skills, tools, and a bit of luck to open doors, windows, and cars, or even break locks at the risk of damaging them permanently.[/p] TIP: [p]I recommend disabling “Separate Interface Processing” in the UI settings for smoother mini-game windows![/p] WARNING! To avoid errors, it is recommended to unsubscribe and resubscribe to the mod. Description: Adds realistic lockpicking mechanics for doors, windows, and vehicles using lockpicks or a crowbar. Lockpicking is performed through engaging mini-games! Introduces a hotwiring mini-game for stealing cars — feel like a real car thief. Allows you to check for alarms in houses and vehicles to avoid making unnecessary noise. Adds the “Lockpicking” skill, which affects success rate and speed. Introduces the “Lockpicker” perk and expands the “Burglar” profession for deeper role immersion. Key Features: Lockpicking System: Use lockpicks and screwdrivers for careful lockpicking of doors and windows with a mini-game that depends on your “Lockpicking” skill level. Use a crowbar for brute force — break locks with a chance of damaging them permanently. Vehicle Breaking: Open cars using a crowbar or lockpicks by completing mini-games that vary depending on the vehicle type. Feel like an electrician with the new Hotwiring feature — an interactive wire-connecting system where mistakes can trigger the alarm or headlights! (Not entirely realistic, I know.) Alarm Inspection: Inspect buildings and vehicles for active alarms before attempting to pick the lock to avoid attracting zombies. Realistic Interaction: The “Strength” and “Lockpicking” skills affect both success chance and lockpicking speed. Fatigue (Endurance) reduces efficiency — be careful not to overexert yourself! For details, see the changelog. Items: Lockpicking Magazine — Teaches the basics of lockpicking. Alarm Magazine — Grants the ability to check for alarms. Lockpick — Used for lockpicking along with a screwdriver. Improvised Lockpick — Crafted from paperclips (requires a screwdriver!). Guide to the New Lockpicking Mini-Game Game Overview [p]You need to control tension and lift the pins to open the lock. Each lock has a unique combination.[/p] Controls Mouse: Hover your cursor under a pin to interact. Lift the pin by moving the mouse upward. Tension Control Keys: A: Decrease tension. D: Increase tension. Hold the key for smooth adjustment. Game Mechanics Pins: Lift each pin to its setting point. Tension: Adjust the tension (shown in the top panel) within the indicated limits (for example, 3–5). Exceeding the limits increases the chance of breaking your pick or the lock. Hand Tremor: Your “Lockpicking” skill level and current tension affect random hand shake (chance increases with high tension and low skill). Compatibility: Tested on Project Zomboid build 42+. There are currently issues with some mods (the lockpicking mode can be interrupted when pressing movement or action keys): True Crawl — compatible (integrated patch). Common Sense — compatible (disable “Crowbar Mechanic” in sandbox settings). Want to Thank Me? Buy Me a Coffee. description: Compatible with Build 42.12 up to Build 42.19 Drink only what you need. Drink Smart adds a “0% Thirst” option to the drink context menu, letting your character drink only the exact amount needed to fully quench thirst instead of wasting extra sips. How it works Right-click a drink in the inventory, container, or ground panel. Open Drink or Open and Drink for sealed containers. Choose 0% Thirst to drink only enough to reach 0 thirst. If there is not enough liquid, the option appears disabled with a tooltip. Vanilla drink options are unchanged. Note: This applies to the context menu in inventory-style panels, not to right-clicking items placed directly in the world. Sandbox option AllowWaterDrinkLowThirst (default: OFF) Allows water containers to show drink options even when thirst is below 0.1. Only changes that restriction — all other vanilla rules still apply. Compatibility Works from Build 42.12 up to Build 42.16 Supports the relevant Build 42 Steam branches Safe to enable or disable before loading a save Not compatible with Build 41 Possible conflicts Should be compatible with most mods Possible conflicts with mods that modify the drink context menu In particular, mods that overwrite these functions may conflict: ISInventoryPaneContextMenu.createMenu ISInventoryPaneContextMenu.doDrinkFluidMenu ISInventoryPaneContextMenu.onDrinkFluid More mods & feedback My other Project Zomboid mods If you find it useful, please consider leaving a thumbs up and adding it to your favorites. Feedback is always welcome. description: Updated version for b42 of my mod Time Decreases Car Condition. HOW IT WORKS This mod adds a chance to greatly damage/remove vehicle parts CHECKED ONCE, WHEN THEY SPAWN. That chance will increase as time passes and can be customized in sandbox settings. Once a vehicle has been checked for damage (when they spawn), IT IS NEVER CHECKED AGAIN. This means that the vehicles that have spawned at the start of the game around the player WILL NEVER GET DAMAGED AGAIN. It is only the new vehicles spawning when the player explore the map, that get damaged. Inspired by Planetalgol's "Worse Vehicle Condition". All credits go to him for the orginial idea. The Sandbox Settings : Start Day : (default = 1) Peak Day : (default = 50) Start Chance to damage/remove parts : (default = 1) Applied before and on Start Day. Peak Chance to damage/remove parts : (default = 50 ) Applied after and on Peak Day. Check chance for removing parts: (default = true ) Uncheck this to disable removing parts Check chance for damaging parts: (default = true ) Uncheck this to disable damaging parts Check chance for breaking locks: (default = true ) Uncheck this to disable breaking locks Check chance for decreasing battery charge: (default = true ) Uncheck this to disable decreasing battery charge Check chance for deflating tires: (default = true ) Uncheck this to disable deflating tires Vehicle part chance multipliers: Chance multipliers for each type of part Starting from the Start Day, the chance to damage/remove parts will gradually increase until it reaches the peak chance, on Peak Day. After Peak Day the Peak Chance is always applied. For reference : to have it on the same level as Planetalgol's worse vehicle condition you would need to set the chance ~= 40 %. Note : The chance is applied ON EACH VEHICLE PART of a vehicle, and more often than not, it is applied more than once per vehicle part. It is not only once per vehicle. So if you set more than 50% that is extremely high! A different fraction of the chance is applied to different vehicle parts. Some are applied the full chance once, others are applied half the chance, but twice. You can tweak these chances with the sandbox settings. Compatibility : It should work with most vehicle mods. Workshop ID: 3448375286 Mod ID: TimeDecreasesCarConditionB42

description: Porting Cheat Menu Phoenix mod to Build 42. B41 Re-upload of the Cheat Menu Phoenix mod. This mod, which worked perfectly for the B41, mysteriously disappeared from the workshop. I'm reposting it for those who might need it. I am not the creator of this mod. Announcement : This mod has been updated again for Build 42 ! Thanks to BlaBla from LoversLab site for continuing the port of this mod to B42 ! Build 42 Change Log 2.15 : Added - "Zombie Population" window (zombie radar) Added - Vehicle skin switching (e.g., Trailer Advert) Added - Option to remove ONLY corpses from the ground (preserves all furniture and other world objects) Fixed - Vehicle rust editing window now reopens correctly after being closed Fixed - Unable to reload weapons when using instant actions mode What remains to be fixed : Nothing What remains to be added (maybe?) : Infinite Fluid Refill Equipped Fluid Item Third-party mod Vehicle Spawner Features B42 : Health Control Item Spawner Vehicle Spawner with condition at 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% Climate control Mode : God / Ghost / Prevent Death Player Stats Menu Creative Mode (Lets you disassemble/destroy anything, NOT a building cheat) Barricade Mode Instant Actions Infinite Carry Weight Night Vision Zombie Population Radar Repair : Clothes / Items Time Control Sandbox Settings Menu Teleportation Mode Terrain : Terraform / Delete / Brush Tool Fire Control Zombie Spawner Animal Spawner Mood Control Immuning Stats Set Skill Level Recipes Control Multiplayer mode : This mod is designed to work ONLY in single-player mode. This mod does NOT function in multiplayer. This mod does NOT support cheating in multiplayer. Cheating in single-player is harmless and therefore allowed, but this mod will never support multiplayer: TIS and we do not condone cheating in multiplayer. For multiplayer games, please use your administrator (admin) privileges. In multiplayer with your friends, if you are an admin, you can use many features that are provided by TIS. If you are not an admin, you can ask your server’s admin to use their privileges to access the features provided by TIS. In multiplayer, you don’t need a cheat mod, as there are already options to teleport, spawn items, and so on. Note for Vehicle Color Change and Time Warp features : The vehicle color change menu works. However, not all vehicles can be recolored. Some police vehicles have a texture that doesn’t accept color changes. On the other hand, vehicles such as the "Masterson Horizon" can be repainted. The Time Warp menu works. You must enter a date AFTER the official start date of the pandemic: July 9, 1993. If you enter the following date: 1993 / 10 / 25 and the time 10 / 0 The game will set the date to October 25, 1993 at 10:00 AM Note for Instant Actions and Infinite Carry Weight features : Instant Actions - Since the original method is inaccessible, an alternative procedure has been implemented. Infinite Carry Weight – Since the original method is inaccessible, an alternative procedure has been implemented. Note that it is not truly “infinite,” since the limit of ItemContainer.setCapacity cannot exceed the maximum capacity of 100. The number 100 is a fixed limit, beyond which the console spams an error. Item Spawner window with third-party mods : Cheat Menu Phoenix only reads data from other mods before opening the item spawn window. Some mods add new items to the base game, but these mods are incomplete, malformed, or contain corrupted data. Some data may be missing, such as: getItemType() getIcon() If this data is missing, it will return nil and cause an error to be displayed, BUT the item spawn window will still open, and you will be able to spawn items whose data is available. Cheat Menu Phoenix cannot fix missing data from other mods. If you are using other mods and encounter errors, please contact the developers of the affected mods so they can add the missing data or fix their malformed or corrupted data. This closes error reports related to the item spawn window. This window works perfectly when the data is complete. Unless errors are reported that PREVENT this window from opening, any new red error reports related to this window will be ignored and removed. Thank you for your understanding. description: It's a kick scooter, get your kneepads and hop on! Special thanks to Albion, Sir Doggy Jvla, Paddlefruit, DrStalker, Jimbeamdiablo, and CrystalChris from the Project Zomboid discord for helping answer my questions! There's also a skateboard! And a Bicycle! ------------------------------ FEATURES ------------------------------ A rideable kick scooter that increases movement speed while equipped. Foldeable which decreases weight, so after you're done scooting, you can fold it up and bring it with you. Hold SHIFT to go faster! Press E while near a scooter to hop on, and press E again while riding to hop off (opening doors have priority, so you can open up a door and scoot in easily) When folded it can be equipped and used as a weapon! Riding the scooter without holding SHIFT takes as much stamina as walking (none), and holding shift takes as much stamina as running. The scooter speed can be adjusted in mod options. Immersive Mode toggle in mod options, with it enabled you will go slower on rough surfaces like grass/gravel/sand/dirt. Spawns in schools, toy stores and other places where it makes sense to find a kick scooter. Is affected by leg/foot injuries and health. If you have a broken leg or foot then you can't scoot at all. ------------------------------ PLANNED FEATURES ------------------------------ Add more animations like turning/breaking/falling off Add tricks ---------------------------- KNOWN ISSUES ---------------------------- Mostly just a few animation transitions that can look a bit janky, but let me know if you find any issues! If you have any issues, please join my Discord and post in the Support channel: This mod can only be added to and extended with the express permission from the original creator. Having received permission, credit must be given to the original creator, both within the files of the mod and wherever the mod roams online. If no permission is received you may not alter the mod. description: This mod changes all camo patterns on military-issue clothing to be as accurate to real life as possible, in terms of both the patterns' structures and colors. Additionally, an optional submod enables the spawning of other camos that could be seen in the 90s, but which are not available in vanilla Project Zomboid. The submod is not integrated into the main mod so that players have a choice between having just the base game camos, or an even greater variety of camos to loot in the world. List of vanilla camo patterns covered by this mod: - US Woodland - US Woodland Urban - 6-Color Desert - 3-Color Desert - Tiger Stripe - Red Dawn KLMK - new functionality: jacket and trousers reversible to a winter version of the pattern List of camos covered by Immersive Camos - Period-Accurate Pack*: - Frogskin - items available: Jacket, Trousers, M1 Helmet; 2 color variants; each item reverses from Jungle to Beach camo - Mitchell - items available: M1 Helmet; reverses from Summer to Autumn camo - ERDL - items available: Jacket, Shirt/Blouse, Trousers, Boonie Hat, M1 Helmet; 4 color variants (Lowland, Highland, Transitional, Misprint) + blouses with USMC logo (for all variants except Misprint) * Contents of this pack will spawn naturally ONLY after enabling it. They can be found exclusively in surplus stores. An exception to this are M1 helmets, which - like vanilla - spawn in a bit greater variety of places. To be able to utilize full resolution textures, you must change maximum texture resolution to at least 1024 pixels in the game's settings. Setting the resolution to more than 1024 pixels will not make any difference, as the textures are all 1024x1024 px or, in case of some items, lower. Credits: - Bella from the Project Zomboid Discord, for giving this mod its current name. - Avionics from this item's comments section, for giving me the inspiration to make the Build 41 Pack - link: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3637569245. description: Zomboid onbly allows you to place 50 weight units of stuff on a single tile. description: B42.13 update: moving to unlisted, this mod needs a lot of work to fix and I don't think it's as important as it originally was now that the thumping behavior has changed a bit. B42.13.1 update: Apparently it is still needed if too many zombies are close together, so I'll see if I can get this working in B42.13 (SP first, then MP) NOTE: mod is currently not working in B42.13+ It's on my to-fix list, no ETA. One hundred zombies running down the street to kill you? Meh. Half a dozen zombies banging on a door somewhere in an apartment block? PANIC! This mod limits how much stress you gain from sounds, which in practice means you will not instantly panic when you get too close to big mob of zombies banging on a security grill. Stress will still build up, but at a reduced rate configured in sandbox options. The default cap of 15 seems like a good balance, but you can adjust this to taste. Yes, you can set it to zero and ignore all the bad noises. To completely eliminate stress from cutting down tress, use this mod Behind the scenes: Every tick the game adds up the stress of all stressful sounds, reduced by their distance (ignoring vertical height) from the player and increases your stress based on the total. This mod caps that increase. A single zombie thumping on a door has a maximum stress value of 15 per tick if you stand right next to it, but only when the sound is playing - there's no stress gain between thumps. So the default cap of 15 isn't the same as one zombie banging on a door, unless you squint at the numbers and say "good enough". FAQ Can this mod be added/removed to an existing game? Yes. If a single zombie banging on my door is a stress value of 15, why doesn't my stress value go up by 15 per tick and max out in 1/10th of a second? Because the sound stress is multiplied by 0.00002 before it is applied. The value in the sandbox options is before that multiplication, because it's easier for humans to deal with "15" than "0.0003" Workshop ID: 3460381012 Mod ID: NepStressGainCap

description: Compatible with Build 42.12 to 42.19.0 (SP / MP) Clean Hot Bar redesigns Project Zomboid’s hotbar and hand-equipped UI to make item status easier to read, less intrusive, and more visually intuitive. It improves moment-to-moment readability during gameplay while keeping the interface compact, clear, and customizable. The mod enhances the B42 hotbar with clearer status feedback, refined textures, better weapon and liquid information, and built-in hotbar reordering support, while staying close to the original gameplay flow. B42 Status Display Improvements This mod visually integrates the new weapon and item status systems introduced in B42: Weapon Head Condition: shows a status bar above the slot when a weapon has head condition data Weapon Sharpness: displays both current and maximum sharpness values White: current sharpness Brown: maximum sharpness (see here) Toggleable Items: clear ON / OFF indicators for items such as flashlights Ammo Counter: displays the current ammo count above firearm slots Hand-Equipped UI Improvements The hand-equipped UI has also been improved to show more detailed item information in a cleaner way. Original textures have been refined as well, with added transparency for a smoother and less obstructive appearance. B42 Liquid System Integration The new B42 liquid system is represented with color-coded bars, making it easier to identify liquid contents at a glance. Some colors were initially generated with AI assistance, so feedback is welcome if you notice anything that looks inaccurate. Animation Effects The visual effects are designed to be noticeable without becoming distracting: Durability Shake: items shake when durability decreases, such as battery drain Flashing Effect: durability values flash when going down Liquid Drain Animation: smooth visual feedback when liquids are consumed Weapon Warning: a warning appears above the character’s head when the equipped weapon loses durability; this can be disabled in the settings panel Customizable Settings Disable status displays for a more hardcore experience Adjust the height of status bars Enable tooltips (default: off) to show item details on hover Scale the size of the hotbar Toggle the weapon durability warning animation above the character Use the built-in hotbar reorder controls from the settings panel Built-in Hotbar Reordering Clean Hot Bar includes built-in hotbar reordering support. The reorder controls are available from the settings panel, keeping the hotbar itself cleaner and less cluttered. This means Reorder The Hotbar is usually not needed when using Clean Hot Bar. Compatibility Compatible with current B42 builds up to 42.19.0 For best results, place Clean Hot Bar near the bottom of your mod load order so other mods load first There may be conflicts with other mods that also add status indicators, modify hotbar tooltips, or heavily override hotbar behavior If the mod does not work as expected, try moving it to the bottom of the load order Reorder The Hotbar is generally not needed, since Clean Hot Bar already includes built-in hotbar reordering If you use Reorder The Hotbar together with Clean Hot Bar, some small visual overlap may still happen. description: Who's the Richest Survivor in Knox Unlocks a few recipes & adds a load more, all allowing you to enrich yourself with Cash, Silver, Gold & Gems Deconstruct Jewellery into tiny fragments for later smelting, saving any Gem stones Unlocks the Ingot mold recipe Combine like items into stacks & then stacks into larger collections & on & on New loot distribution locations for gold, silver, cash & gems You might even be able to bash a zomb over the head with an ingot or two Nothing in this mod is locked or gate kept behind any profession or recipe magazines etc BUT to cast the ingots you'd need the required vanilla steps, like pottery to press the clay mold then a kiln to fire said mold followed by a furnace to cast the ingot. All of the Combination type of recipes also have the opposite recipe to break the item down to its smaller item. This also includes the pallets of ingots BUT to prevent conflicts this does not include the vanilla pallet of gold or any additional pallets added by map mods. All the recipes are located in the crafting menu in a new tab called Extra Money Cash You can stack 10 Money bundles into a pile & 10 piles into a briefcase of cash & 10 briefcases into a Pallet of Cash. Gems There are Diamonds, Rubies, Emeralds, Sapphires & Pearls. These are removed from Jewellery or possible found in the vanilla rare Gem bag items. You can combine them into a pile of 10, 10 piles into a bag & 10 bags into a briefcase of Gems. Metals A new item called Tiny Gold/Silver fragments has been added so you don't lose the metal when you remove any precious gems. Once you get enough metal to start making ingots: Stack 3 ingots to save weight, Stack 3 of those to make a stack of 9. Add 5 of those together to make a pallet of Gold/Silver, Note regarding 42.11 update: This update added the option to "take gold bars" from the vanilla pallets found placed around the world, which will only give you 30 bars. The pallets added by this mod are a different item, and will require/give you 45 bars, I have no idea where the missing 15 bars go from the vanilla pallet. So the vanilla pallets are nice for display purposes but I don't recommend taking the bars, maybe a future update will give us back those missing 15 bars. But why? I dunno, for bragging rights I guess. Maybe when MP hits it'll have a lot more purpose. Its mostly made because I wanted to have something to aim for & a pallet of gold takes a lot of work. For the math orientated users out there, one pallet of gold or silver equates to the following; 45 Ingots 360 Small Bars 1440 Sheets 14400 Small Scrap 288000 Jewellery items So not something you're going to accomplish in the early game. To help reduce the grind, all the items have been added to the loot distribution tables, in the obvious places; banks, jewellery stores, floor stashes, police evidence lockers, pawn stores, maybe some other Easter egg locations. description: KR FriOS Battery-powered refrigeration for the post-apocalypse. Portable fridges, freezers, and stoves powered by rechargeable batteries — not ice packs, not generators. Place them anywhere, load them up, and your food stays fresh. Even if you leave and come back days later. 🧊 Four Systems. One Core Battery. Four dedicated devices, each tuned for a different job — all powered by the same FriOS Battery. Pick the one that fits your mission and swap batteries between them as needed. ⚡ Power System — Charge, Load, Run. From sunlight to runtime. The FriOS Solar Charger recharges FriOS Batteries, vanilla car batteries, and standard cells using real-time ambient light. Load a charged FriOS Battery into any device through the new menu (left-click the device) or by dragging it in the classic way. Once loaded, the device runs on its own — draining to 10% before shutting off automatically to protect the battery's lifespan. 📦 Item Catalog — Including the new FriOS StepVan. Six items and one vehicle. The FriOS StepVan is the latest addition to the line: a delivery van with an industrial freezer integrated into the rear compartment and passive FriOS Battery charging fed directly by the vehicle's own battery. A rolling cold-storage base. All devices come in 3 lines with multiple color options: Solid Color — A single color covering the entire device. Available in: Red, Blue, Orange, Cyan, Green, Black, Pink, White, Yellow, and Purple. Gray Trim Line — Dark gray body with a colored accent stripe matching the Solid Color palette. Special Edition — Two exclusive variants: Spiffo and FriOS. ⚙️ How It Works Place a FriOS Battery inside any FriOS device — left-click to open the menu, or drag it in. Put food (or cookware) inside to activate it. The device runs automatically — no manual switches. Recharge batteries with the FriOS Solar Charger during daylight hours (04:00–20:00). When no player is within 20 tiles, the device drops to suspend mode (10% consumption) — it won't die instantly while you're gone. ⚠️ Known Issues Visual desync inside standard vehicle inventories. If you store a FriOS device with food inside the trunk, glovebox, seats, or any inventory slot of a standard vehicle, the device appears active visually — but once the chunk unloads, the displayed age of the food isn't refreshed with the cold factor applied. The system still tracks the food as refrigerated internally; only the visible age sync fails. Quick fix: take the device out of the vehicle and place it on the ground. As soon as it re-registers, the system recalculates the real age applying the cold factor accumulated during offline time. The food returns to its correct state with no loss of preservation. This specific case (device inside a standard vehicle's inventory — not inside the FriOS StepVan's freezer compartment, which works correctly) was attempted to be fixed without success. It's a visual sync issue, not a real loss of refrigeration. ✅ Guarantees Food preservation is persistent. Food freshness is tracked in item data. When you return to an area, the device calculates how much time passed and applies the correct preservation factor. Multiplayer safe. When a chunk unloads, the device enters standby. When it reloads, everything resumes correctly. Save/load safe. Fully compatible with singleplayer saves. Exiting and re-entering a world does not corrupt food state. Battery drain is fair. Suspend mode reduces consumption to 10% when no player is near — not zero, not full. No fire required. Electric stoves use battery power, not fuel. Cook anywhere. 🌤️ Solar Charger — Charge by Weather The solar charger's output depends on current conditions: Operating hours: 04:00 AM — 08:00 PM. Indoors: no charging. Approximate charge times (full sun, midday): FriOS Battery (10% → 100%): ~30 in-game minutes. Car battery (any model): ~5 in-game hours. Conventional battery: ~90 seconds (effectively instant). 🗺️ Where to Find Them FriOS devices spawn naturally across the world in relevant locations: Cooler & Fridge — Electronics stores, camping stores, fridges in homes, restaurants, break rooms, military surplus. Freezer — Commercial kitchen freezers, fishing stores, butcher areas, hoarder stashes. Stoves — Kitchens of all types, camping stores, stove-adjacent locations. FriOS Battery — Fridges, freezers, electronics stores, camping gear, pawn shops. Solar Charger — Electronics stores, survival gear, military storage. Rare by design. FriOS StepVan — Good-condition parking lots, occasional traffic jams. Very rare. 🔧 Compatibility Build 41 (41.78.7) ✔ Build 42 (42.17.0) ✔ Singleplayer ✔ Multiplayer ✔ Requires: KR CoreOS No known mod conflicts 🔭 Future Content These are ideas and features planned or being explored for future updates. Nothing here is guaranteed, but this is where the mod is headed. FriOS Wind Charger — A wind turbine charger to complement the Solar Charger. Project Zomboid's engine exposes real-time wind speed (0–120 km/h) and direction. Unlike solar, it works at night and during storms — but output depends on weather conditions. A windless clear day produces nothing; a stormy night charges at full rate. FriOS Monitor — A companion item that displays battery level and estimated remaining runtime for a nearby device. Battery capacity upgrades — Find or craft components to extend battery life on your devices. Efficiency upgrades — Scavenge electronic parts to reduce a device's power consumption over time. Wine cooler / medicine fridge variants — Specialized device types with different preservation profiles. Check out my other mods! Working! How does it work? Makes the car shop lifts functional, removing the need for a car jack when the car is near the lift. There is no obvious effect besides the "car jack" item being removed from the list of "Required tools" on the "Vehicle Mechanics" window. Move the lift to your own car shop! Enabling the option to convert the vanilla tiles, you will be able to pick-up the world car lifts and place them on your own base. It requires a screwdriver and Electrical Level 3, and will result in four heavy parts. Be careful, it can break! Improve your chances with more Electrical level. (Mechanical or Metalworking requirements were not possible with how moveable tiles work.) Sandbox options - Range: The distance range from the vehicle where the car lift operates (radius from the driver door tile). - Require Power: Indicates if the car lift requires available power to operate, whether it is from hydro (world power) or a generator. - Convert to Movable Tiles: Convert vanilla tiles into moveable tiles. This process can be undone with the revert option. - Revert to Vanilla Tiles: Revert moveable car lift tiles into vanilla tiles. To succesfully revert, this option must be kept enabled until ALL tiles are reverted. Frequently Asked Questions - Can I install it to an existing save? - Yes, by default the mod just makes the existing lift tiles on the map functional. If you want to craft them, you will have less chances to find a magazine since the loot spawns at map discovery. - How do I learn the recipe? - Find and read the "Carzone Commodities: Car Lift" with Mechanics 4 and Metalworking 3, or learn the recipe automatically at Mechanics 6 and Metalworking 4. - How should I place the lift tiles? - The tiles must be placed in the form of a complete lift with the correct orientation, with both columns and center pieces. It doesn't matter how many center pieces to place, it could be 1 or 10 (for wide vehicles). - How can I pick lift? - You just pick the individual pieces as you would any furniture (if you meet the skill and tool requirements). To be able to pick vanilla car lifts (the ones that spawn at car shops), you need to enable the "Convert to Movable Tiles" Sandbox option. This will convert the vanilla tiles into the mod tiles (the same you can craft) as they are discovered. Be mindful, there is a chance to break the pieces that will decrease with better Mechanics level. - Why does my vehicle don't fit in the lift? - Some vanilla car lift on small repair shops have only 2 tiles without hitboxes, so the fit is TIGHT. Big repair shops' lifts are wider (3 tiles without hitboxes), and you can build your own custom width car lift. Some modded cars also are very tall, and collide with the top bars. description: Bandit creator Bandit Creator is an extension of the Bandits mod, allowing you to fully customize Bandits and their Clans. Want to decide how your future killer looks? Now you can! Accessible from main screen menu or in game using debug mode. Compatibile with B42 version for single and multiplayer. Customization Options Here's what you can modify: Outfit – Clothing, jewelry and accessories for each body part. Physical appearance – skin tone, hair / beard style and color, makeup. Attributes: Health, Sight (affects weapon accuracy), Endurance (determines when they need to stop to catch their breath) Strength (affects melee combat, shoves, and barricade damage) Weapons – melee, primary, and secondary weapons, plus ammo count. Bag type – the contents are auto-generated based on their expertise. Bandit special skills (expertise) Clan spawn settings: Define AI behavior, spawn location, time frame, and group size. Problems After the game starts, some assets are loading in parallel for a short while. As a result if you open the Bandit Creator, it is possible that some of the clothing may be missing. Simply reload the creator again. Sometimes the creator may load longer than expected and freeze the game for 5-15 seconds. Just be patient Be mindful about screen resolution and font size. Creator adapts to resolution to a degree, but if the resolution is very low and font size is very big, you will experience problems. Bandit Expertise Each bandit can have up to three unique skills, called expertises. Some are not yet implemented and are marked accordingly: Assassin – Only approaches if unseen; can kill with one stab; silent. (Not implemented) Breaker – Breaks barricades/doors quickly; carries extra tools. Electrician – Sabotages generators and electrical devices; carries tools. Cook – Steals or sabotages crops; carries food. Goblin – Performs mischievous (but non-lethal) actions in your base. (Not implemented) Infected – Can bite the player like a zombie, with the same consequences. Mechanic – Sabotages cars and steals fuel; carries tools and a gas can. Medic – Heals themselves or allies; carries medical gear. (Not implemented) Recon – Moves faster than others. Thief – Specializes in stealing from the player. Repairman – Carries useful tools and supplies. Tracker – Tracks the player more easily; carries maps. Trapper – Plants bear traps. (Not implemented) Traitor – May pretend to be a friend. (Not implemented) Sacrificer – Explodes on death. (Not implemented) Zombiemaster – Attracts zombies to the player. (Not implemented) Mod integrations The mod comes with several pre-built clans and bandits using vanilla items. However, it also supports external mods that add new weapons and clothing. Just enable the mods, and Bandit Creator will let you use those items. Note: If you disable those mods later, affected bandits will spawn without their gear. Your configurations will remain intact unless you re-save them. Here is a nice set of mod integrations. How creations are stored The configuration files of bandit creations (and their clans) consist of two text files (bandits.txt and clans.txt) that are saved on your local computer. There are two different storage place types for these files, and you must decide which one to use for every individual bandit profile you create. Understanding this is crucial and while this may look complicated at first, it gives the necessary flexibility. Local storage This is a single storage that exists outside of mod folders. Every bandit created in local storage will not be impacted by future mod updates. This is the best storage for players who want to: create their bandits for single player games server admins who want to decide how bandits will look like for every players on that server. Local files reside in /Zomboid/Lua/bandits folder. If you are not a modder you may stop reading here. Mod storage This storage ties every bandit creation to a specific mod and puts its configuration files in that mod. You should only tie your creations to a mod that you own. Just like I tied default bandit creations to Bandits mod. If you edit this creations your changes will get overwritten when I update the mod on Steam. So the only situation when you would chose this storage is when you are the mod author who controls the updates. For example: You created a weapon or clothing mod and you also want to create some bandits using them. This way if someone uses Bandits and your mod they will get some new fresh bandits using items from your mod. You want to create an integration mod that only defines the bandits and sets the dependency to both Bandits mod and the mod providing with the clothing / weaponry. For b42 files reside in /<modid>/common/bandits folder, for b41 in /<modid>/media/bandits folder. You will be able to save to a mod only if if these folders exist in the mod folder and bandits.txt and clans.txt empty files are created in there. Configuration files from mods and local storage are loaded simultaneously and merged in memory. Local is loaded last. The merging process allows you even to have bandits from the same clan defined in different storages. So you don't need to make clans, you can just expand what there already is. If you like my work, be sure to give it a LIKE and Credits Ravense - art Workshop ID: 3469292499 Mod ID: BanditsCreator
