description: Build Support: B42.12 to B42.19 (Build 42 only, SP / MP Host tested on recent builds) The Shortcut adds a fast shortcut bar for items, crafting recipes, and building projects. Add what you use most, then double-click to craft/build instantly (when requirements are met), or right-click to jump to the relevant menu with the entry selected — so you spend less time browsing lists and more time playing. Note: I have been making small tools to make the game more convenient to play, allowing me to focus on the content of the game itself without being bogged down by complicated and tedious tasks. Now, this tool can help you operate the new crafting system and the new building system introduced by B42 much more easily. If you were previously using my Quick Access mod mainly for its shortcut bar feature, you can now replace it with The Shortcut. It’s easier to use, more powerful, and far more stable than the old mod. I will later remake Quick Access into a specialized tool focusing only on backpack nesting, similar to Escape from Tarkov. Important: I did not set up a separate open/close button. The panel is fully controlled through a hotkey, which is set to "TAB" by default. You can also quickly switch pages using the mouse wheel on the panel. Item Page You can drag items from your inventory into slots for quick actions. The main interaction logic is: Double Click: Quickly perform actions with certain items, such as drinking, eating, smoking, or reading. More actions will be added in the future. Right Click: Open the right-click menu. Crafting Page In the crafting interface, you can press the "+" button to add recipes to the slots. The main interaction logic is: Double Click: If the recipe’s conditions are met (indicated by a green checkmark on the bottom left), you can craft it immediately by double-clicking. Right Click: Open the crafting panel and automatically select the recipe. Mouse over: View basic recipe information. Building Page In the building interface, you can press the "+" button to add building projects to the slots. The main interaction logic is: Double Click: If conditions are met (green checkmark), double-clicking will build directly. If not, it will generate a red preview. Right Click: Open the building panel and automatically select the project. Mouse over: View basic information about the project. Settings Page In the settings page, you can customize the shortcut bar to your liking. Options include: 1. Number of rows and columns (up to 16x16) 2. Slot size 3. Control widget position 4. Panel and slot transparency 5. Custom hotkey settings 6. Reset all settings Better Performance Tuning I’ve spent a long time developing and testing this mod, continuously optimizing it since the release of Quick Access. Now it runs very stably while consuming minimal resources. However, if you set up a large number of slots (like 16x16), there may inevitably be some FPS drop. I will continue to monitor and optimize performance to keep it as efficient as possible. Gamepad Compatibility Currently, it does not support gamepads. During my gameplay time, I have used a gamepad fewer than 20 times, and I don't own one. However, I hope to find a way to make it compatible in the future. About I took inspiration from several games I frequently play and merged their interaction logic into Project Zomboid, such as Enshrouded, Grounded, and Escape from Tarkov. I’m not the first one to make a shortcut bar mod for Project Zomboid, and I want to thank the following mods for providing lots of ideas. If you don’t like my UI design, feel free to subscribe to their mods for similar functionality: - BZquickslot - Better Building If you enjoy my mod and your circumstances allow, it would be amazing if you could buy me a cup of coffee, but first and foremost, enjoy your game! You can join my discord channel for more information Rocco's Mod Common Issue Fix If you find that your Shortcut are not showing up or are outside the window, follow these steps to fix it: Locate your Project Zomboid save files. By default, it should be here: C:\Users\“[your user's name]”\Zomboid\Lua Delete the ShortcutConfig.lua file. If you want to republish my mod, you need to follow these rules: 1. There must be substantial and important improvements. 2. If my mod has not been updated for a long time and has caused many issues, you may modify and republish it. Workshop ID: 3470659758 Mod ID: TheShortcut

Retained support for legacy versions: B42.13, B42.12. ***December 2025 Update*** NOW UPDATED TO B42.13 MULTIPLAYER! Backwards compatibility to B42.12 deployed! Volume 4 is now compatible with B42.12! Announcing: collaboration between the Frockin' Splendor! franchise and Tomb's Player Body! My mate Tomb just published a goth skin, makeup and hairstyle mod, which pairs perfectly with the Frockin' Splendor! franchise. Go check it out! Every piece of high quality, fishnet, nylon and lace accessories you will ever need to complete a gothic, punk or otherwise edgy and eye-catching look: bodysuits, leotards, tops & crop tops, boleros, shorts, skirts, leggings, gloves, corsets and stockings. At launch there are 113 different items, 1568 variants in total. All can be found in containers at reasonable places, and in "gift boxes". Use context menu options to adjust the appearance of the outfits. Certain items also have an alternative, ripped appearance, use context menu option to rip some holes. Naturally, you cannot un-rip them. A new tech has also allowed a structural system that defines fishnet and nylon as their own distinctive fabric types. You will be able to salvage them for scraps similar to the vanilla functions. Fishnet scraps can be recycled into threads, and nylon scraps can be disposed of to gain tailoring xp. This mod is the second part of a multi-stage project to improve and expand a certain B41 mod and bring it to B42. With all major branches being brought over to B42, this concludes most of the effort, and makes Volume 4 the final instalment in the mainline series. There will be an epilogue after this one to tie every volume and Shirts & Ties together with zombie outfits that utilises the combined varieties of the franchise, and bring over any leftover items. Currently there are at least 22 zombie outfit archetypes and 12 famous zombie outfits planned for the epilogue. Q: Is this mod save compatible? A: YES. Q: I can't find the stuff in containers! A: While the mod is save compatible, you will need to go to areas previously unexplored for the new items to start spawning in. A new tech has allowed this mod to place items in custom containers, or, "gift boxes", inside other containers such as wardrobes or crates. This way all Frockin Splendor! clothes can be found in reasonable quantities, while not crowding out the loot tables for vanilla and other modded items. These "gift boxes" have between 0.55% and 1.19% chance to spawn. Q: Why didn't you port the crafting system to B42? A: At the current stage B42 crafting is in a very unfinished state. There are placeholder codes and recipes and are clearly subject to change. It would be unwise to overhaul the old crafting recipes only to have to redo it when The Indie Stone inevitably changes things. Crafting will come later. With that being said, I have built a structural framework to define fishnet and nylon as separate fabric types, so you will be able to salvage the items for threads and xp. Q: Mod compatibility issues? A: All Frockin Splendor! mods are guaranteed to be compatible with each other. There should be no conflicts with other mods, to the best of knowledge. Please report any error you encounter in the BUG REPORT post. Q: What about character model mods? A: All but one clothing items do not have a separate mesh, meaning that they can be used with various character model mods without issue. Q: Can I use your mod in my mod pack? A: Ask for permission! Q: Can I translate your mod or port it back to B41? A: Feel free to do translation, and I'd be happy to incorporate them into the mod, but I kindly ask that back-ports are NOT to be made. Q: Will you port the new functions and items back to B41 yourself then? A: After Frockin' Splendor! Epilogue is published I will think about porting everything new back to B41. Naturally, this will make Kink It Up! Extra obsolete, so I will need to think about the logistics of things. If MP comes to B42 beforehand then there would be no need anyway. Liking the mod? Give it a rating to show your support! This mod is part of the Frockin' Splendor! Phase 1 Series. description: A compact, lightweight weapon holding 20+1 rounds. Weighing only 400 grams unloaded it's easy to put it in a pocket (or ankle holster) and forget about it until it's needed. Just be aware of the slow reloading, as you insert rounds one-by-one through the breach into the internal magazine. My goal with weapon mods is to add weapons that fill a niche not readily available; In this case a gun you can use a non-primary weapon that won't take up much of your carry capacity, has a little bit more stopping power and easier handling than an M9 but a drawback that prevents it from being an overly-good primary gun. Credits Weapon design, reference images and main texture by KelTec arms. Parts of the texture are from Keltech PR57 by Brahian SG FAQ Does this mod work in B41? No, B42 only. Is this mod compatible with Rain's firearms? Yes, the PR-57 supports attachments from Rain's Firearms but does not require Rain's Firearms to work. Is this mod compatible with <other firearm mod>? The weapon is built using only vanilla features so probably. Can this mod be added to/removed from existing games? Yes, but when adding the gun will only show up as loot in new map areas. Are you going to add support for stripper clips? No, because that would require too much reworking of the reloading code because the base game doesn't support multiple reload options. I may revisit this once B42 firearms are more stable. Why does this gun use 5.56mm rounds instead of 5.7mm? Because I didn't want to add a whole new ammo type just for one gun. Both rounds use the same diameter bullet and look similar. Sure, a 5.56mm round has approximately four times more kinetic energy... but if "battery" can simultaneously be a AAA and a heavy duty lantern battery then a 5.56x45mm round works as a 5.7x28. (This mod also adjusts the weight of a 5.56mm round from 25 grams to a more accurate 10grams, otherwise the weight of the ammunition ends up higher than the weight of the gun!) Does it fit in an ankle holster? Yes; it can placed in normal holsters, shoulder holsters, ankle holsters and any modded attachment points that support HolsterSmall items. Is this weapon appropriate for 1993? The distinctive reloading system was developed in the 1920s, the PR-57 was developed in the 2020s, so on average this weapon is appropriate for any game set after 1970s. description: Compatible with Build 42.10 to Build 42.19 — SP / MP Project Cook adds a dedicated cooking panel for Project Zomboid’s evolved-recipe cooking system. It helps you choose valid base items, browse compatible ingredients and seasonings, check cooking/nutrition information, and add ingredients through a cleaner and more intuitive UI. Required Mod & Load Order Project Cook requires [B42] NeatUI Framework. Recommended load order: [B42] NeatUI Framework Project Cook Project Cook Pixel Icon Pack — optional addon The Pixel Icon Pack only replaces some Project Cook panel icons with pixel-art versions. If enabled, it must be placed after Project Cook. Special thanks to ivmakk for providing lots of inspiration and ideas for this mod. What Project Cook Does Project Cook is designed mainly for evolved-recipe style cooking: meals where you start from a base item and add compatible ingredients or seasonings. Examples include soups, stews, salads, stir-fries, burgers, sandwiches, pasta-like meals, and other ingredient-based recipes. Some vanilla cooking actions still belong to the normal Crafting system first. In those cases, you may need to create the initial food/container through vanilla Crafting or through Neat Crafting before continuing inside Project Cook. Open the Panel You can open Project Cook in several ways: Hover over the vanilla Crafting button on the left-hand sidebar to show the Project Cook button. Right-click a valid food item or recipe base item and choose the Project Cook option. If the selected item can be used as a base item, it will be selected automatically. Base Item Panel Choose a valid base item, such as a cooking pot, bowl, burger, sandwich, or another item/container that can accept ingredients. Fill: fills supported water-based containers from a nearby valid water source. Empty: empties supported recipe containers and recovers the empty container. Add: queues selected ingredients or seasonings to be added. Rename: lets you rename the finished food. Rating: shows recipe rating information when available. Cooking Info Panel The Cooking Info panel gives useful guidance about the current recipe. Nutrition information depends on your traits and Cooking skill: Nutritionist: full nutrition details. Cooking Level 2: nutrition categories, exact values hidden. Cooking Level 4: values rounded to hundreds. Cooking Level 6: values rounded to tens. Cooking Level 8: full exact nutrition values. Ingredients & Seasonings Panel Once a base item is selected, you can browse compatible ingredients and seasonings. Compatible ingredients are shown based on the selected base item. Seasonings are handled separately from regular ingredients. Each base item has its own ingredient limit. Each seasoning type can only be added once. Right-click items to choose between multiple instances of the same item. Double-click an ingredient or seasoning to add it directly. Use the + button to select several items first, then add them together. Frozen ingredients must thaw before they can be used in recipes that do not allow frozen items. Recent versions also include stricter filtering to avoid non-cooking “technical food” items being handled as normal cooking ingredients only because they are internally defined as Food by the game. Pixel Icon Pack Project Cook Pixel Icon Pack is an optional sub-mod that replaces some cooking panel icons with pixel-art versions created by ivmakk. If you switch icon styles, restart the game so the icons refresh correctly. Compatibility Notes Project Cook is intended to work in both SP and MP for supported Build 42 versions. For best results: Keep [B42] NeatUI Framework above Project Cook. Keep optional Project Cook addons below Project Cook. Restart the game after changing icon packs or UI-related mods. If a server uses Project Cook, make sure both server and clients use the same updated Workshop version. Feedback & Bug Reports Bug reports are very helpful, especially with clear steps and logs. Please use the Bug Report thread and include: Project Zomboid version. SP, MP Host, or Dedicated Server. Relevant mod list and load order. Item, recipe, base item, ingredient, or seasoning used. What you expected to happen. What actually happened. Screenshot or short video if possible. Relevant error log or stack trace, if one appears. Clean Redownload / Update Troubleshooting If Steam does not update the mod correctly: Close Project Zomboid completely. Unsubscribe from Project Cook. Wait until Steam finishes uninstalling it. Subscribe again. Let Steam finish downloading before starting Project Zomboid. After major Build 42 updates, verifying game files can also help: Close Project Zomboid. Open your Steam Library. Right-click Project Zomboid. Go to Properties > Installed Files. Click Verify integrity of game files. More Mods & Support If you enjoy this mod and your circumstances allow, buying me a coffee would be greatly appreciated — but most importantly, enjoy your game! Discord server: Rocco's Mod Credits Original mod by Rocco: PZ Workshop Items Maintenance / compatibility updates for newer B42 builds by Afyrmo: PZ Workshop Items Pixel icon inspiration and assets by ivmakk. There must be substantial and important improvements. 2. If this mod has not been updated for a long time and has caused many issues, you may modify and republish it. description: This mod adds a variety of weapons that don't align with the era's setting. If you value realism, please consider carefully before subscribing to this mod. Current total number of weapons : 79 Mod Overview This mod is inspired by my childhood obsession: the mobile shooter Crisis Action, first released in 2014 and still active today, now approaching its 10th anniversary. B42 weapons were notably underpowered in the original version, so their damage has been significantly buffed. B41 weapons largely retain the original stats. Note: The B41 version of this mod contains multiple unresolved issues. Since this version is nearing deprecation, I'm not planning further fixes — even though B42's stable multiplayer release may still take a while. For the best experience, it's recommended to pair with the Ammo Maker mod. (Only B42) Gameplay Mechanics - Firearms You can acquire modded firearms from diverse locations — police stations, gun shops, survivors, and even school lockers. Once obtained, firearms can be upgraded using Upgrade Points. Each weapon has its own upgrade cap and unique attribute bonuses. Some firearms, when dismantled, yield Weapon Fragments, which can be used to enhance matching weapons or be broken down into Upgrade Points. - Melee Weapons Melee weapons can be found in tool shops, warehouses, garages, and similar locations. Unlike firearms, most melee weapons cannot be upgraded — they are already at max level upon acquisition. Their stats closely mimic the original game's values. - Weapon Enhancement Upgrade Points are required to strengthen weapons. You can acquire them by dismantling firearms, melee weapons, weapon parts, or fragments. Additionally, some weapons (firearm or melee) require specific Weapon Fragments to be eligible for upgrading. - Weapon Fragments These can also be acquired randomly from loot boxes or zombie drops. Weapon Fragments can themselves be dismantled into Upgrade Points if needed. - Weapon Parts Attachable to firearms, these parts grant specific attribute enhancements — such as increased fire rate or slight weight reduction. - Weapon Codex The Weapon Codex is the most important item in this mod. It can be obtained from gun shop magazine racks, bookshelves — or occasionally from general bookstores. Only after acquiring this codex does gameplay officially begin. The left panel of the codex displays weapon series; collecting all weapons in a series yields rewards. When you open a weapon's detailed view (with the 3D model), weapons marked with a check are collectible targets. description: Find the Perfect Fit! Adds clothing sizes to Project Zomboid for a deeper and more realistic looting experience. High tailoring skill lets you adjust clothes to your own body size. 1. Size System Clothing now comes in 6 sizes: XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL. Each size corresponds to a weight class: Emaciated, Very Underweight, Underweight, Normal, Overweight, Obese. Not all clothing have size, but if you find an item that should have size but doesn't, comment below and I'll consider it. Your current size appears on the Character screen, next to your weight. Size distribution: Penalties for ill-fitting clothing: Tight clothes take longer to wear and might be impossible to equip. Tight clothes cause muscle soreness and slow post-exercise recovery. Tight clothes have a higher chance of tearing when climbing fences or windows. Tight pants and skirts cause stiffness in legs while running and sprinting Loose clothes reduce insulation and combat speed. Loose clothes increases the chance that you can trip after climbing fences Loose pants/skirts may fall off if not secured with a belt. 2. Check Size You can inspect clothes to see their size. With low tailoring skill, you get a rough estimate: tight, loose, or perfect fit. With high tailoring skill, you see the exact size. Successful checks reward a small amount of tailoring XP. 3. Resize Clothes With enough tailoring skill, you can resize clothes up or down by 1 size. Requires proper tools and materials, and only some clothes can be resized. Resize result: Failure: clothing may lose condition. Success: clothing may gain a bit of condition. Success always grants tailoring XP. 4. Condition Decreases Over Time Clothing will slowly lose condition over time. Wet, dirty and bloody clothes will degrade faster. Clothes with high wind resistance and water resistance can last longer. Higher maintenance and tailoring help reduce the degrading rate. You can increase condition by reconditioning them, similar to repairing weapons. Some clothes can be reconditioned using just strips, for others, you will need a spare one. Reconditioning mechanics: Success chance and durability restored increase with Tailoring and Maintenance levels. Failure can reduce condition. Each recondition attempt lowers future success rate and amount restored. 5. Clothes crafting (B42 only) B42 introduces some clothing items which can be crafted. You can choose sizes of the output items in the crafting window beforehand (by clicking on the size tag). Notes This mod is based on Size Labels, with more added features. Most features can be customized via sandbox settings. Compatible with multiplayer and existing saves. Should be compatible with all clothing mods. Just remember, not all clothes have size. Smart Radial Menu A smart radial menu for quick access to common item actions. Supports controllers and the Steam Deck. Also supports split-screen, displaying a radial menu for each player. B42 only. For the B42.12 version, please use this instead: Smart Radial Menu [B42.12] Features Dynamic Radial Menu: Scans inventory and proximities, displaying the following relevant options: eating, drinking, smoking, using meds, reading, setting alarms, researching and crafting. Controller Support: Designed for mouse + keyboard, gamepad, and Steam Deck navigation. Item Filtering: Excludes spoiled, hazardous, and poisonous items (if known to the player), as well as literature already read and skill books you cannot read yet. Tainted water and food is optional. Learning Craft Recipes: Displays recipes that can be researched from items. Evolved Recipes Support: Craft advanced cooking recipes directly from the menu. Clothing Actions: Adds actions to wear, unequip, and inspect clothes, as well as the item's extra actions if available. Crafting: Adds B42 recipes you can craft from your inventory and nearby containers. Submenus for ingredients, maps and equipped clothes: Added submenus to separate spices from other food, maps from other literature, and the currently equipped clothes from the rest. Integration: Safe to add and remove from existing saves. Localized: Translated for multiple languages using AI, except some vanilla text not officially translated yet. Menu Navigation *Keybind is customizable Minimum Recommended Settings Item stacking and use It will group stacks of items and will use drainables, food and liquid containers from least to most uses, nutrition and liquid amount, respectively. For example, it will use the painkillers with the fewest uses remaining until depleted, then move on to the next available painkillers. For evolved recipes, the opposite is done: the item with the most nutrition or liquid amount is used first. While not perfect, it helps remind you to use available ingredients. Fluid containers on the floor will have the option to drink them directly as in vanilla, or to grab them from the floor. As in vanilla, you cannot directly drink from large capacity containers in the inventory, such as buckets. Skill Books, skill magazines, schematics and recipes will be given priority over other literature even if Unwanted. For clothing, it will try to sort items from head to toe, prioritizing those in the best condition, and more uses left for items like gas masks/SCBAs. Bags that have been renamed will be given priority, making them easier to find. Items in the player's inventory will appear first, arranged clockwise from the top of the radial. Unwanted items appear last, behind frozen, except for equipped clothes, which are sorted head to toe. If hiding Unwanted items, researchable and equipped items are always shown. Crafting items are sorted with inventory first, then alphabetically. The worst condition item and then uses remaining is selected (and more to less uses for filters/tanks/batteries), with batch crafting supported if allowed by the base game. Update 1.8.9 Updated to 42.18 Improved performance in general, specially for large inventories. Re-sorted some body locations. Sorted gas masks/SCBAs by filter/tank more uses left. Sorted filters/tanks/batteries by more uses left. Cigarettes can be packed from the menu if applicable. Added fluid submenu to containers. Added cooking items for evolved recipes. Fixed sorting for the reading slice. Fixed the submenu for large fluid containers. Fixed tooltip sticking to mouse pointer after closing the menu. Fixed opening the menu while on pause. Fix for controllers: Select slices with any of the DPad buttons again. Update 1.8.71 Controller support is currently broken for radial menus, so I had to do some workarounds to fix it until an official patch is released. [strike] Fix for controllers: Closing/Selecting has to be done now with DPad-Up only, and fixed the hold to open menu option. [/strike] Fix for controllers: Fixed immediately aiming when selecting a slice and interrupting the action, which was broken again. Mod compatibility TidyUp Meister Picking Meister Drink Smart Better Sorting 42.13+ compatibility patch Organized Categories 42.13+ compatibility patch Extended categories (B42) No additional compatibilities are currently planned. Known bugs This is my biggest mod project to date, so bugs may be expected. Extra mouse buttons on gaming mice can't be used to hold the menu open due to how the game code works, but work in toggle mode. When items are marked as favorite, you might not be able to use recipes on them. This is a vanilla limitation. 'Insert battery' has an option that can insert multiple batteries into a flashlight and waste extras. This is a vanilla bug, just avoid it. As of B42.17 controller support is currently broken in vanilla, this is unrelated to the mod. Please use the 'Bug Reports' discussion to paste error logs. This mod is not and will never be a replacement for the right-click menu. If you can and would like to support me by buying me a coffee, I'd greatly appreciate it - but most of all, I hope you enjoy the mod! Workshop ID: 3494108029 Mod ID: SmartRadialMenu

description: Compatible with Build 42 up to Build 42.19+ Show Key Origin helps you identify where a key belongs by showing the distance and direction to its origin directly in the inventory tooltip. It can also display a visual origin line in the world, pointing from your character toward the related building or the original spawn position of the linked vehicle. This makes keys much easier to identify, sort, and keep organized. Main Features Shows the distance to a key’s origin. Shows the direction toward that origin. Adds a context-menu option to toggle a visual origin line. For house keys, the line points toward the related building. For vehicle keys, it points toward the vehicle’s original spawn position. Optional compass requirement through Sandbox settings. How It Works Hover over a key in your inventory to see its origin information. Right-click a key and use the context menu to show or hide the origin line. Use the information to identify duplicate keys, sort useful keys, or figure out which building or vehicle a key belongs to. Optional Sandbox Setting You can enable a Sandbox option that requires having a compass in your inventory. When enabled: Tooltip origin information only appears if you have a compass. The visual origin line is only available if you have a compass. Optional TchernoLib Support If you enable TchernoLib, the origin line can be displayed thicker for better visibility. TchernoLib is optional. Show Key Origin works without it. Compatibility Works from Build 42 up to Build 42.19+. Safe to enable or disable in both new games and existing saves. Compatible with most mod setups. Possible conflicts are mainly expected with mods that heavily modify inventory tooltips or key/item context-menu behavior. Localization Recent versions include expanded translation support for multiple languages, including legacy TXT translations for older Build 42 versions and JSON translations for Build 42.15+. More Mods & Feedback You can find my other Project Zomboid mods here If you find Show Key Origin useful, please consider leaving a thumbs up and adding it to your favorites. Feedback, suggestions, and bug reports are always welcome. description: You're immune to the Knox virus, so why do you wake up with global topographical amnesia? This mod lets you start with map knowledge of your immediate surroundings, as well as knowledge of the roads in a much larger area. Both the immediate radius and the distance of know roads from your starting point can be configured in sandbox options. FAQ What do the sandbox options do? Start Knowing Roads gives all new characters knowledge of the roads around their starting location. Add to Existing Characters gives existing characters road knowledge, around their location when they first log in after this mod is activated. Home radius creates a circle around a new character's start location where they know 100% of the map. Set to 0 to disable. Road radius is the distance from the starting location where roads are revealed. Debug prints a bit of extra information. Does this mod work in B41? No, B42 only. Does this work with modded maps? Yes, provided they have set up forage zones correctly; specifically having 'Nav' zones on roads. A few places on the map reveal areas without roads! That's because the game's forage data doesn't match the roads; this is mainly noticeable on a few highway sections that were converted from right angle corners to nice long curves/angled sections in B42. Can you avoid revealing buildings next to the roads? Map knowledge is tracked in 32x32 units, so there will always be some overlap on the edges of the roads. description: Overview : Say goodbye to becoming a jack-of-all-trades! This mod introduces a new skill development system that encourages balance and decision-making by setting a cap on total skill levels. Designed with multiplayer and RP servers in mind, this mod promotes role specialization and interdependence. Confirmed to work with Build 41/42. Split-screen play is not supported. May be considered upon request. Features : Skill Cap System You can level up freely until your total skill level reaches the cap. Once the cap is reached, skill leveling behavior depends on the cap setting. If there are skills marked as reducible, one will be randomly chosen to decrease, allowing the new skill to level up. If there are no reducible skills, skill level-up will be suppressed. Skill Cap Buttons Cap control buttons are added to the skill panel in the character info window. Each button has three toggle states that can be switched by clicking: : Gain XP and level up freely until the total cap is reached. : XP gain and leveling are disabled; skill may be reduced if over the cap. : XP gain and leveling are disabled; skill is protected from reduction. Skills without a cap button are excluded from the system. You can customize which skills are excluded via Sandbox settings. Sandbox Options : These options are available in Sandbox Options. Seesaw Game > Total Skill Cap : Sets the total level cap across all skills. Once the combined level exceeds this value, no further skill gains are allowed. Seesaw Game > Excluded Skill Cap : Sets a semicolon-separated list of skills to exclude from the total skill cap. These skills will not be affected by the cap and can continue to level up freely. Options : These options are available with Mod Options in B41. Level Down XP Rate : Sets how much XP is reduced when a skill is leveled down due to reaching the total skill cap. Show Skill Cap Info : Displays total skill cap information in the Skill Panel. Known Issues : Setting a high EXP multiplier may cause the total skill count to become inaccurate when multiple levels are gained from a single exp acquisition. This is currently a limitation, but I plan to consider addressing it if there is significant demand in the future. If leveling up is disabled due to exceeding the cap limit, any recipes acquired through that level-up will remain learned. Future plans : Bug fix (if it exists) Release Notes : v0.4 - Hotfix for Build 42.15. v0.3 - Hotfix for Build 42.13. v0.2 - Fixed cap button problem. v0.1 - New release as beta version. Please refer to "Change Notes" for the older history. If you enjoy this mod and would like to support its development, you can do so through the services below. Your support helps cover the cost of renting a dedicated server for multiplayer testing, as well as AI service subscriptions used for development - expenses I personally pay for every month, totaling over $50. description: Being the 'Common Sense' of vehicles, this mod adds A LOT of Features and QOL/Rebalancing Changes, I urge you to read the full list below! Trust me, you'll be wishing some of these options were in the vanilla game. [WIP Mod for Multiplayer/Singleplayer B42.19 and UP]. Supports all modded vehicles! Almost everything can be selectively disabled/enabled (the important stuff at least), most options are enabled by default. Climbable Vehicles does not currently work for multiplayer, requires enabling in the sandbox settings, and will be moved to a different mod eventually anyways. I only recommend using it for screenshots as it's very outdated, for now. NEW FEATURES: - Adds vehicle zones across the entire map (literally thousands) including vehicles in garages, gas station, more traffic in your traffic jams, farms, and more. - Adds a new custom vehicle spawn rate, chance to spawn burnt, damaged, and more customization in the sandbox settings. - Spawns more corpses in cars, you'll find quite a few here and there car seats. - Some vehicle zone types, like parking lots, can spawn vehicles facing in random directions to simulate the initial waves of chaos of the apocalypse. - Improves junkyards and traffic jams by adding back wrecked vehicles, removal of random parts, rebalanced vehicle qualities, and randomly opened doors/windows. - Bombs can now trigger car alarms AND be planted on vehicles to explode them (smoke, pipe, aerosol, remote detonators, plant on doors, above wheels, and in the ignition, etc.). - A new system for refueling vehicles from pumps at gas stations, which includes, but is not limited to, not needing to stand still for a minute while pumping gasoline, repairing the pump you just ripped out after driving away with it still attached, sounds, fuel station status, etc. - Adds the ability to exit from a moving vehicle, but I'd be careful at higher speeds! - Weather affects players with an open door, a window open, or a windshield smashed (more detailed than worth explaining). - Adds vehicles hoods, trunks, and trailers as a generic crafting surfaces; for crafting recipes that require a table. - Adds a crafting recipe to clone a car key, either as a backup or for a friend. It is very similar to the 'Copy Building Key' recipe and it requires reading the same magazine from it. - Adds the ability to open/close and unlock/lock your own door while in a vehicle. - Adds the ability to enter/exit some vehicles through the trunk (assume for most heavy-duty vehicles it will work). Only works if you can see the "Trunk" container icon from the seat you're in (usually the rear row). That feature, that is accessing the trunk from the inside if you're in a specific seat, is vanilla and I made this to work based on that. - As the driver of a vehicle, you can electronically open/close any window. Press "Z", or enter the Vehicle Seats UI another way, then hold LEFT or RIGHT ALT to see your options. From there, you can either click an individual window or press a number on your keyboard to open the corresponding window. - You can now unhotwire (rewire?) hotwired vehicles at level 3 electrical and level 2 mechanics. - Automatically opens the car door and opens your proximity inventory when faced with too many items in a vehicle seat you tried to sit in from the outside (helps with taking corpses out). BUT, if there is at least one other seat that isn't the driver seat that is empty enough to fit those items on it (fully empty for a corpse), then it will transfer those items automatically for you to sit in. - Adds a TWD reference, a flipped prison bus in Rosewood (if you have the correct KI5 vehicle mod enabled), there's more potential here (WIP). - Advert trailers now have trailer storage. SANDBOX SETTINGS: - General spawn rate defaults to vanilla if no value is entered. Junkyards, traffic jams, and special traffic jams ignore this setting. - Spawn rate for traffic jams (otherwise recognized as bumper to bumper traffic) is defaulted to very high, but the vanilla Vehicle Spawn Rate value slightly alters it. - The Traffic Jams in LV toggle enables/disables all the new traffic jams I added in LV specifically. - The Traffic Jams outside LV toggle enables/disables all the new traffic jams I added everywhere else. - Random Vehicle Angles is a toggle for if some specific types of car zones, such as parking lots and ambulances, will be rotated around at random. Basically, it is a slight immersion thing. - Corpses Spawning in Vehicles can be set to "None", "Rare", "Normal", and "Common" (default is 'Normal' which is about 8%). - Bombs interacting with vehicles can be toggled off/on. - The new system for refueling vehicles from pumps at gas stations can be toggled off/on. - Weather affects players in vehicles can be toggled off/on. - Jumping out of a fast moving vehicle can toggled off/on and the damage received can be reduced/increased. - The ability to turn all vehicle zones into burnt wrecks, completely configurable at a set rate. - The ability to completely customize the quality of cars you find for all vehicle zones. - The ability to prevent 'Good' vehicles from spawning ('Good' vehicles are a VANILLA thing). - The 'Climbable Vehicles' addon (read near the top of the description for a warning). LOAD ORDER INSTRUCTION!!!: In general, treat this mod like a map mod for load order (at the top), but still place after normal map mods. Required mod for MILITARY VEHICLE ZONES: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3436499337 If you use or want a mod that removes/replaces vanilla vehicles, it must be one of these two: Kraz's No Vanilla Vehicles (B42): https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2535461640 OR Vanilla Vehicles Replacer (KI5): https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3423424077 Shoutout to KI5's (year accurate / lore friendly) vehicle mods which are primarily supported in this mod for balancing and special treatment (I still take suggestions for other vehicles like the W900 trucks mod): https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=2490220997 If you want corpses to spawn in KI5 vehicles specifically, install this mod and follow THEIR load order instruction. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3457132019 Use in combination with other vehicle mods if you wish, I have not discovered any conflicts (yet), these have a few additional features that I don't (yet): https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3281755175 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3677886085 EXTRA SPECIAL SHOUTOUT TO (Alex) @RedChili FOR HELPING ME WITH CLIMBING ANIMATIONS https://steamcommunity.com/id/mreastman/myworkshopfiles/?appid=108600 Workshop ID: 3520758551 Mod ID: WayMoreCars

description: This is a complete rewrite using the original Home Inventory as reference. 引用自 maraganina： Looted the 14th pipe wrench because you forgot you already had 13? Didn't take that sledgehammer because you already had one but now you realized that was on your previous character? This mod allows you to designate zones in your home(s) or base(s). A list of all items in those zones will be displayed in the new Home Inventory [strike]tab[/strike], available [strike]in the Character Info panel (Health screen)[/strike] by clicking a new button in the sidebar. Safe to add/remove mid campaign; doesn't overwrite any game files. ... The Home Inventory mod allows the player to create and manage custom zones: "home" zones; similar to how the Animal system works in B42. The items inside home zones are fetched and saved, and can be seen as a list in a new [strike]tab[/strike] panel called "Home Inventory" located in the [strike]Character Info panel (the heart icon)[/strike]. Home zones can cover multiple bases, and can also cover different areas of each base. It's up to you to decide how you will organize your bases and the items inside them. The list of items is only fetched when you add or remove zones, or when you click the [strike]"Home Inventory" tab[/strike] "Manage" button, so the mod has virtually no effect on performance. If you are too far from a zone, their tiles will not be loaded, and the game will think your items don't exist. To prevent this, the mod saves the items of each zone to a cache, so you can keep checking your home inventory while you are away. What's new? This mod adds many extra features in addition to the currently existing ones in the original mod, which includes: Vehicles Storage: Any items in a vehicle or trailer inside a zone should now be accounted for. (since 0.7.0) (thanks for the idea, @Sophia (Sophel) and @Crystalmancer!) After a long drive, you can open the items list and hit refresh to show your newly acquired loots. The name of vehicle is displayed alongside its specific part for easier search. Improved UI (again, hopefully) (since 0.6.0) The Zone panel can now be resized, and it's also made more compact. Quick Search: Right-click on an item will show whether you have collected that item and the current amount stored in your Home Inventory. (since 0.4.0) NOTE: The amount of items collected for the default option is now placed in the tooltip of an item, visible when hovered. (since 0.5.0) Container Tooltip: Hover over the container name of an item to show its inventory icon. (since 0.3.0) Integration with Smarter Storage (since 0.3.0) (Thanks for the idea, @ivmakk!) The "Container" column will now display the custom name set by the mod if it exists. The custom icon and background will be used in the container tooltip when hovered. Improved UI (since 0.2.0) The items panel can now be opened with a new button next to the "Designated Zones" button. (A new custom icon is also used.) A refresh button to reload items without needing to re-open/close any panels. Items sorting with ascending and descending order by clicking on the header text. Selectable filter criteria with a drop-down list next to the search bar. Resizable panel to expand all truncated texts to your heart's content. Mod options: some previously hard-coded values (such as zone colors) can be adjusted and all changes made can be applied mid-game. (since 0.2.0) A key can be set to open/close the items panel (KP_ADD or "Numpad +" by default) A number of bugs in the original mod is also fixed (hopefully): Incorrect size reported by the zone manager panel. (A 1-cell zone will show up as 4) (might be the same as the previous one) Zones bleeding into each other. (Two non-overlapping zones that are right next to each other will cause an item in one zone to show up in the other as a duplicate entry) Interference to the display designated zones for animals. This mod does not hide or show them. Incompatibilities This mod only conflicts with the original one, but that's mostly because having 2 different items system is kind of redundant in my opinion. It is planned that a special function to import mod data from the original mod for migration. Final notes A special thanks and all respects to the original mod's creator maraganina, I've been using your mod for a few months now, and it has been a convenience in every run of mine ever since, and of course, this mod would have never existed without your contribution to the Steam Workshop. For everybody else, if you like this mod, be sure to check out the original one, too! GLHF and keep on surviving! :3 Workshop ID: 3522009163 Mod ID: cf_home

Supports Version 42 SP+MP and Version 41 SP+MP This mod allows you to place tent walls, floors, and ceilings at your character's current location using vanilla tent items. You can configure tent walls to be invincible or assign them custom HP so that zombies can destroy them. All tiles are dynamically generated and deleted. The mod does not include any map, so you can place and retrieve tents anywhere. These are the default sandbox settings. You can adjust them however you like. For now, let's test the default configuration. In Build 41: camping.CampingTentKit is used. In Build 42: Four colored tents (Base.TentBlue, Base.TentYellow, Base.TentBrown, Base.TentGreen), Base.CampingTentKit2, and Base.ImprovisedTentKit are supported. The tent must be unfolded, and a "Put up Tent" option will appear on right-click. When you click "Put up Tent", a tent of the configured size will appear starting at the character's position. The tent item is consumed, and a Tent Key is created. The Tent Key is used to manage your tent: Take down Tent / Enter or Exit Tent / (Build 42) Refresh Ceiling Rendering. Also, when right-clicking the key, it will highlight the tent associated with that key while the context menu is open. Tents don't have doors by default, and if the walls are invincible, doors would be meaningless. So entering/exiting is done via the key. You can exit only from inside the tent. You can enter only if you are right up against the tent wall from the outside. Clicking "Take down Tent" will cleanly remove the tent, as shown above. From the outside, when you stand close to a tent wall, the "Enter Tent" option will appear. Now let's change the sandbox settings and try making a bigger tent with a rain collector. A 10x10 tent is created as configured. Going upstairs, you can see the rain collector was generated properly and is functional. In Zomboid, if walls and ceilings are in the exact same tile, the upper floor can be seen through certain angles, as shown. To fix this, you can enable the "Install Ceiling One Tile Lower" option in the sandbox settings. This prevents the upper floor from showing through. Mattresses that are only 1 tile in height will generate a single tile, like above. You can also specify custom tent items in the sandbox settings. List the item IDs including their modules, separated by semicolons (;). I added items from the All-in-One Backpacking Shelter mod: Hx.AIOBShelter;Hx.AIOBShelterPillow;Hx.AIOBShelterMattress;Hx.AIOBShelterAll The "Put up Tent" option appears correctly. Tent placement and key generation work fine. Take down Tent works as expected. This feature is for Build 41 multiplayer: You can duplicate tent keys. With a Tent Key + Unusable Metal + Saw, you can craft a duplicate key. If you have multiple keys, right-click on the exact one you want to copy for accurate duplication. One duplicate key made copying another tent key Both keys created successfully. Duplicate keys can only be used to enter/exit the linked tent. When close to a tent wall, right-click to see "Enter Tent" From inside the tent, "Exit Tent" will appear. If you right-click with a key for a different tent, no context menu will appear. If you enable "Remove Tent Enter Distance Limit" in the sandbox options, you'll be able to enter the tent from a distance, allowing the mod to function similarly to an RV interior. When you click "Exit Tent", your character will return to the location they were in before entering. Inside the tent, right-clicking the tent key will let you control any generator within 20 tiles on the same floor around your character. You can remotely check generator info, turn it on/off, refuel it, and repair it. However, you must manually obtain and connect the generator yourself, and your character must know how to operate it in order to turn it on or off. Workshop ID: 3524273533 Mod ID: RealTent

description: Restore your vehicle's engine quality with a Wrench, Spare Engine Parts, and Mechanical skill 4+ Unlike vanilla engine condition (which affects durability), engine quality determines starting reliability, fuel efficiency, and cold weather performance. This mod lets you restore quality from any percentage up to 100%. Why Use This Mod? Have you ever found a great military vehicle, but its engine quality is completely ruined? Have you already repaired and fully upgraded a car for long trips, but starting the engine still requires minutes of attempts? Then this mod is for you - restore the engine to its day-one state, just like it was set from the factory. Key Features Engine Quality Restoration: Improve quality from any percentage up to 100% Skill-Based Mechanics: Higher Mechanics skill = better quality increases per iteration (just like vanilla engine repairing works) Configurable Resource Cost: Adjust engine parts consumption multiplier in Menu -> Options -> Mods -> Restore Engine Quality (1-5 per restoration, default: 2) How to Use Requirements: Wrench (or Ratchet Wrench), Spare Engine Parts, appropriate Mechanics skill level (4+) Access: Right-click vehicle Engine → Restore Engine Quality (the same context menu where "Repair Engine" located) Process: Each restoration consumes engine parts and improves quality based on your skill Resource Cost By default, requires 2x more Spare Engine Parts than regular engine repair (making it more challenging but not grindy). description: Adds a new skill in the survival category called toughness. This is your character's mental resilience to the hardships of the apocalypse, with each level reducing the amount of panic, pain and discomfort they'll feel. Toughness XP can be earned by killing zombies. It will take about 4450 total zombie kills to reach max level in toughness at x1 XP rates. The new positive trait "tough" provides a starting toughness level of +1 and a x4 XP multiplier, reducing the total number of zombie kills for max level to only around 1000. Each level of toughness reduces the total amount of panic felt by your character by -10%, pain by -5%, discomfort by -5% and an extra 10% added to the discomfort nullification threshold. This means a character with level 2 toughness will not gain any discomfort at all if the total combined discomfort of their clothes and moodles is at or below 20%. Since the total discomfort pecentage level can go above 100%, level 10 toughness won't completely remove discomfort if enough uncomfortable clothes are being worn. If these values are not to your liking the XP rate and stat reduction from toughness can be configured in the sandbox. This mod can be seen as an alternative to the "become desensitized" mod, providing a more gradual increase in panic reduction as the playthrough progresses rather than suddenly granting the desensitized trait after a set number of zombie kills. description: This mod adds M998 HMMWV (Humvee) with Animated Doors and a fully functioning Turret to Project Zomboid. It is necessary to have the Military Tool Kitinstalled. *Only for B42 SP and MP *Compatible with old saves *Compatible with KI5 vehicles Resources Animated Doors Animated Addons Turret The turrets have heavy coding that adds a completely new ballistics system that is independent of the systems in the Standard Game, performing calculations for each projectile independently, calculating its energy, ability to cause damage and transfix bodies, vehicles and walls. Doors, hoods, trunk lids and more. They have their own colors, so you can assemble your Humvee with the color variation of the parts you want. How to use the Machine Gun The machine gun must be installed in the vehicle You must sit in the Gunner's seat You must place the 12.7x99mm (.50 BMG) Ammo Box already loaded with 12.7x99mm (.50 BMG) Round in the gun compartment. Press the Right Mouse Button to aim and the Left Mouse Button to fire. ATTENTION, the projectile will be fired where the barrel of the machine gun is pointing and not necessarily where you are aiming, so for more precise shots it is recommended that you wait for the turret stop before firing. (It is still possible to fire with it moving) ATTENTION, when the projectile is fired, it will travel all the way until it completely loses its synergy and stops, so if there are vehicles in its path and the projectile has enough synergy, it will cause damage and may or may not transfix them. The same logic applies to walls, just as in real life a .50 BMG projectile can transfix some walls and still have the energy to destroy things in its path. So use with caution, a Browning M2HB is not a toy. It is necessary to have the Military Tool Kit installed. description: OOPSIES! Hey guys, I did a quick and dirty update for the last version a bit ago, but it sounds like no dice! You can add it to existing worlds, but it'll probably only spawn in new areas, or if you have loot respawn enabled. I kept the spawn rates the same, so it shouldn't flood the world with guns. If the console has a repeated error, it's probably an issue with an item not being replaced on a zombie. If that happens, try reloading the save. If you have debug on, you can also reload the lua. If you see an item labeled "fr_loadout_", do NOT equip it. I added a fail safe in case players do, but haven't been able to confidently test it yet. If you want to test it, please back up your save first! Thanks! It should be compatible with any gun mod that's compatible with vanilla. Please report any other bugs to the discord! https://discord.gg/WKjTuqW Features 13 FULLY customizable guns! 90ish different spawn variants! Removable, replaceable parts! Make the gun YOU want! Got lucky and found you a civilian AR15 with a 16 inch barrel? Nice! Feelin' like running through the jungle instead? Just pull off the forend, toss that 16 inch barrel in the trash, and burn that collapsing stock, cause you can slap on a full stock, 20 inch barrel and triangular forend! Wanna turn that snub nosed .44 into a discount hunting rifle? Grab a wrench and bash off that barrel, toss on a 10 incher, weaver attachment, scope and a pistol stock and GO WILD! Need to sneak around and assassinate someone in your borderline socially unacceptable "world war 2" roleplay server, but only got you a big ol' bolt action with a 26 inch barrel? Saw it down to 12 inches, cut off that stock and, I dunno, hide it in your pants leg. It's still pretty big. Replace any of the following! Muzzles Grips Stocks Forends Barrels Slides Trigger groups Internal magazines Scopes Big ol' bulky laser sights Planned features! Here's some stuff I'd like to add for the full version! Different mag types! Guns using different ammo types! Part conditions! Gotta maintain that barrel or you might have to swap it out! Home made parts! Just in case you break the stock on your Winchester Model 70 and can't find another. Or if ya just wanna get a little Mad Maxy. Working bayonets! All the custom parts might complicate this one, though. More guns! I had something like 60-100 modeled when we went on hiatus, and I'd like to add 'em all in. description: Tired of zombies magically appearing out of nowhere? With this mod you can disable respawn but still face an endless threat. Clear the streets by destroying corpses (burn, bury, or stash them) or leave the corpses alone, and zombies will keep rising again forever. SANDBOX SETTINGS GUIDE: Revival Chance (%) – Sets the probability that a zombie will revive at all. For example, if set to 40%, there is a 40% chance the zombie will revive and a 60% chance it will remain dead. Fixed Revival Time – Set the number of in-game hours before a zombie revives. Note: If Random Mode is enabled, this value is ignored, and only the Min/Max Revival Time settings are used. Random Mode – When enabled, zombies revive after a random period instead of the fixed time. The revival time is calculated between the Min Revival Time and Max Revival Time settings. Min Revival Time – Defines the minimum number of in-game hours that must pass before a zombie can revive. For example, if Min is 5 and Max is 20, the zombie will revive somewhere between 5 and 20 hours. Max Revival Time – Defines the maximum number of in-game hours before a zombie can revive. Works together with Min Revival Time to create a random revival window. Workshop ID: 3555199477 Mod ID: UndyingZombies

mod_name: [B42] Immersive Preservation: Canning and Jarring (of evolved recipes)
description: Preserve 'evolved recipe' foods such as soup, stew, etc. in jars using the vanilla jarring method, for an immersive expansion to the game's preservation mechanics. Optional - remove requirements for salt and vinegar. Optional - sandbox settings: days until stale/rotten for all jarred food. Description: 1. Cook your evolved recipe. 2. Place into canning jar. 3. Cook sealed jar for an hour. 4. Store and enjoy at a later point in time. Auto-learning of jarring process lowered from level 8 to level 4 cooking. At default settings, jarred food (including vanilla preserved vegetables) lasts 300 days before going stale and 400 days before rotting at normal spoilage setting when kept without refrigeration (vanilla: 60 and 90 days). Note that the vanilla mechanic accounts for the age of produce, so make sure to can your produce at its freshest and as soon as possible after jarring. Please see my Realistic Distributions: Alcohol, Cigarettes, Clutter mod for more jars, lids, salt, and vinegar spawns. Additionally, see Rebalanced Yields: Butchering for more homesteading tweaks. Extra Info: -Compatible with all modded items as long as you can use them in the evolved recipes. -Jars allow you to store more produce than in a cooking pot or bowl as they are lighter. -Jars and lids returned in all expected scenarios, unless the lid is at low condition and gets broken. -The opened soup/stew/rice/pasta jars do not count as metal and can be microwaved. -Even though the jar is briefly displayed as 'uncooked', you will correctly receive cooked food if you decide to open it without canning. -The spice and seasoning icons are now transferred to the jar as of version 1.1.2 of this mod - they do not do so in vanilla when e.g. portioning soup from cooking pot into bowls. Future Plans: -Potentially create a realistic version - as the vanilla method is not safe for canning most of the things players are going to be canning. This will do for a video game for now, enjoy the expanded functionality. A pressure canner is used to reach higher than boiling temperatures (kills botulism spores) and preserve food that does not have naturally high acidity and/or salinity, and would otherwise be rendered unpalatable. The developers intended to allow the player to preserve high acidity vegetables in a water-bath canning method - this is suitable for many pickled vegetables, tomato sauces, relishes, jams, and chutneys. -Maybe a check for how big the food is, potentially allowing or requiring the player to use two jars. Compatibility: Lua implementations were used when possible to avoid overwriting vanilla scripts and functions. Only the vanilla canning 60/90 days script was affected. This mod will potentially extend the shelf life of any mods that allow more jarring and preservation as long as they use the vanilla script. Translations are provided for: DE, EN, ES, FR, IT, PL, PTBR, RU, and UA. Thanks to Refúgio Z for PTBR, and WRex for UA translations. Permissions: Please do not modpack or reupload. If this mod is deleted, you are welcome to reupload to Steam Workshop only. Thanks and enjoy! description: Changes the animal yields to provide more realistic, immersive quantities of meat from butchering. Build 42.12 note: Compatible with the latest update. Description: As you can see from the screenshots, vanilla butchering for larger animals (i.e. not chickens) is a complete waste of time as of the latest unstable build. I have balanced the functions that create the resulting loot by hand to provide a balance between realism and immersion for gameplay. An actual, fully grown cow would certainly provide more beef than this mod, but it certainly should provide more than three chickens, as it currently stands in vanilla gameplay. I strongly recommend you use the Butcher Hook Animal Size Fix mod as it provides further balancing to the butchering aspect of gameplay, the developers have missed out a vital parameter related to animal size when factoring in the butcher hook. From the author: To make a long story short, since build 42 came out any and all animals would have a static size of 0.6 on the hook due to being resized for the UI, the issue is that this ALSO affected the value used for butchering and harvesting meat from them. As such all this mod does it add an additional parameter to be passed to the butchering util file that uses the correct animal size rather than the static 0.6 that was used before. No animal meat values are changed or modified by this mod in any way, this only affects animals butchered on the hook. If this changes - being true as of the latest unstable build (October 2025), I will update the description accordingly. Similarly, if butchering is rebalanced by the developers, I shall make sure my mod is still relevant. You can use the mod Bug Zapper 9000 instead, but please load my mod after, by placing Rebalanced Yields: Butchering lower on the load order. This mod already includes one of the bug fixes, and the same script needed to be modified to rebalance butchering. Extra Info: -Cuts of meat, from all animals, weighing more than 0.4 can be halved with a craft recipe. -Overall, this mod does not focus on just increasing the amount of meat pieces that animals provide by butchering, but making sure that you do not get stacks of small unusable pieces. You will be getting larger cuts weighing up to several kilograms, you can process these in recipes and your aim upon butchering a large animal should switch to preservation. -Pigs have a moderate chance of providing lard, allowing the player to establish a sustainable source of cooking fat into the apocalypse. -Additionally, this mod tweaks the amounts of bones that animals, particularly small animals, have a chance to drop. Larger animals will still drop small bones (cows did not drop small bones, I have changed this so they do), and you should know that in vanilla it is possible to break larger bones with hammers to create fragments that can be used in recipes as small bones. -Penalty for not using the butcher hook reduced, as in vanilla, the lack of a butcher hook meant that large animals would yield half the pieces of meat, therefore twice as little in terms of hunger reduction and calories. Also, no leather. Using a butchering hook still provides a 20% bonus to base-defined animal values, so you would, in theory, benefit from 20% increase in meat yield by using it. -Vanilla roadkill would result in mangled scraps, as both the minimum and maximum yields for number of items would be halved, and the "meat ratio" (i.e. meat to nothing ratio, based on theoretical yield of the animal weight and your butchering skill) would be randomly set to a low amount. I have reduced the penalty for roadkill, however it is still sizeable, so you should avoid running over any animals that you can shoot or otherwise kill in melee. -This mod does not add any items that did not exist in the base game, however as hunger reduction/calories/protein/fats, etc. are governed by the base items as well as the scripts that spawn them, I had to use a lua implementation to tweak the calories of base meat items to real life values, and this should not conflict with mods that alter these items. Future Plans: -Make sure that rodents and raccoons (which use the Base.Smallanimalmeat item) are balanced further as it really is anyone's guess as to what is going on between the butchering and the animal trapping system. -Bacon from pigs maybe? Compatibility: Load this mod after the Butcher Hook Animal Size Fix and/or Bug Zapper 9000 by placing Rebalanced Yields: Butchering lower on the load order. This mod overwrites the AnimalPartsDefinitions.lua file responsible for the butchering loot and so will almost always be incompatible with other mods that affect the butchering loot. Additionally, this mod tweaks 2 functions in ButcheringUtil.lua (to make changes to "no butchering hook" and "roadkill" penalties) and therefore will probably be incompatible with other butchery balancing mods. Permissions: Please do not modpack or reupload. If this mod is deleted, you are welcome to reupload to Steam Workshop only. Thanks and enjoy! description: Compatibility: Build 42.12 - 42.19 Trap Manager is a clean and practical interface for monitoring, comparing, and understanding your traps in Project Zomboid Build 42. It gathers your traps into one clear window, shows their current status in a sortable table, explains key values with helpful tooltips, and includes a built-in simulator to preview vanilla catch chances by animal, trap, bait, zone, and skill. Trap Manager does not change vanilla trap mechanics. It only reads, organizes, and explains trap information. Sidebar shortcut: hover the Zone icon on the left sidebar to slide out the matching Trap button, then click it to open or close Trap Manager. What Trap Manager Does Shows all your traps in one window instead of checking them one by one. Displays trap data in a clear, sortable table. Adds tooltips that explain what each value means. Includes a built-in catch chance simulator. Helps compare traps, bait, zones, and skill levels more easily. Keeps vanilla gameplay untouched: no changes to capture logic, items, recipes, or odds. Trap List Window View all your traps in one place. Sort rows by clicking column headers. Resize columns by dragging separators. Hide or show columns from the header context menu. Use per-row visibility toggles to temporarily hide rows from the list. Read practical details such as bait, freshness, distance, chance, hours alive, and more. Built-in Catch Chance Simulator The simulator lets you preview vanilla trapping chances by combining: Animal Trap Bait Zone Trapping Skill Selecting an animal can automatically populate other fields with valid values, and tooltips help explain how each factor affects the result. Note: displayed chances are based on vanilla trapping logic. They are best understood as base vanilla candidate/catch chances. Mods that change trapping rules, cold modifiers, nearby-player behavior, or trap processing may affect the real result in-game. Window Controls Refresh — updates the trap list immediately. Auto — enables hourly in-game auto-refresh while the window is open. Vector — draws a line from your character to the trap currently hovered in the table. Reset — restores your default column layout. Full — shows every column and resizes the window to fit them. Show all — temporarily shows rows you previously hid. ModOptions — Native B42 Choose the hotkey used to open or close the window. Enable or disable hourly auto-refresh. Enable or disable longer explanatory tooltips. Choose which columns should be shown after pressing Reset. Restore factory defaults for the reset layout at any time. How to Open Trap Manager Left sidebar: hover Zone, then click the slide-out Trap button. Hotkey: use the key configured in ModOptions. Compatibility Compatible with Build 42.12 to 42.19. Designed specifically for Project Zomboid Build 42. Safe to add or remove from existing saves, since it is UI-focused. Does not alter vanilla trap mechanics. Generally compatible with other UI mods, Languages Includes translations for: AR, CA, CH, CN, DA, DE, EN, ES, FI, FR, HU, ID, IT, JP, KO, NL, PH, PL, PTBR, RU, TR, UA If your language is not available, the mod falls back to English. FAQ Does Trap Manager change catch chances or trap mechanics? No. It only reads, organizes, and explains trap information. Are the simulator chances exact? They are based on vanilla trapping logic and are intended as practical guidance. If several animals are valid candidates at the same time, vanilla may choose between candidates, so the displayed value should be read as a base chance estimate rather than a guaranteed final outcome. What is the difference between “Shown columns” and “Default columns”? Shown columns are the columns visible right now. Default columns are the columns restored when you press Reset. What does “Apply factory defaults” do? It restores the original default column setup used by Reset. What does “Vector” do? It draws a line from your character to the last trap you hovered in the table, helping you orient yourself more easily. Is the mod heavy on performance? No. It is lightweight, and auto-refresh only runs once per in-game hour while the window is open. Feature Summary One clean window for all your traps. Sortable, resizable, and hideable columns. Helpful tooltips across the interface. Built-in catch chance simulator. Sidebar shortcut and hotkey support. Native Build 42 ModOptions. Save-safe and gameplay-safe. Multilingual support. Install it, open the panel, and understand your traps at a glance. More Mods & Feedback You can find my other Project Zomboid mods here If you find this mod useful, please consider leaving a thumbs up and adding it to your favorites — it helps other players discover it. Feedback, bug reports, balance suggestions, and translation improvements are always welcome. Workshop ID: 3566766862 Mod ID: TrapManager

description: A simple b42 port of my "Item Stories" b41 mod. I've bundles all item stories into an All-In-One package, as requested. This mod makes buildings more "lived in" by spawning items inside them. It is picking what to spawn randomly from a 'story' system. If you've tried my "'immersive barricaded start" mod , this will spawn items in a similar way, but for every building, and at a much lower chance. Since this mod will spawn extra items, it is recommended you play with LOWER loot than usually would. I'd say it's pretty balanced so far, but I'm open to feedback. Start and Peak sandbox settings : start settings are applied before the start day, peak settings applied after the peak day, and proportionally scaled settings are applied between start day and peak day. Other stories can easily be added via submods, to spawn specific items in specific rooms and/or on specific furniture sprites for example. List of Item Stories included : "Room Loot": Spawns an item picked from the loot table of the room the item will spawn in. Kitchen items in kitchens, bedroom items in bedrooms, etc. Chance are low and customizable through sandbox settings, and it can trigger in ALL rooms and on ALL furniture sprites. Propane Tanks in Garages :Triggers in garages, basements, and sheds, spawns propane tanks ZuperCart's Supermarket Carts in Stores: Triggers in a variety of stores. Spawns Zupercart's supermarket carts. (Requires Zupercart mod, this story isn't used if you don't enable Zupercart) ZuperCart's Trolleys in Warehouses & Factories : Triggers in a variety of factories & storage areas. (Requires Zupercart mod, this story isn't used if you don't enable Zupercart) Pool cues and balls on billiard tables : self explatnatory Pallet crates in warehouses : Triggers in a variety of factories & storage areas. (Requires Forklift mod, this story isn't used if you don't enable Forklift) (New for this version) Rideable stories : Spawns a bicycle/skateboard/kick scooter sometimes in garages, basements, and some other rooms. (Requires Bicycle or Skateboard or Kick Scooter mod, this story isn't used if you don't enable one of them) I've removed the "Tire Racks in Mechanics and Garages" story , it was too much of a pain in the ass to deal with. Taking suggestions If you have an idea for an item story, you want an item to have a chance to spawn in some rooms or furnitures, leave it in the comments. Or better yet, simply make a mod yourself that uses the framework. You only need to know how set up a lua table, how building rooms are named (Click here for a list of PZ's rooms), and how to check furniture sprite names using the Brush Tool of PZ's debug mode. Though keep in mind that stories can only spawn inside a building (or basement). 'Forest' stories aren't possible, for example. Limitations Randomized Houses: Item stories are only generated in rooms that have not generated a vanilla randomized house story event. So if you absolutely want Item Stories to trigger on every room, you'll need set the Sandbox Setting "Meta" -> "Randomized House Chance" to "Never". Tilesets with no surface offsets : Some mods use tilesets that haven't properly mapped their tiles' furniture surface offsets, which means some of their furniture tiles will be considered as floor instead of furniture. Which generally means much lower chances of item story spawns. Even some furniture in vanilla don't have their surface offset mapped. One example would be the strongbox tiles, the I can't really do anything about it. The devs have said they're going to implement a sudo-3d map for each sprite, but it'll be a while before they release it in a build. These sprites can be recognized easily by simply trying to "Place Item" on one of these tiles to see that it's not working. The mod will still work fine though, it's not like these tiles break anything. 2D items : Some items in vanilla (like the ValuTech television, or the candy) don't have a 3D model. Also, some mods don't make proper 3D models for their items, too. In such cases, the item will be displayed in 2D on the ground. So don't be surprised if you find some ! Can it spawn modded items? Yep! Specifically, the 'Room Loot' story (the most common one) can spawn them, since it picks items directly from the same loot tables as containers. And then there's also Zupercarts carts & trolleys, and Forlift's pallet crates, for which I specifed the item Ids of the carts. However, I am NOT responsible if another modder hasn't properly inserted their custom items in the loot tables. What about performance? I made sure that when the player explores, the item stories spawner triggers on one unexplored room at a time, every tick, instead of all unexplored rooms at once. Because of this, even when I teleported into the middle of Louisville's biggest buildings, I didn't notice any lag. Workshop ID: 3569303590 Mod ID: ItemStoriesB42
