description: What it does Pick a weapon and stick with it. Every zombie you kill with it is counted, per weapon. Hit enough kills and it starts earning stuff: more damage, faster swings, bigger mags, better crits, tougher condition. Your beat-up machete slowly turns into something with a name, a stat line, and a bit of an attitude. If you played Vorpal Weapons on Build 41, you already know the loop. This is that idea, rebuilt from scratch for Build 42. "Something stirred within it. I felt it before I saw it." Three tiers Keep killing and the weapon climbs three tiers: Marked - it picks up its first affix. Bonded - a second affix stacks on. Blooded - past 200 kills, it gets a full multi-stat bonus and becomes properly yours. Every tier-up fully repairs the weapon, so a blade you've bonded with won't just crumble on you. Thresholds are all sandbox-adjustable if 200 feels too high or too low. "It stopped being a separate thing. It's just my arm now." Weapons get a personality On top of the stat affixes, each weapon grows a character based on how you actually use it. Fight at night a lot and it turns Nocturnal. Kill fast and often and it goes Ravenous. Play slow and picky and it becomes Patient. Never touch a whetstone and it stays Pristine. Change how you play and the personality drifts over a few days. These aren't just labels. A Nocturnal weapon cuts your panic at night. A Patient weapon gives crit chance. A Scarred weapon gains durability when you repair it. The effects get stronger as the weapon levels. Your tooltip ends up reading something like Proven. Nocturnal. Hunting. (that last word is a live mood that shifts with time of day, weather, and how rough things are right now). Guns too Pistols, rifles, shotguns, SMGs, all of it. Same kill-and-grow loop. Affixes can change fire rate, accuracy, magazine size, reload speed, recoil, noise, jam chance, and stagger. Your M9 turns into a Steady M9 of the Arsenal. Your shotgun ends up a Blooded Savage Shotgun of Destruction. It works with weapon mods automatically. Rain's Firearms, Brita's, whatever you run. If Zomboid treats it as a weapon, this mod will bond with it. Blooded weapons survive being reforged Saw off your shotgun, dismantle your fire axe, build a nail bat. If the weapon is Blooded, all the history carries over to the new form: kills, affixes, the lot. Lower-tier weapons don't survive the change, the bond has to run deep enough first. So a Blooded blade you've carried for 300 kills stays yours even when you turn it into something else. Vorpal Shards Something fell from the weapon. Sharp. Warm. Shards turn up rarely out in the world. Use one to reroll a weapon's affixes, three rerolls per shard. The old rolls get logged in your journal so you don't lose the record. The journal A worn notebook that keeps track of everything you've run into: every affix you've discovered, every weapon you've bonded with, and field notes from the lore books you've read. Eight different people wrote in it before you. Their story goes from "huh, weird" to "oh no" the deeper you read. "The pages are mostly blank. A few nervous notes. Morrison wasn't sure what he was writing down." Settings & compatibility Eight lore books scattered around Knox County fill in the journal as you find and read them. Full sandbox control: kill thresholds, affix rarity, which affix categories are on, notifications, or just switch the whole thing off. Safe to add or remove mid-save. Build 42.18.0+. Multiplayer is server-authoritative and fully synced. TooltipLib recommended for the best tooltips. Want the full affix list before you install? It's in the Discussions tab. Pour one out This whole thing is a love letter to Vorpal Weapons by electroglyph. Back in the day it was the weapon progression mod. Then he caught a case, went away, and never came back, and the mod sort of died with Build 41. This one's for you, electroglyph. The spirit lives on. Free my boy. His only crime was making bangers. Blood taught me your name. I practiced it in the dark. You slept. I whispered. If you ever see electroglyph out there, tell him Dark Sauce says thanks. description: Extended Categories (B42 SP & MP) Greatly expands the categories used in the game and applies its logic dynamically to all items, including those added by other mods. This also dynamically changes the categories of water containers based on their contents. For example, a bottle of soda will be categorized as "Beverage - Soft Drink", while an empty bottle, carton, mug or anything else that holds liquids will be categorized as "Container - Liquid" rather than "Food" or "Water". You can even mix some booze into your soda, and it will be categorized as "Beverage - Cocktail"! 📂 Categories Currently, the following broad categories are covered: 🍗 Foods → divided into Canned, Preserved, Prepared, Meat, Fish, Condiments, Spices, and much more 🍹 Beverages → Alcohol, Water, Tea, Coffee, SoftDrink, Cocktail, etc, with dynamic categorization based on container contents 👕 Apparel → clothing, protective gear and accessories divided into categories like Footwear, Socks, Top, Outerwear, Headwear, Gloves, Underwear, etc. 📚 Literature → Magazines, Hardcovers, Picture Books, Brochures, Fliers, Recipes and more. Categorized items such as phone books as "Literature / Junk". ⚔️ Weapon → Melee weapons divided by skill type and guns into Pistols, Rifles, Shotguns 🔫 Ammo → Magazine, Box, Carton 🚬 Cigarettes → not "Junk" anymore, but categorized as "Smokes" 💌 Memento → all plushies are now "Memento - Plushie" 🪴 Gardening → seeds, seed packets and compostable items 🍳 Cooking → utensils, cutlery and more (WIP 🏗️) 🛠️ Tools → subdivided by relevant skills (WIP 🏗️) 🧱 Materials → subdivided by relevant skills and/or material types (WIP 🏗️) Anything else that's in a box, bundled, stacked, cartoned, etc. will also be categorized as "<Category> - Box" or similar. For example, "Box of Nails" will be categorized as "Material - Box". If you have any ideas or requests, please let me know! For in-depth information and discussion about the categorization logic, visit the Categorization discussion. 📋 Changelog/Release Notes I write detailed change notes on every release. You can find them in the Change Notes tab of this page. 🌐 Translations Visit the Translations discussion to help with translations or see the current available languages. 💡 Recommendation This mod works best together with a mod that allows you to transfer items by their category, such as CleanUI. ⚙️ Compatibility This mod works with the latest version (42.14) and is safe to install or remove at any time. It supports both singleplayer and multiplayer. Built-in compatibility is included and/or maintained for the following mods: Food mods: Vanilla Foods Expanded Sapph's Cooking (WIP, needs more testing) Clothing/container mods: Authentic Z Frockin' Splendor! Pack Mule Customizable Containers Gun mods: Guns of '93 - you can add this optional patch created by Jiopaba and me to categorize guns by their ammo type! GaelGunStore - Note: triggers a lot of lua errors on load, this is not an issue with my mod and it does not affect gameplay. Read the error I trigger manually on game start for more information. Firearms B42 - Note: Same as with GaelGunStore, except it's only one item that triggers this. This should work with ANY other mod that adds content, as I use a broad approach to categorize items based on their properties, rather than specific item names. If a mod honors the game's item property and tag system, their stuff will be categorized correctly. If the mod adds custom categories, food types, body locations or other properties, you might see some items not being categorized correctly, or having missing translations ("IGUI_ItemCat_XXX"). If you run into any issues like that, please let me know, and I'll see what I can do to improve compatibility. Or, if you've tested another mod and everything works fine, please share that as well. :) 🙏 Acknowledgements A special thanks to Better Sorting for inspiring me to make this mod. I've made an extension for it with a similar idea, but it's much less comprehensive as there were far less useful properties/tags available on items pre B42, so most of it is based on assumptions on item names. Since Better Sorting wasn't being updated and I have a different approach to sorting in the first place, I decided to make my own fresh B42 mod from scratch, that I can continue to expand on. My other mods Workshop ID: 3650035249 Mod ID: CAExtendedCategories

description: Tank Water Tank Water adds a complete, realistic industrial water storage system to the world of Project Zomboid. Designed to feel like a natural part of the vanilla game, this mod introduces large-scale water infrastructure commonly found in farms, warehouses, construction sites, and industrial areas — with uncertainty, planning, and long-term survival in mind. Not every tank is guaranteed to contain water. Some may save your run. Others will remind you that nothing is free after the water shutoff. Features Industrial Water Tanks Adds multiple industrial water tanks with different capacities: 1200 L – Industrial Tank (S) 2000 L – Industrial Tank (M) 5000 L – Industrial Tank (L) 10000 L – Industrial Tank (XL) Tanks spawn naturally in appropriate industrial, rural, and construction-related locations. Each tank has its own stored water amount and can spawn full or empty. How to Use – Tank Water System This mod adds a realistic water storage and transfer system to Project Zomboid, allowing you to pump, store, filter, and manage large quantities of water without magic or instant refills. 1. Place a Water Tank Obtain a Water Tank. Place it on the ground where you want your water storage. Tanks store large amounts of water. Water Tanks only function when properly connected to a pump. 2. Connect a Motor Pump Place a Motor Pump near a water source (river, lake, rain collector, etc.). Connect the pump to the tank using a Transfer Hose. Hose connections are site-to-site and respect distance limits. No infinite range. No teleporting water. 3. Choose Your Water Source Carefully If you pump contaminated water, the tank will store contaminated water. If you pump clean water through a filter, the tank will store clean water. You cannot mix clean and contaminated water in the same tank. Once a tank is filled with one type of water, that state remains until emptied. 4. Filtration System Filters allow contaminated water to be purified before entering the tank. Filters have limited durability. If the filter breaks, the pump stops automatically. No hidden purification. The system respects water state logic. 5. Water States The system uses only two states (vanilla-compatible): Clean Water Contaminated Water If contaminated water is stored: You must boil it before drinking. The tank does not magically purify water. 6. Pumping & Wear Pumping consumes fuel. Motor Pumps slowly degrade with use. All actions are progressive (no instant transfers). 7. Maintenance & Risk Large tanks reduce micromanagement. Water cleanliness must still be managed manually. Accepting contaminated water means accepting risk. Water is powerful. But it is never automatic. Inspection & Interface Interactive inspection UI for tanks and motor pump. Displays tank type, capacity, stored water, percentage, and visual progress bar. Displays pump fuel level, condition, operational status, and connection state. Skills & Requirements Operating and repairing the motor pump requires vanilla-style skills: Electricity Level 1 Mechanics Level 2 Required skills and tools are clearly displayed in the inspection panel. Tools Required Screwdriver Vise Grips Gameplay Focus Designed for long survival runs and base infrastructure planning. Encourages realistic water management instead of instant solutions. Scales naturally from mid-game to late-game survival. Why It Matters After the water shutoff, reliable water sources become rare. Industrial tanks can secure your base for days, weeks, or even months — but only if you have the fuel, skills, and setup to use them. Finding a massive tank doesn’t guarantee safety. It guarantees responsibility. Design Philosophy Vanilla-friendly balance and pacing. No instant or magical systems. Physical distance matters. Infrastructure must be built, not exploited. Scales naturally from mid-game to late-game survival. This mod is meant to feel like something that should have always been there. Compatibility Singleplayer and Multiplayer supported. Safe to add to existing saves. No vanilla files are overwritten. No sandbox options required. Not compatible with Dynamic Backpack Updates, Skill Recovery Journal mod. Mod Interaction Tank Water is designed as a standalone infrastructure system. The industrial tanks added by this mod do not automatically integrate with other water-related mods. Water transfer is handled exclusively through the Tank Water motor pump and hose system. Known Interactions [B42] Functional Gutters Tanks will NOT automatically collect rainwater from gutters. This is an intentional design decision to avoid passive or infinite water generation. [B42] Water Pipes / Plumbing Mods Tanks will NOT automatically connect to the features of other water system mods. Vanilla rain collectors and plumbing remain unaffected. Design Notes Physical distance, fuel consumption, and player interaction are core design pillars of this mod. Automatic integration with plumbing or rain collection systems would bypass these mechanics. Compatibility patches may be considered in the future if they respect the same balance and constraints. This mod prioritizes realism, player involvement, and infrastructure planning over passive automation. Notes Standalone system (no external mod dependencies). Balanced to feel like an official Project Zomboid feature. Designed and tested for Project Zomboid Build 42. Credits 3D models, system design, UI, and implementation by MasterGG This mod's permissions fall under TIS's policy: Ask for permission (theindiestone.com) This mod can only be added to and extended with the express permission from the original creator. description: Numb Trait Adds a progression-based emotional hardening system tied to zombie kills. As survivors accumulate kills they gain traits that progressively reduce emotional penalties. There are currently two versions of this mod included — enable only one at a time: NumbTrait_B42 — v1 (original). Build 42.13.2+ NumbTrait_B42_V2 — v2 (redesign). Build 42.18+ Running both simultaneously causes double kill progression since each version tracks kills independently. Switching from v1 to v2 You can safely switch from v1 to v2 on an existing save without starting a new character or save. Disable NumbTrait_B42 and enable NumbTrait_B42_V2 — your kill count carries over. Your next kill will trigger v2 to re-evaluate your kill count and apply the correct v2 trait, which may differ from what you currently hold due to the redesigned tier order. Sandbox settings are not compatible between versions — reconfigure from scratch when switching from v1 to v2. Tier Progression Kill thresholds are configurable per tier in Sandbox settings. Stat Clamping v1: Hardened through Apathetic hard-lock Panic to 0. Discomfort is clamped to 0 for all custom traits and is not configurable. Desensitized uses vanilla behavior. Numb clamps all stats to 0. v2: Panic now descends gradually per tier. Discomfort is now capped and configurable per tier. Desensitized receives mod-side Stress, Unhappiness, and Boredom clamping (Panic and Discomfort remain vanilla at Desensitized). All values below are defaults and configurable in Sandbox settings. Corpse Looting Immunity Stress and unhappiness from looting corpses are suppressed: v1: Hardened, Calloused, Detached, Apathetic v2: Hardened through Desensitized (T2–T6) — Desensitized is now included Negative Trait Removals * Pacifist and Smoker removals are optional and configurable in Sandbox settings. Sandbox Options Both versions: kill thresholds per tier, enable/disable individual tiers, max Stress/Unhappiness/Boredom per tier, optional removal toggles (Brave, Desensitized, Smoker, Pacifist), and auto-reapply removed progression traits. v2 additionally: max Panic per tier (Hardened–Apathetic), max Discomfort per tier (Hardened–Apathetic), and max Stress/Unhappiness/Boredom for Desensitized. v2 uses a unified Enable* toggle naming convention (EnableBrave, EnableHardened, …, EnableNumb). Known Issues Trait icons need to be re-made or properly re-scaled for the Project Zomboid UI Stress gain from the Smoker trait appears to ignore this mod's stat clamping Starting with a Veteran character using NumbTrait v2 means no trait progression until you reach the requirements for the Numb trait. description: Are you tired of finding all these specimens, microscopes, and science magazines but having nothing useful to do with them? Same. Introducing the Science skill - finally a reason to hoard all that nerdy stuff! What does Science do? Research Specimens Found a jar with a brain in it? A dead rat? Some weird mushrooms? Now you can actually study them! Just find a microscope, plop your specimen nearby, and get that sweet, sweet Science XP. Where to find microscopes: schools, medical clinics, hospitals, police stations (forensics), and the occasional fancy house. Unlockable traits Some specimens are tagged for trait research: each unique item type you study at a microscope counts toward that trait. By default you need 10 different tagged specimens per trait (see mod data — vanilla.lua — if you want the full lists). You still get Science XP every time. If your character already has the trait, you keep the XP but no longer progress that unlock. Herbalist — berries, mushrooms, medicinal plants, and many wild forage plants. Reaching the threshold unlocks Herbalist (including the usual recipe/knowledge you’d expect). Blacksmith — metal specimens: ingots, ore, scrap, and related items (the mod often merges variants of the same metal into one research “slot”). Gardener — crop and herb seeds (research the seed items as specimens). Look for the small gray "R" on item icons - that means you haven't read/researched it yet and it can give you Science XP! Faster Learning Higher Science = faster skill book reading. - Up to 50% faster at Science 10 - Also speeds up recipe research from items XP Boost Science makes you smarter at everything (except punching zombies): - +2% bonus to all non-combat XP per Science level - That's +20% at max level. description: Goose's Kentucky National Guard Professions Authentic 1993 KYNG professions, loadouts, and equipment for the Knox Exclusion Zone. This mod adds seven historically grounded professions drawn from the units and equipment the Kentucky National Guard would realistically have deployed during the 1993 Knox Exclusion Zone operation. Each profession comes with a profession-appropriate loadout with realistic ammo counts, rations and field equipment that are designed to be balanced, immersive and true to the era. If you want your playthrough to actually feel like you survived the first hours of the apocalypse as a member of the military, this is where you start. Professions CBRN Specialist (MOS 74D, -10 Points) Chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear specialist from the 103rd Chemical Battalion. Combat Engineer (MOS 12B, -16 Points) Field engineer from the 201st Engineer Battalion trained in demolitions and obstacle clearance. Equipped for breaching, fortification and improvised munitions. Combat Medic (MOS 91B, -12 Points) Medical specialist from the 917th Medical Company of the 201st Engineer Battalion. Carries a full trauma kit and field pharmaceuticals enough to give field care and sustain a squad of four. Infantryman (MOS 11B, -10 Points) Standard light infantryman from the 1st Battalion, 149th Infantry Regiment. Carries a full combat load with appropriate rations, protective equipment and standard issue weapons. Military Police (MOS 95B, -12 Points) Perimeter security and law enforcement specialist from the 198th Military Police Battalion. Equipped for checkpoint duty and civil control operations within the KEZ. Motor Transport Operator (MOS 88M, -10 Points) Logistics driver and vehicle operator from the 2123rd Transportation Company. Jeeves Integration The bridge between your Discord server and your Project Zomboid server. Jeeves Integration connects the Jeeves Discord Bot to your game, bringing chat relay, player rank colors, alert sounds, and remote server commands all into one seamless package. Discord Chat Relay Messages sent in your Discord server appear in-game, and in-game chat flows back to Discord. Keep your community connected whether they're playing or just hanging out in the server. Player Rank Colors Assign ranks to players through the Jeeves bot, and their names are automatically colorized in the in-game chat. Six rank tiers are available, each with a fully customizable color chosen from a palette of 27 options: Rank 1 — Fuel Rank 2 — Spark Rank 3 — Cinder Rank 4 — Flame Rank 5 — Blaze Rank 6 — Inferno Rank colors are configured through sandbox options, so admins can customize the look to match their server's identity. Colors update in real time — no restart needed. Alert Sounds When the server is about to restart or a mod update is incoming, players hear customizable alert sounds at configurable countdown intervals (10 minutes, 5 minutes, 1 minute, 10 seconds). Choose from 11 different sound options for each alert tier — or disable them entirely. Separate sound selections for automatic restarts and mod updates give you full control over how each event sounds. Server Commands Jeeves Integration acts as the command bridge for the entire Jeeves ecosystem. The bot writes commands to shared files, and the mod picks them up and executes them in-game. description: B42.16 Compatibility Update A vanilla default reload animation replaces the custom animation until an official fix for custom animations is released. The mod will now work in all versions of B42. Hopefully. What It is It enables you to create a crossbow from a bunch of junk. What It Do It do: - Be a (short-ish)-ranged weapon - Be quiet to fire - Be good at hunting animals (if you're sneaky enough) - Be making you feel sneaky and cool as hell - Be accessible to create (even to wilderness playstyles with no access to other ranged weaponry) - Be giving you a reason to collect/save some otherwise less than useful items - Be scaling decently with critical chance and range as aiming level increases - Be allowing ammo to be retrieved from dead zombies (configurable in sandbox settings) - Be rarely spawning the items themselves as well as the recipe magazine in appropriate places/denizens throughout the world - Be able to be added to multiplayer servers and existing saves Alright, I'm done with the 'be' thing, promise. What It Don't It don't: - Reliably one-shot zombies, especially at low aiming levels. It's made of scraps- temper your expectations. - Handle hordes well. Probably best to pick zombies off one at a time. If you attract a crowd, then good luck. - Reload quickly. Custom (sorta) reload animation means it takes a second or two to ready another shot. NO MAGAZINES! Crafting Requirements A magazine will be required in order to learn the recipes. Researching an existing item or reaching the auto-learn level of the respective skill will also teach the recipes if a magazine cannot be found. - Makeshift Crossbow: Requires Maintenance level 4; recipe auto-learned at Maintenance level 6 - Makeshift Bolt: Requires at least Carving level 2 in order to carve bolt shafts. The recipe itself can be auto-learned at Carving level 4. Learning the recipe for assembling the bolt will also teach the recipe for crafting its constituent parts (flights and shaft). "Why... ...does firing the crossbow fill the area with light?" At the moment, ranged weapons are hard-coded to emit light when fired. Smarter, handsomer modders than myself have tried to tackle this and so far no dice. Maybe some day I will find a solution for this! ...doesn't it train my aiming skill?" It does, just much more slowly than most conventional firearms. Aiming XP is based on damage done per shot, and seeing as this is essentially a rubberband nail gun, it's gonna be a bit slow to train aiming. Not much I can do about that one, sorry. ...does my reloading skill go up so fast?" Opposite situation, but similar issue: you gain ~1 reloading XP per reload of most weapons/magazines. Since you reload between shots with this thing, that's sorta just how it works. Your reloading arm is going to be absolutely YOKED, though. ...does it not fire after reloading sometimes in MP?" Because I'm a bit of a hack and can't find a way to overcome some of the desync issues multiplayer causes the weapon. If you can't seem to reload it, just set it down, then pick it back up. Should put it back to normal operation. ...are the requirements to craft everything so high?" Because I like the idea of you having to survive with only rocks and sharp sticks for a while before you can start using ranged weapons. This mod is meant to bridge the gap between low-tech, abundant melee weapons and high-tech, rare firearms. It can't really replace either, so it is what it is. Enjoy. Want more desserts in Project Zomboid? Calling all dessert lovers and aspiring pastry chefs—come join the fun! Tired of fighting zombies? Is your character feeling down? Craving something sweet? Then treat yourself to some desserts and get that sugar boost—you might feel a little better. With just a few “simple” steps, you can easily make a variety of desserts. For example, you can grow pumpkins or sunflowers, collect seeds, grind them into nut powder using a mill, and make macarons. You can also craft tools like spatulas or cake turntables in a furnace and use them for baking. Or use a butter churn to turn milk into whipped cream. Simple, right? But if those “simple” steps feel like too much work, you can always find desserts while looting the world. Some might be spoiled, but hey—once it’s in your stomach, it’s all the same, right? You might get a stomachache or feel a bit worse… but come on, in an apocalypse, being able to enjoy sweet roll cakes and cream puffs isn’t such a bad deal. After eating too many sweet desserts, you might start craving something savory. You know—sweet and salty balance. When that happens, you can enjoy a hearty bowl of pork soup or cook up some spicy ramen in a metal pot. And if you're heading out on a zombie-hunting “picnic,” packing some kimbap will make it even more enjoyable. ---Developer’s Note Hello! This is my first mod, made from scratch with zero coding experience and a lot of trial and error. There may still be rough edges… but I hope you’ll be kind and enjoy it anyway! I’ll continue improving it over time. I’m also gradually adding more desserts and ingredients. My goal is to bring a full “pastry chef” experience into Project Zomboid. description: Forged by Combat The apocalypse doesn't forgive hesitation. But it does reward those who survive it. Forged by Combat is a progressive combat mastery system for Project Zomboid. Every zombie you put down with a melee weapon leaves a mark — not on you, but in you. Over time, that experience shapes a fighter. No matter your skill with an axe or a hammer, the more you kill, the deadlier you are. How it works Kill zombies with melee weapons to earn XP and level up your Fighting Skill perk, visible in the Skills tab. No XP boost, only your kill count matters! 10 levels of progression — you start rough, and earn your edge: Melee kills only — vehicles, stomps, and ranged weapons don’t count Profession and trait starting bonuses — Veterans start with bonuses, the nurse doesn’t… Mid-game install compatible — initializes from your profession and traits XP bar visible in the Skills UI Three sandbox difficulty settings: Soft, Medium, Brutal How it feels Levels 0–2: Penalties to damage and attack speed. You’re not a fighter yet. You’ve never done this before. Your grip is wrong, your timing is off. The weight of the weapon feels foreign in your hands. Level 3: Baseline. You hold your own. You’ve found your footing. Swings land where you mean them. Skulls crack a little easier now. Levels 4-10: Growing bonuses to damage, attack speed, and critical chance. You become something to be feared. You split skulls like firewood. The weight of your weapon has disappeared. You never miss. One-handed weapons reward speed. Two-handed weapons reward power. Progression table Thresholds Bonuses Values are meant for medium difficulty Speed caps at level 6. Damage and crit continue to grow up to level 10. Sandbox settings Soft: 75% of bonuses and penalties Medium (default): Full values Brutal: 125% — higher ceiling, steeper early game Compatibility Build 42.13+ Available in English 🇺🇸, French 🇫🇷 & Spanish 🇪🇸. Other languages can be added — feel free to ask in the comments. Compatible with most mods — does not alter zombie behavior or loot tables Multiplayer: not fully functional. Fix on the way 🚑 Credits This mod was inspired by the Combat Mastering Skill mod. The core mechanic is different: progression is driven exclusively by melee kills — no XP bonuses from books or other sources. This is my first mod 👶 Feedback, bug reports, and suggestions are very welcome — don't hesitate to leave a comment. Workshop ID: 3668844554 Mod ID: ForgedByCombat

ATMs: deposit, withdraw, and transfer money to other players from your bank account.Branch System (Sedes) Create multiple branches of your shop — each with its own cash register, shelves, and ATMs. Right-click registered points and assign them to a specific branch. Each branch maintains its own shopping cart, commission tracking, and seller attendance. Manage all branches from the Config panel: create new ones, remove old ones, see them listed in real time. Players interact with the branch closest to them — the sede context is automatic.Buy & Sell Browse items by category (Melee, Ranged, Ammo, Medical, Food, Tools, Clothing, Bags, Materials, Books, etc.). Bulk sell — sell multiple items of the same type at once. Floating Cart Widget shows your current cart at a glance.Jewelry Exchange Dedicated tab to exchange rings, necklaces, earrings, bracelets, watches, diamonds, and gold bars for bills. Auto-detects modded jewelry by name patterns (diamond, gold, pearl, ruby, emerald, etc.). Select all / deselect — exchange multiple jewels in one click.ATM & Banking Virtual bank account per player — deposit bills, withdraw later. ATM Transfers: send money directly to another player's account from any ATM. Debit Card system: find a debit card in the world, link it to your name, then use ATMs. Balance Widget — floating panel showing Bills + Account + Total. Hybrid payment — pay with bills, account balance, or both.Seller & Commission System Admins assign Sellers (by username or server role: Seller, Vendedor, Moderator). Sellers can "Attend" a cash register — they earn a commission on every transaction (buy, sell, exchange). Commissions are tracked per branch (sede) — sellers earn only from their assigned branch. Commission is configurable (0-50%, default 3%). If no seller is attending, commissions accumulate as pending — sellers can claim them later with a button. Self-commission prevention: you can't claim commissions from your own purchases. Commission paid in cash (if seller is present) or deposited to account (if deferred).Dynamic Economy 9 price tiers from FREE to LEGENDARY with smart auto-pricing based on item properties. description: Every night could be your last. Siege Night turns your base into a battleground. Every few nights, the dead march on your position from a single direction -- wave after wave, growing stronger as the night goes on. Build your walls. Stock your ammo. Survive until dawn. Built for fortress defense. Solo or multiplayer. Mod ID: SiegeNight | Workshop ID: 3669589584 Workshop URL: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3669589584 Wave Cycles -- WAVE (dense assault), TRICKLE (stragglers), and BREAK (patch up and reinforce). 3 to 7 waves per night, escalating as midnight approaches. Directional Attacks -- every siege picks one of 8 compass directions and all zombies come from that angle for the entire night. Different directions each siege force real decisions about where your walls go. Siege Scaling -- zombie count scales with sieges survived and players online. Early game: 3 waves, ~75-150 zombies. Late game: 6-7 waves, up to 1,500. Siege Modes (MP) -- Per-Base (independent sieges per group) or Unified (one global siege targeting the busiest area). Configurable in sandbox. Safehouse Anchor Mode -- zombies target your claimed safehouse instead of your player position. They attack your base even if you leave. Dawn Survival -- make it to sunrise and your character announces the kill count. The siege panel tracks everything. 30+ Sandbox Options -- tune siege frequency, zombie count, scaling, spawn distance, anchor mode, special zombie rates, mini-horde thresholds, and more. Spread across 3 sandbox pages. Kill Tracking -- a Siege Night tab in your character info (press H) shows wave/phase, kills this siege, lifetime totals, and full siege history for the last 20 nights. Sprinters -- fast. Blend in with the horde until they're already on you. Breakers -- construction gear. Built to smash through your barricades and walls. Tanks -- military outfits, 5x normal health. Two per siege by default. Specials start spawning after midnight when the siege is at its peak. All rates and tank health can be tuned or disabled in sandbox options. Between siege nights, your activity generates heat. Generators (+15), gunfire (+10), driving (+8), heavy construction (+5). Heat builds around your location and decays slowly when you go quiet. Push your luck too far and you'll hear: "Something's attracting them from the south..." Mini-hordes come from the direction of your heat source. An attractor system pulls them toward you. Kill enough and the attractor shuts off -- the rest scatter. Cooldown between triggers and a daily cap so you won't get chain-hit. Recommended MP Baseline ("Normal") If SiegeNight feels like it's dumping hundreds of zombies on you early (ex: day 3 Rosewood), these are a good starting point for multiplayer. Note: SiegeNight is still being balanced. The defaults are intentionally flexible, not a tuned "Normal" difficulty yet. description: Jeeve's Hordes Surviving the apocalypse just got a whole lot harder. Jeeve's Hordes adds dynamic, unpredictable horde night events to your server that will keep every player on edge. You never know exactly when the next horde is coming — only that it is coming. How It Works Hordes strike at night on a randomized schedule. The server picks a random interval between events (configurable from every few days to once a month), then picks a random time during the night window to unleash the dead. When the horde arrives, zombies spawn around every online player and are drawn toward them by a pulsing sound lure. A warning moodle appears on the morning of a horde day so you know tonight is the night — giving you just enough time to prepare, barricade, and arm yourself. Survivor Escalation Every horde you survive makes the next one more dangerous — just for you. Each survival adds to your personal zombie multiplier, meaning veteran survivors face increasingly brutal waves while newer players get a fair fight. Your multiplier caps at a server-configurable maximum. The global horde count also grows over time. Each event adds more zombies to the base count, so the entire server faces a rising threat as the days go on. Death resets your progression. If you die, your personal multiplier goes back to zero. High risk, high reward. Rotten Flesh & Zombie Stew Zombies have a chance to drop Rotten Flesh when killed. Collect it to craft Zombie Stew — a foul concoction made by combining Rotten Flesh, water, and a cooking pot. Eating Zombie Stew before a horde grants you immunity for that event. The horde ignores you entirely — no zombies will spawn around you and the lure won't pulse near you. Perfect for nights when you're undergeared or just want to sit one out. But be careful: Using Zombie Stew for 5 consecutive horde nights triggers a streak penalty that resets your entire survivor progression back to zero. You can't rely on stew forever. Fragrance à la Jeeves Found rarely in the world, Fragrance à la Jeeves is a mysterious cologne with a very different effect. Using it doesn't protect you — it attracts the dead. On a non-horde day, the fragrance triggers a personal horde just for you — a solo event using the same spawning and progression mechanics as a normal horde night. On a horde day, the fragrance grants a 200% zombie spawn multiplier — tripling your wave size. Survive it, and you'll earn double progression plus a boosted military airdrop (when Jeeve's Drops is installed). It's the fastest way to climb the ranks — if you can handle the heat. Horde Reward Scaling: Every 10 hordes survived increases the loot multiplier on your completion airdrop by +0.2×, capping at 3.0×. Fragrance doubles this progression rate and guarantees a military crate type. The longer you survive, the better your rewards. Using fragrance for 5 consecutive horde nights increases your lure radius by 50%, drawing zombies from further away during future hordes. The penalty resets on death or any horde night where fragrance was not used. Stew and fragrance share a 7 in-game day cooldown — using one blocks the other. Fully Configurable Every aspect of the mod is adjustable through sandbox options: Scheduling — Set the earliest start day, frequency range, and night hours Zombie Count — Base count per player, increment per event, and maximum cap Spawn Behavior — Min/max spawn distance, safe radius, lure range and volume Progression — Survivor multiplier cap Items — Rotten Flesh drop chance, Zombie Stew immunity toggle Fragrance — Toggle Fragrance à la Jeeves on/off, configure world spawn rate Warnings — Toggle player warning moodles on/off Discord Integration Designed to work seamlessly with the Jeeves Discord Bot (part of the Jeeves server stack) for full server management. When paired with JeevesBot, your Discord server receives: Notifications when a horde is scheduled Alerts when the horde begins Summary when the event ends, including survivor count Admin commands to trigger, stop, or check horde status from Discord Discord integration is optional — the mod works perfectly as a standalone. Compatibility Build 42 — Multiplayer and singleplayer. Note: Jeeve's Integration is required and must load before Jeeve's Hordes. It provides the custom moodle framework for horde warning, immunity, and fragrance indicators. If using Jeeve's Drops as well, ensure the load order is: Integration Drops Hordes. The mod.info enforces this automatically via loadModAfter. Part of the Jeeves Ecosystem Jeeve's Integration — Discord chat relay, player ranks, custom moodles, and server commands Jeeve's Claims — Safehouse, land, and vehicle claim protection Jeeve's Drops — Airdrop and supply drop events with guarded loot Jeeve's Journals — Skill recovery journals Jeeve's Patches — Compatibility fixes for popular mods Jeeve's QoL — Quality-of-life improvements bundle Jeeve's Personal Computer — In-game computers, arcade games, training disks, and skill backup Jeeve's Zones — Admin-defined map zones with per-zone rules Jeeve's Build — Buildable furniture and structures from licensed tile packs Jeeve's Solar Arrays — Solar power generation (Immersive Solar Arrays for Build 42) Workshop ID: 3672042113 Mod ID: JeevesHordes

description: Revamped and updated version of the mod: The Calm Before The Storm Built for version B41.78+ and B42.13+! DESCRIPTION - SAFE TO ADD/REMOVE MID-GAME! - WORKS IN MULTIPLAYER! Nowhere is safe forever. "Horde Rush" is a survival-focused mod designed to keep you on your toes and test your base defenses when you least expect it... Are you prepared to hold the line? PREREQUISITES For this mod to function correctly, you must adjust a few specific Sandbox Options. You can find these settings under `Advanced Zombie Options` (if editing in-game) or under the `ZombieConfig` section (if editing your server's SandboxVars file). 1. Enable Zombie Respawn The mod relies on zombies existing in the world. Make sure respawning is turned on by setting the following values to greater than zero. Default Values here are pretty good enough. Respawn Hours = 72 Respawn Unseen Hours = 16 2. Adjust Population Multipliers To ensure the horde events feel appropriately challenging and intense, I highly recommend tweaking your population levels. Default values here are also pretty good: Population Multiplier = 2.0 Population Start Multiplier = 1.0 Population Peak Multiplier = 1.5 3. Increase Sound Follow Distance Zombies need to be allowed to travel long distances when they hear any in-game events' sounds. Follow Sound Distance = 450 Note: If you set the "Horde Distance" in the mod options higher than 300, you must increase this sandbox value to match it using formula: Follow Sound Distance = Horde Distance * 1.42 HOW IT WORKS * No Artificial Spawns: This mod does not spawn new zombies out of thin air. It only attracts the undead that are already roaming nearby in your world. * Sandbox Scaling: Because it uses the existing local population, the difficulty and size of these waves are directly tied to your game's default Zombie Config in the Sandbox options. Play with high population multipliers, and you'll face massive, overwhelming hordes. Play on lower populations, and the rushes will be more manageable. The event cycles through three phases: * The 'Cooldown' Phase - The time between events. Gameplay is normal and zombies will behave as usual. * The 'Calm' Phase - The period in which mass zombie migration occurs. Towns and cities will seem deserted and eerily quiet. This gives players the opportunity to scavenge and build defenses before the inevitable horde arrives. * The 'Storm' Phase - Zombies return in massive hordes and persistently hunt down the player(s). It will take some time... quite some time for the horde to actually march toward your location, providing a window to prepare your defenses. The event begins with smaller waves of stragglers and escalates into larger groups as the main horde arrives. Zombies are, by default, always aware of the player's position, which can be changed in the sandbox options. FOUND AN ISSUE? Please, raise this issue on my GitHub: https://github.com/drag0no/PZ_Rin_HordeRush/issues CREDITS Massive thanks to socialtroglodyte for the brilliant core logic of this mod and permission to use his code! description: Advanced Health System Survive your own body. Advanced Health System is a complete physiological overhaul for Project Zomboid focused on progressive, realistic health deterioration based on player decisions. This is not a random illness mod. This is a systemic survival framework. Your body reacts to: Sleep neglect Poor nutrition Dehydration Stress accumulation Physical exhaustion Infection Weight Temperature Poison Health conditions develop gradually through defined stages: Mild → Moderate → Severe → Peak → Recovery No instant deaths. No unfair spikes. No invisible RNG. Core Features Progressive 3–8 day health episodes No phase skipping Only one dominant critical condition at a time Immunity cooldown after recovery Critical conditions can affect vitality Integrated with Vanilla First Aid skill First Aid Reworked First Aid is no longer reactive — it is preventive. Gain XP by maintaining proper hygiene Gain XP by sleeping correctly Gain XP by preventing severe episodes Auto-examination system with skill-based diagnosis High skill reveals dominant conditions and true severity Low skill means limited perception. High skill means informed survival. Health Interface You can open the interface with the H keybind or by using the mod button on the vertical buttons of your screen. Minimalist body silhouette Color-coded severity based on medical knowledge No numbers, no bars, no artificial stats Clean and immersive visual feedback The body tells a story — if you know how to read it. Advanced Medical Items This mod introduces a set of advanced medical items designed to expand survival possibilities without replacing the vanilla system. Electrolyte Drinks – Improve hydration recovery and help stabilize the body under stress. Broad Spectrum Antibiotics – More effective against infections compared to standard treatments. Beta-blockers – Help control stress-related physiological responses. Anti-inflammatory Medication – Reduce internal strain and inflammation effects. Medical Thermometer – Useful for tracking body condition and detecting abnormalities. Vanilla medical items are still fully functional and remain a viable option. However, AHS medical items are generally more effective and suited for advanced or critical conditions. Dynamic Traits System AHS introduces a fully dynamic health trait system driven by your character's habits and physical condition over time. Traits are not static – they evolve based on how you play. Poor habits (dehydration, stress, infections, exhaustion) may lead to negative traits. Maintaining good health over time can grant positive adaptations. Your body reacts to accumulated strain through hidden systems such as: Hydration Sleep Stress Physical Bacterial Poison Weight Temperature You are not given exact values. Instead, your character provides subjective feedback based on their First Aid skill. Diagnosis & Perception The diagnosis system is designed around uncertainty and interpretation. Low First Aid → vague and unreliable feedback Higher First Aid → more precise and consistent observations Symptoms may overlap or appear gradually Not all conditions are immediately obvious “You feel better… but something is still not right.” Design Philosophy AHS is not a numbers-based system. No visible stats or exact condition values No instant clarity on what is happening Focus on immersion, interpretation, and survival decision-making Your character does not know everything. You must observe, interpret, and adapt. AHS does not punish single mistakes. It punishes accumulated neglect. Three days without proper care will have consequences Ignoring warning signs will escalate risk Recovery takes time — there are no instant fixes Your worst enemy might not be the zombies — it might be your own body. Compatibility ✔ Multiplayer supported ✔ Designed for long-term survival runs ✔ Does not replace vanilla health system Stay alive. Stay aware. description: A fully-featured smartphone mod for Project Zomboid Build 42. Find phones in houses, offices, and stores. Use them to navigate, message other players, and more. Install xPhone Sound Pack (separate Workshop item) to unlock GPS voice guidance with spoken directions in English and Spanish. == PHONE MODELS == xPhone Disposable — The cheapest model. Found commonly in houses. Has a fixed internal battery that cannot be replaced or recharged. Once the battery dies, the phone is permanently dead. Use it wisely. xPhone Standard — Mid-tier model found in offices and stores. Uses a replaceable battery (xPhone Battery item). When the battery runs low, swap it for a fresh one from your inventory through the phone's settings menu. xPhone Solar — Rare high-tier model. Its built-in battery automatically recharges when you are outdoors during daytime. The longer you stay in sunlight, the more charge it recovers. Nearly self-sustaining for light usage. == BATTERY SYSTEM == Every phone has a 0-100% battery that drains realistically based on what you do: - Music Playback: moderate drain (~8h on Disposable, ~11h on Standard, ~20h on Solar) - GPS Navigation: lightest drain (~11h on Disposable, ~16h on Standard, ~33h on Solar) - Idle: no drain while the phone is in your inventory and not in use The Solar model recharges automatically when you walk outdoors during daylight hours. == APPS == Messages (Text Messaging) Each phone gets a unique 5-digit number assigned when first activated. Save contacts by name and send private text messages to any player at any distance. Conversations are displayed in a chat-style interface with timestamps. A Global Chat channel lets everyone with an active xPhone communicate together. You receive real-time toast notifications for incoming messages from any screen — click to jump directly to the conversation. GPS / Maps A full navigation system with a real-time rendered map showing 1,000+ named streets, buildings, points of interest, and city labels. Features include: - Search: type any place name or street to find it instantly - Navigate: select a destination and get A* pathfinding with an optimal route drawn on the map - Voice guidance: turn-by-turn directions spoken aloud in Spanish or English (requires Sound Pack) - Mini-map: always visible on the GPS home screen while navigating - Full-screen map: zoomable and pannable world map, click anywhere to set a destination - Nearby POIs: discover nearby locations sorted by distance - City quick-access: jump to any city from a sorted list with distances - Off-route detection: automatic recalculation if you stray from the path - Vehicle awareness: detects if you are driving and adjusts speed estimates and arrival voice lines xPottify (Music Player) A built-in music streaming app that automatically detects all installed True Moozic-compatible cassette and disc mods. Browse by collection, pick a song, and listen while you loot and survive. Music plays through your character's position in the world — other players nearby can hear it and the volume changes in real time based on distance and your volume slider. With earphones connected, music is private. Without earphones, it attracts zombies. If no compatible music mods are installed, xPottify shows a friendly message explaining how to add them. Settings - Connect/disconnect earphones from your inventory. With earphones connected, all phone sounds (music, GPS voice) play privately — zombies cannot hear you. Without earphones, sound plays through the phone speaker and attracts nearby zombies. - Adjust voice guidance volume - Swap batteries (Standard model only) - View phone number, battery level, and phone model info == MULTIPLAYER == Fully works in multiplayer. Phone numbers are synced across the server. Players can exchange numbers and send private text messages from anywhere on the map. The global chat channel connects all active phones. The server tracks all phone numbers and persists global chat history. == LOOT == Phones and spare batteries spawn naturally in the world through the distribution system. Disposable phones are common, Standard phones are uncommon, Solar phones are rare. Spare batteries can be found in electronics stores and offices. == LANGUAGE == Supports English and Spanish. Switch language in Settings — all UI text updates instantly. 📋 Changelog v1.1 — March 3, 2026 Phone Identity & Persistence - Phone registration (number, contacts, dead state) now persists across save/load via player ModData backup - Picking up a different phone shows the activation/login screen correctly (SIM swap logic) - Four clean activation cases: your phone → activate, someone else's → login, unowned + have account → auto-bind, unowned + no account → first-time setup Battery System - Battery level now backs up to player ModData — survives drop/pickup and save/load without resetting to 100% - Context menu shows the real battery value instead of always showing 100 Volume System - Volume setting now persists across ModData loss (backed up to player ModData) - Fixed volume resetting to max when songs auto-advance or are manually changed - Volume changes are now heard by nearby players in real time via the broadcast system Multiplayer Audio (Major Fix) - Fixed double audio bug: nearby players were hearing each song twice (one from PZ engine propagation + one from custom broadcast) - Music playback now uses client-only SoundManager instead of player emitter, eliminating engine-level sound duplication - Remote players hear music exclusively through the custom broadcast system with proper distance-based volume falloff - Fixed song restarting for the listener when the emitter changed volume — remote sound instances are now muted instead of destroyed - Fixed stop/pause not working for nearby listeners — the broadcast now distinguishes pause (mute, keep position) from full stop (destroy) - Fixed low volume (1/10) making music inaudible for nearby players — minimum hearing range of ~8 tiles regardless of volume setting - Volume changes are now heard by nearby players in real time via the broadcast system xPottify Music Player - xPottify now dynamically scans all installed True Moozic-compatible mods (cassettes, discs, CDs, vinyl) - No longer hardcoded to specific genres — works with any music mod that uses GlobalMusic - Shows a helpful message when no compatible music mods are installed ☕ Support the Developer Thank you so much for downloading and playing my mods! Every subscriber, comment, and rating means the world to me. If you enjoy this mod and want to support my work, you can buy me a coffee! Your support helps me keep creating and improving mods for the community. ☕ buymeacoffee.com/XaviChang Every coffee fuels another late-night coding session! ☕🎮 Workshop ID: 3675737813 Mod ID: xPhone

Dead Man's Dossier [B42][MP] Build 42 multiplayer-safe. A collectible objective system: zombies drop torn pages, assemble a dossier, follow coordinates to a hidden stash. Works in multiplayer 42.1.17. Police, military, medical, firefighter, and ranger zombies drop torn document pages. Collect all pages for a tier, assemble a dossier, and follow the coordinates to a hidden supply stash. The loot spawns on the ground at the stash location — gear up and survive. How It Works Kill zombies wearing police, military, medical, firefighter, or ranger outfits They have a chance to drop torn document pages Collect all pages for a tier, then right-click a page to Assemble Dossier A progress bar plays while your character reads and assembles the pages The completed dossier reveals coordinates to a hidden supply stash A colored marker appears on your world map showing the stash location Travel to the stash and right-click the dossier to Verify Stash Location Proximity hints guide you in — color-coded "getting warmer" feedback When you're close enough, loot drops on the ground at the stash tile for you to pick up If your map marker disappears (e.g. after a server restart), Verify Stash Location or View Stash Map will restore it automatically Don't want the mission? Right-click the dossier and choose Abandon Mission to discard it and start fresh Five Tiers Police (2 pages) — Pistols, shotguns, ammo, police clothing, bulletproof vest, holster, walkie-talkie Military (3 pages) — Assault rifles, pistols, magazines, scopes, ammo, camo gear, military backpack, ALICE webbing, bulletproof vest Medical (2 pages) — Antibiotics, bandages, suture needles, painkillers, surgical tools, scrubs Firefighter (2 pages) — Axe, sledgehammer, crowbar, fireman gear, blow torch, bolt cutters, welding mask Ranger (2 pages) — Hunting rifle, shotguns, knife, hatchet, scopes, ranger clothing, compass, rope, trap box Each page has immersive lore text — internal memos, classified reports, incident logs, and field notes that tell the story of Knox County's fall. Where to Find Pages Pages drop from zombies wearing the matching outfit. They also spawn in relevant containers: Police pages in police station lockers, desks, and gun storage Military pages in army hangars, surplus stores, and military storage Medical pages in hospital drug cabinets, clinics, and medical storage Firefighter pages in fire department lockers Ranger pages in ranger outfit containers and tool storage Map Markers When you assemble a dossier, a colored marker is placed on your world map at the stash location. Each tier has a distinct color. Markers persist across saves and can be toggled on/off with a button on the map screen. Sandbox Options Server admins can tune everything under Dossier Mod in Sandbox Options: Page drop chance per tier — High (30%) / Normal (15%) / Low (8%) / Very Low (3%) Page container spawn rate — How often pages appear in world containers (Common / Uncommon / Rare / Very Rare) Stash reward rarity — Multiplier for reward drop chances (Generous 2x / Normal 1x / Scarce 0.5x / Minimal 0.1x) Stash proximity radius — How close you need to be to collect rewards (5-50 tiles, default 15) Use Custom Rewards — Load reward items from a config file instead of the built-in tables (see below) Custom Rewards (Admin Config) Server admins can fully customize what items each stash tier drops: Start the server once — a config file is auto-generated at Zomboid/Lua/DeadMansDossier_Rewards.cfg Edit the file to add, remove, or change items and their drop chances Enable Use Custom Rewards in Sandbox Options Restart the server — custom rewards are now active The config file uses a simple format: [Police] Base.Pistol = 0.40 Base.Shotgun = 0.25 # Base.Sledgehammer = 0.05 (commented out = disabled) [Military] Base.AssaultRifle = 0.05 SomeMod.CustomWeapon = 0.10 (cross-mod items work too) The Reward Rarity sandbox multiplier still applies on top of custom chances. Items from uninstalled mods are silently skipped. If the config file is missing or has errors, the mod falls back to the built-in defaults. Cross-Mod Support Military stash caches can drop X-Virus and Medical stash caches can drop Knox Antidote. Works with or without those mods installed — if the mod isn't active, the item is silently skipped. Translations Item names are now routed through PZ's translation system (thanks to feedback from Shahin·Wolf). Translators can add new languages by copying Translate/EN/ItemName.json to a language folder (e.g. Translate/CH/) and translating the values. Same goes for DeadMansDossier.json (UI + lore) and Sandbox.json (option labels). Submit translations via Workshop comments and they'll be added to the next release. Compatibility Build 42 — works in multiplayer (tested on 42.1.17) Mid-save compatible — can be added to an existing save Roadmap Stash loot currently drops on the ground — planning to add a supply crate container in a future update Feedback and suggestions welcome! If a stash location seems off, please let us know and we'll fix it. Support Found the stash? description: Fine tune loot spawns and respawns by area and time by reducing their chance of spawn Setup Open the configs window by clicking the PhunLewts button in the Admin or Debug window This is a list of all your different configurations. The Default profile is the configuration used if you are not using with PhunZones or if the zone you are in does not specify a configuration. It's the perfect place for your global defaults! Let's make ammo really rare. To do so, I'll edit the default config, click the Categories tab, edit the Ammo category and set it to 90 That makes ALL items in that category reduce their spawn by 90%. Now, let's say I want no ammo spawning in certain places. To do this, I create a new config, inherit from default (which has the 90% reduction for ammo) and change the Ammo value to 100 I can then assign that config to a zone via the PhunZones editor IMPORTANT This mod only reduces loot when the game spawns or respawns items in a container. It cannot reduce loot in containers that are already filled (eg a custom map that ships with loot already in containers). However it will apply when those containers restock. That also means that changes in your config will not affect containers that have already been stocked It cannot force loot to respawn in custom maps that are missing or have broken forage zones. Basically if the game won't restock the container, this mod won't be able to change that There are no longer dependencies required, however it is strongly suggested that you use PhunZones. Without it, only your default config is used Remember, the values reduce loot spawns. 100 = 100% reduction and 0 = no reduction! Configuration Settings More Phun Stuff Coded with love for our awesome PhunZoid community. Check out the GitHub repo for more info. Workshop ID: 3676250472 Mod ID: phunlewt2.1

description: PhunSprinters 2 the sequel to the Academy Award winning PhunSprinters. PhunSprinters is the ultimate sprinter mod for Zomboid. PhunSprinters does not simply add sprinters. It calculates risk and that risk can change depending on where you are, how long you’ve survived, the moon cycle, and the environment. 🧠 How Sprinter Risk Is Calculated Sprinter behaviour is determined by stacking modifiers in this order: Global Base Risk (in your settings) Zone Override (if PhunZones 2 is installed) Hours Discount (Ease-In) Moon Phase Modifier Darkness / Night Rules Light Suppression Final Sprinter Chance & Behaviour 🌑 Modes There are four different modes that determine when sprinters will run 🔦 Light Suppression (Flashlights Matter) When enabled, bright light can force sprinters to walk This creates emergent gameplay: Flashlights become tactical tools Base lighting matters Night travel becomes a risk vs reward decision It brings some of the Phun of mode #4 to the other options (this option doesn't do anything if using Mode 4) ⚠️ Some limits exist to prevent performance issues in dense areas. ⏳Hours Discount (Difficulty Easing) The Hours Discount slowly ramps difficulty over time. Instead of applying full risk immediately, sprinter chance increases gradually. Example: Zone Risk: 50% Hours Discount: 100 Player Hours: 50 ➡️ Effective Risk = 25% Risk increases linearly until the discount hours are reached. This is ideal for fresh servers, new characters, and multiplayer balance. 🌕 Moon Phase Modifiers Moon phases multiply the current risk. Example: Zone Risk: 20% Full Moon Modifier: 200 → will effectively double (200%) the risk to 40% New Moon Modifier: 50 → will effectively half (50%) the risk to 10% Moon modifiers scale risk, they do not replace it. Unless you set it to 0, then it means there is no risk! Key differences to version 1 Support for PhunZones 2 Removed requirements for dependencies (PhunZones and PhunLib are no longer required) Unified the UI and core mods (UI is no longer a separate mod) Drop B41 support (current version of PhunSprinters will continue to work for B41 but this greatly simplifies things) Improve performance Reduce amount of "Why they no sprint" moments More Phun Stuff Coded with love for our awesome PhunZoid community. description: Dynamic Evolution Z Adaptive World & Horde System The world is no longer static. Dynamic Evolution Z introduces a persistent, invisible behavioral system that reshapes zombie activity over time. The longer you survive — and the more aggressively you reshape the map — the more the infection reorganizes itself. No UI. No mutation gimmicks. No arcade bosses. Just systemic pressure. Core Systems Persistent Global Evolution Zombies evolve individually as days pass and player activity increases. Evolution is saved per zombie — some adapt faster, others stagnate. Individual Identity Each zombie develops independently. Different evolution baselines, different growth rates, different outcomes. No synchronized scaling. No artificial difficulty spikes. Leader Archetypes Rare evolved zombies can emerge as Leaders. Leaders: Increase group cohesion Improve persistence of nearby zombies Make dispersal harder Influence horde structure They are not bosses. They are behavioral catalysts. Ambient Wander Layer The world breathes even when you are not fighting. Subtle population drift occurs across chunks over time, preventing long-term stagnation and creating slow territorial pressure. Migration System Large-scale clearing has consequences. Under certain conditions, groups may begin relocating across nearby chunks — especially after heavy player activity. Safe areas do not remain safe forever. Layered Behavior Priority Meta-events, player pursuit, leadership influence and ambient drift follow a clear priority structure. Systems do not conflict or override vanilla behavior. Leader Archetypes Leaders are not all the same. When a zombie reaches advanced evolution, it may develop a distinct behavioral archetype. These archetypes do not grant artificial health or damage bonuses. They alter group behavior. HIVE Strong group cohesion Keeps nearby zombies tightly clustered Maintains formation longer than normal Harder to split apart HUNTER Improved tracking persistence Better memory of last known player position Groups remain engaged longer during pursuit Less likely to abandon a chase FRENZY Higher reaction to noise events Increased tendency to investigate distant sounds May redirect nearby zombies toward disturbances SHADOW Enhanced path persistence More likely to follow remembered routes Difficult to shake off once detected SPLIT Weaker cohesion Encourages group fragmentation Spreads pressure across multiple directions Creates unpredictable dispersal patterns STALKER Selects and follows a single prey Uses memory instead of direct pursuit Relentless but not fast — it never truly loses you Builds long-term tension and presence HOWLER Acts as a living signal node Calls and gathers nearby zombies Pushes hordes toward detected players Creates escalating pressure in waves Leaders are rare. Not every group has one. Not every evolved zombie becomes one. You may never know which type you are facing — until the horde behaves differently. Debug Commands -- List of commands: DynamicZ.DebugSetEvo(0.5) DynamicZ.DebugAddKills(500) DynamicZ.DebugSetStage(3) DynamicZ.DebugMakeLeader() DynamicZ.DebugForcePulse() DynamicZ.DebugCommand("/dz_set_evo 0.9") DynamicZ.DebugMakeLeader("SPLIT") DynamicZ.DebugInspect() DynamicZ.DebugStatus() DynamicZ.DebugUntrack() DynamicZ.DebugReset() DynamicZ.DebugHelp() DynamicZ.DebugCommand("/dz_inspect") -- Available commands on server: /dz_set_evo <0..1> /dz_add_kills <amount> /dz_set_stage <0..3> /dz_make_leader [HIVE|HUNTER|FRENZY|SHADOW|SPLIT] /dz_force_pulse /dz_reset /dz_inspect /dz_status /dz_untrack /dz_debug on /dz_debug off Sandbox Options Fully modular system: Enable Evolution Layer Enable Leader System Enable Migration Layer Enable Ambient Wander Layer Play it subtle — or turn the world hostile. Design Philosophy Dynamic Evolution Z does not add mutations. It adds adaptation. The infection does not become stronger through raw stat boosts. It becomes more organized, more persistent, and less predictable. You are not fighting stronger zombies. You are fighting a system that reacts. Performance & Multiplayer Build 42 Compatible Multiplayer Safe Server-side logic Optimized update throttling No global constant map scanning Layer conflict prevention system It is not compatible with Wandering mod, Starving mod, Thump with Friends. Designed to scale without heavy FPS impact when properly configured. Official compatibility layer for They Fear The Light. Intended Experience Early Game: Near-vanilla behavior. Mid Game: Subtle pressure and increasing cohesion. Late Game: Organized movement, territorial shifts, adaptive persistence. Clearing a town is no longer a permanent solution. If permission is granted, proper credit must be given both within the mod files and wherever the mod is published. If no permission is received, the mod must be treated as 'On Lockdown'. Servers are allowed to include this mod in their modpacks and apply internal changes, as long as proper credit is given to the original creator. Support the Mod Support the Project If you enjoy this mod and want to support future updates and new systems: Your support helps expand the project and keep development active. Every contribution makes a difference. Thank you for your support! ❤️ A like or favorite helps a LOT! Workshop ID: 3676814360 Mod ID: DynamicEvolutionZ

description: Multiplayer compatible. Safe to add to existing saves. Armor Makes Sense replaces vanilla armor discomfort with realistic physical costs: endurance drain, heat buildup, breathing restriction, muscle strain, and worse sleep recovery. No stress penalties. Just physics. Why This Exists I spent days grinding blacksmithing to craft full plate armor. When I finally equipped it, the game punished me with discomfort and stress. My character was miserable. That felt wrong. Armor should cost stamina, mobility, heat, and fatigue, not sanity. So I replaced the system. What This Mod Does Armor Makes Sense removes vanilla's psychological discomfort and replaces it with physical costs. Protective gear now drains endurance, strains muscles, restricts breathing, traps heat, and slows recovery through existing vanilla systems. Despite the name, this is not just an armor tweak. To make the system behave consistently, I had to treat clothing as a whole ecosystem. The name stuck. Features Discomfort removed Vanilla's discomfort modifier is set to zero on all wearable items. Armor no longer causes stress. Speed rebalance Run speed and combat speed modifiers are reassigned by body region. Leg armor affects running. Arm and shoulder armor affect combat speed. Light pads stay neutral. Endurance drain Heavier armor increases endurance usage during movement and combat. Walking is almost free. Sprinting in full plate is not. Thermal pressure Armor traps heat. In hot weather you overheat faster. In cold weather, insulating armor helps. Breathing restriction Gas masks and respirators reduce airflow. The penalty scales with exertion: negligible at rest, noticeable under heavy effort. Muscle strain Heavy arm and shoulder protection adds fatigue per swing. A chest plate does not slow your swing, but gauntlets and shoulder pads do. Better-crafted armor restricts less than crude scrap. Sleep recovery Sleeping in rigid armor slows fatigue recovery. It is an emergency choice, not a default. Layering overhaul Vanilla limits some combinations in ways that do not make much sense. This mod re-slots 79 items across 8 custom body locations so layering works more naturally. In-Game UI Tooltips show burden level and breathing restriction Burden tab breaks down total loadout cost Help button explains each mechanic in plain language Compatibility Game version: Build 42.14.1+ Other armor mods: should generally work through automatic item classification based on defense stats, weight, and item properties More in the Makes Sense series Translations Russian Spanish Source: GitHub Workshop ID: 3677430162 Mod ID: ArmorMakesSense

Core Features Dynamic atmospheric gas hazards Wind-driven fallout events Outdoor contamination rendering system Gas masks, filters, and SCBA support Full sandbox configuration Multiplayer-safe admin tools Translations: English, German, Russian, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish Hazard Types Light Gas (Industrial vapours, household leaks) Becomes stronger at higher elevations Can slowly fill enclosed spaces Encourages vertical awareness Heavy Gas (Chlorine-like industrial contamination) Settles in low terrain and underground areas Creates dangerous pockets in basements and valleys More concentrated closer to the ground Chemical Fallout Large-scale drifting contamination events Moves with the wind Reported through the Emergency Broadcast System Persists temporarily before dispersing NEW: Can infect crops with mildew and damage them (default disabled) The wind direction matters. Listen carefully. Artillery Gas Events Temporary artillery strikes can create dangerous contamination zones for up to 8 hours. Toxic Gas — causes direct toxic exposure damage Stun Gas — rapidly drains endurance Burning Gas — causes burns and can ignite zombies Radius and duration fully configurable Exposure & Survival Gas exposure builds over time Unprotected survivors cough and deteriorate Animals can die from prolonged exposure Roofed buildings protect crops and livestock from fallout Stay too long inside contaminated areas, and the effects escalate. Protective Equipment Supports all vanilla gas masks and respirators Gas masks degrade through use Filters become less effective as they wear down SCBA units provide full protection while oxygen lasts Bandanas and dust masks provide minimal emergency protection Sandbox & Server Configuration Everything can be configured through sandbox settings: Event frequency and duration Gas strength and spread Fallout drift speed Mask durability loss Animal damage scaling Spawn scaling over time And more Admin Tools & Multiplayer Spawn Light Gas, Heavy Gas, and Fallout zones Create artillery contamination events Create permanent hazard zones Manual fallout triggers Server-protected admin commands Compatibility Build 42 compatible Singleplayer supported Multiplayer supported Uses vanilla gas masks and SCBA equipment FAQ Question: Can I add or remove the mod mid-save? Answer: Yes. You can safely add or remove the mod during an existing save without affecting savegame stability, based on all my testing. All zone data is stored inside your ModData. If you remove the mod, the existing zones will remain in your save, but they will no longer function because the code handling them is no longer running. I still strongly recommend deleting all existing zones before uninstalling the mod. --- Question: How do hazards spawn in Singleplayer? Answer: Hazards are spawned by the Event Manager. It automatically searches for eligible areas around the player and spawns either a Light Gas Zone, a Heavy Gas Zone, or a Fallout Zone. Light and Heavy Gas Zones can repeatedly affect the same building if you live outside a city. Fallout Zones are different. Every now and then, the Event Manager creates a massive cloud with a radius of roughly 400–500 tiles. It slowly drifts across the map following the current wind direction. It might pass you by... or it might head straight for your base. --- Question: How does it work on Multiplayer? Answer: Check the screenshots for the Toxic Sky Zone Editor. The Event Manager also works in Multiplayer, but I generally do not recommend using it on busy servers. If hazards are generated simultaneously for 50+ players, it can consume a noticeable amount of server resources. For Multiplayer, manually placed hazard zones are the recommended solution. --- Question: How compatible is the mod? Answer: Compatibility was one of the main design goals. The mod only modifies gas mask filters to roughly match the vanilla filter depletion rate. I also added safeguards to prevent players from being affected by both Hazard Toxicity and Corpse Sickness at the same time. The only mods that may interfere with Toxic Sky are those that manipulate the global Water & Power systems. They can prevent the Event Manager from starting. If that happens, simply disable the "Water and Power" option in the Mod Options menu. The Event Manager will then start immediately, ignoring that condition. --- Question: I suddenly died after staying too long inside a gas zone. Answer: This is intentional. Hazard exposure accumulates using the game's Food Poisoning system. While you can partially counteract it with food that reduces food poisoning, prolonged exposure will eventually become lethal. If you prefer the old behavior, you can enable Legacy Mode, which applies direct health damage instead of toxicity. --- Question: My server uses 12 hours of real time for one in-game day. How does that affect the mod? Answer: It doesn't anymore. The mod now includes a time conversion helper that automatically scales all calculations to the default timing the mod was designed for. It has been tested with server day lengths ranging from 30 minutes to 12 real-world hours. I expect it to work with 24 real-world hours per in-game day as well. However, hazard damage and toxicity updates will occur much less frequently, resulting in slower progression and larger jumps in health loss or toxicity whenever they update. Permissions Free to use in servers, modpacks, and collections Personal edits and server modifications are allowed Please credit Toxic Sky when publishing derivative versions Reuploads of the mod itself without modification are discouraged. Thank you — and good luck surviving under a Toxic Sky. Workshop ID: 3677858792 Mod ID: ToxicSky

description: Companion mod for Solar Floodlight by alexander.ronin13. Extends solar floodlights with car batteries, motion sensors, and lightbulb slots. Never modifies Solar Floodlight files. This is a companion add-on only — it does not include, modify, or redistribute any Solar Floodlight code. Solar Floodlight on Steam Workshop Features Extended Batteries — Car batteries, lighter batteries, and ISA mod batteries work in floodlights. Drain scales with capacity (car batteries last multiple nights). Condition-based degradation. Larger batteries boost light radius (+2 to +6 tiles). Condition preserved on removal. Motion Sensor — Install a motion sensor for proximity-activated lighting. Configurable detection radius, detection targets (players/zombies/both), and optional passive drain. Requires Electrical skill (configurable). Lightbulb Slot (off by default) — When enabled, floodlights require a lightbulb to operate. Accepts any vanilla lightbulb. Bulbs degrade over time and eventually burn out. Condition preserved on removal. Operating Modes — ON (always on), OFF (always off), AUTO (night only). All parameters fully configurable via sandbox options. Custom battery and bulb types can be added without a mod update. Full multiplayer/dedicated server support. Quick Reference — Nights to Empty (8h nights, 100% condition) - CarBattery1 (50 Ah): ~3.4 nights — sustainable ~4 PZ months - CarBattery3 (75 Ah): ~4.2 nights — sustainable ~5.4 PZ months - CarBattery2 (100 Ah): ~4.8 nights — sustainable ~6.4 PZ months - DeepCycleBattery (200 Ah): ~6.8 nights — sustainable ~9.5 PZ months - SuperBattery (400 Ah): ~9.7 nights — sustainable ~13.5 PZ months Setup 1. Subscribe to this mod and Solar Floodlight 2. Add both to your server's mod list (this mod loads AFTER Solar Floodlight) 3. That's it — works automatically Server Config WorkshopItems=3680577450;3683488496 Mods=SolarFloodlight;SLBatteryPack Sandbox Options Battery: CondLossPerNight (1.5), CondLossOnZero (3.0), ConditionMin (0), EnableRadiusBonus (on), ReferenceAh (2.5), BatteryTypes (registry string) Sensor: SensorSkillLevel (4), SensorRadius (15), SensorPassiveDrain (0) Bulbs: EnableBulbs (off), BulbLifespanMult (1.0), BulbTypes (extra types string) See the README in the mod folder for detailed descriptions, scaling formulas, tuning guides, and technical documentation. ISA Battery Support ISA batteries (WiredCarBattery, DeepCycleBattery, DIYBattery, SuperBattery) are supported out of the box. Capacity is read from ISA's ModData when available. Mid-Save Safety Safe to add or remove mid-save. All data is stored in Solar Floodlight's own ModData and is simply ignored without this mod. Workshop ID: 3683488496 Mod ID: SLBatteryPack
