description: Lets you see upstairs in a normal way. Compatible game versions: 41.78 and above; 42.13 and above Installation Subscribe and make sure you have ZombieBuddy installed properly. Q/A Why ZombieBuddy is required? This is a Java mod and ZombieBuddy is a Java mod loader. What this mod does is not achievable in a standard mod, and while it is possible to make a Java mod by replacing the game's class files, such mods tend to break even on minor game updates. The mod loader solves this problem by injecting code at runtime. Can I verify what the mod does and build it myself? Yes, the source code and build instructions are on GitHub. See below. Multiplayer support? Yes. ZombieBuddy must be installed manually before you join a server. Is it safe to add to or remove from an existing save? Yes. Does it work on my game version? Both Build 41 and Build 42 are supported. Build 41 requires version 41.78 or later, and Build 42 requires version 42.13 or later. It doesn't work on my game version that is supported! This is most likely because ZombieBuddy is not installed correctly/not working. Installation requires manual steps, please follow its instructions carefully. Another reason might be that you didn't enable the mod for your save. If that's not the case for you, please report it. Mod does work!!! Enjoy! description: [NO MULTIPLAYER YET] The version 1.6 and any update after this version offers a different experience from the 1.5 since the virus have been nerfed to oblivion. If you want to try the unforgiving legacy experience of this mod, try GamerKreep's patch for this mod -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- If you’ve ever unleashed the Necroa Virus in Plague Inc. and watched the world fall into chaos… now it’s time to survive it. This mod brings the terrifying essence of the Necroa Virus into Project Zomboid, transforming the Knox Event into something far more hardcore. The zombies are no longer static — they evolve, becoming more aggressive, smarter (and sometimes even special) over time. These changes are fully modeled in-game, meaning the differences aren’t just in their stats, but also in their appearance and behavior. Inspired by the iconic plague from Plague Inc., this version introduces expanded virus mechanics and increasingly aggressive undead systems designed to amplify tension, unpredictability, and dread. Expect brutal survivability, harsher consequences for your mistakes, and the constant feeling that the infection is always one step ahead of you. [Be Advised] This mod is not beginner-friendly by any means. While playing, you might even feel a bit of 2020 nostalgia — you won’t be able to touch everything bare-handed without consequences. Masks matters. The airborne infection is fully modeled here, and you are not a special survivor immune to the airborne strain of the virus (you can disable this mechanic by turning the Air Infection option off in the settings). Although the zombies may not seem too difficult at the beginning of the game, they will become a serious threat by mid to late game. They will no longer be a simple obstacle — they will be a constant danger. Barricade your doors and windows, because it truly makes a difference in this mod. [Considerations] This mod uses code from inactive/dead mods such as Sense of Smell (Sense of Smell's code was replaced by my own version on update 1.6) and Susceptible. I was unable to contact the original creators to request permission. If you are the owner of one of those mods and do not want your code used here, please contact me so I can update this mod and recreate those mechanics from scratch. My apologies in advance. Special thanks to Phil J Herman, Spyjack, Notloc, Mr Sunshine, SimKDT — and the biggest of them all, Ryuku. You’re the GOAT. This mod took me 8 months to create, and I built it with passion and care. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Roadmap (Will only be added once stable is out) -Restore story-related content that was broken by updates (the same content featured at the beginning of the first Pr1vateLime episode of this mod) -Add new unique animations for zombies -Add voice sounds for zombie laments -Implement increase on procedurally generated survival houses -Restore zombies eating bodies (content that was removed when the mod was taken down) -Add zombies breaking small fences -Add spitter-type zombies -Add acid zombies -Expand story-related content -Add additional icon features that are not yet implemented -Develop a more complex zombie migration system -Translation for Korean, Janapese, Chinese, Russian and Spanish (More features to be added later)

Create custom shops with their own themes, sprites, loot pools, and pricing Design progression systems: gate purchases behind skills, traits, professions, or playtime Build server-wide economies with skill trainers, vehicle dealerships, starter hubs, and late-game vendors Set up seasonal or event shops that rotate stock on a schedule Control spawn rates, placement, and conversion of vanilla machines per shop type Tune every economic lever: earn rates, caps, pricing, restock timers, and more via sandbox settings Currency & Economy PhunMart ships with PhunWallet, a built-in dual-currency system: Change: found as loot in the world. Think of it as cash. Tokens: earned by playing: surviving, killing zombies, completing milestones. Bound to the player. Both pools have configurable caps, earn rates, and death-recovery settings. All customisations are saved to your file system. They survive restarts, wipes, and version updates. Does it work in Single Player? Yes. Designed for multiplayer servers but fully functional in SP. Can I add into existing game? Yes Where can I see it in action? SP, your own server, or come play on ours. More Phun Stuff Coded with love for the awesome PhunZoid community. description: Multiplayer compatible. Safe to add to existing saves. Nutrition Makes Sense Nutrition Makes Sense rebuilds how hunger, food, and weight work so maintaining yourself feels more intuitive in normal play. In vanilla, staying on top of weight usually means monitoring calories and checking body weight. NMS was made to reduce that kind of number-watching by giving the player earlier, more useful feedback through ordinary gameplay. Food values have also been adjusted across around 600 vanilla items to have more realistic nutritional values. Weight changes are also less wobbly and more grounded in sustained eating patterns. The goal is not to make nutrition harsher. It is to make it more readable, more responsive, and easier to manage without turning it into a numbers chore. What changes Hunger reflects energy state If you're not eating enough, hunger starts to show it earlier, instead of leaving weight change as the main thing to monitor. Food values are rebuilt Satiety, calories, and macros are authored per item based on the actual food. You do not need to lean on a few outlier foods just to maintain yourself. Weight follows sustained patterns Missing one meal will not meaningfully change your weight. Repeated overeating or undereating will. Deprivation takes sustained neglect Ordinary inconsistency will not wreck you. Serious deprivation only sets in if you stay underfed for too long, at which point stamina recovery slows, fatigue rises, and melee damage starts to fall. Protein matters too Protein is tracked across multiple days. Going too long without decent protein intake slows healing. What you see Reworked food tooltips with simple readouts for satiety, energy density, and dominant macro. A malnourished moodle when nutritional deprivation starts kicking in. Health panel entries showing active penalties from deprivation or protein deficiency, and whether things are getting better or worse. Weight trend with exact number shown on the character screen. More in the Makes Sense series Source: GitHub Workshop ID: 3690404044 Mod ID: NutritionMakesSense

DESCRIPTION Tougher Vehicles is a simple, highly customizable utility mod that lets you adjust how much damage your vehicle takes. Say goodbye to your car turning into paper after hitting a few zombies! Everything is designed to be "plug-and-play" without breaking core mechanics or causing conflicts with other custom vehicle mods. KEY FEATURES - Customizable Durability: Tweak the durability multiplier for physical parts (engine, hood, doors, windows) from 2x stronger up to completely unbreakable via Sandbox Options. - Tire Protection: Set your tires to be indestructible and always fully inflated. - Battery Saver: Significantly slow down the car's battery drain rate when using the radio, heater, or headlights. - 100% Safe: The battery drain setting ONLY applies to actual Car Batteries attached to the vehicle. It does NOT affect normal small batteries used for flashlights or portable electronics. SANDBOX OPTIONS You have full control over the mod's behavior through the Sandbox menu. The available dropdown options are: 1. Global Durability Multiplier: 1x (Vanilla / Normal) | 2x Stronger | 3x Stronger | 5x Stronger | 10x Stronger | Unbreakable (Immortal) 2. Tire Protection: Vanilla (Can take damage & lose pressure) | Indestructible & Always Inflated 3. Battery Drain Rate: Vanilla (Normal drain) | 2x Slower | 5x Slower | 10x Slower FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ) Q: Why do my car windows still break when surrounded by a horde of zombies? A: The durability multiplier applies to every single part of the car, including the windows. However, windows in Zomboid naturally have very low base health (often just 10-20 points). Even if the mod makes them 5x or 10x tougher, the small amount of damage that gets through from constant zombie banging will eventually shatter them. They are much stronger now, but they are not invincible (unless you pick the "Unbreakable" option). Q: Why does my car still take damage when crashing into trees or buildings? A: High-speed impacts against static objects deal massive amounts of damage all at once. The mod reduces this damage significantly based on your chosen multiplier, but it doesn't completely erase it. The 2x, 5x, and 10x options make your car much tougher, but it still behaves like a realistic car. Technical Details If my mods make your run a little less painful, please consider leaving a 👍 Like and ⭐ Favorite! Got any feedback or bug reports? Feel free to drop them in the comments. Stay safe out there! If you enjoy this mod and want to support my work, feel free to buy me a coffee! Workshop ID: 3691268775 Mod ID: TougherVehicles

description: Slide Bite You picked up a semi-auto pistol for the first time, what could go wrong? ───────────────────────────────────────── In vanilla Project Zomboid, a character who has never touched a gun in their life handles a semi-automatic pistol with perfect form every time. Slide Bite fixes that. Semi-automatic pistols have a reciprocating slide that travels rearward over the grip on every shot. An inexperienced shooter who holds the gun too high gets the web of their hand caught by that slide. The result is a cut. It bleeds. It can get infected. It hurts. ───────────────────────────────────────── What Happens When It Triggers A laceration is applied to your right hand — treated like any other cut in the game. Clean it, bandage it, watch it for infection. Ignore it and it compounds. Your character says something. They noticed. ───────────────────────────────────────── Risk by Skill Level Aiming 0 — 10% chance per shot Aiming 1 — 5% chance per shot Aiming 2 — 2% chance per shot Aiming 3+ — 0%. Muscle memory. You've got it now. ───────────────────────────────────────── How to Stop It Pick the right profession — Police and Veterans start knowing how to hold semi-auto pistols correctly. Level up — reach Aiming 3 and the risk disappears entirely Wear gloves — any gloves in the hand slot protect you fully, including modded ones Read the manual — find the Pistol Technique Manual in gun stores, police stations, and army surplus to permanently learn proper grip at any skill level Learn the hard way — get slide bitten enough times and your character figures it out on their own ───────────────────────────────────────── Revolvers Are Now a Real Choice Revolvers have no slide. There is nothing to bite you. A complete beginner can pick up a revolver on day one and fire it without consequence. This makes early gun selection meaningful. The revolver is forgiving — low capacity, slow to reload, but safe to use while your skills are zero. The semi-automatic is more capable, but it will punish you for holding it wrong until you learn. Choose based on your confidence, not just your loot. ───────────────────────────────────────── Works With Modded Weapons and Gloves Any semi-automatic pistol with a detachable magazine is automatically eligible. Any item in the hand clothing slot automatically protects. No patches needed for weapon or clothing packs. ───────────────────────────────────────── Multiplayer Ready All wound application and stat tracking run server-side. Works on hosted and dedicated servers without configuration. ───────────────────────────────────────── Mod ID: SlideBite Build: 42.16 Version: 1.1 Workshop ID: 3693775109 Mod ID: SlideBite

description: Half the Workshop independently hooks ISToolTipInv.render to add content to item tooltips. Every one of them saves the original function, replaces it with their own, crosses its fingers, and ships. Load two together and it's a coin flip whose content shows up. TooltipLib fixes this. One managed hook per surface. Mods register as providers instead of fighting over who owns the render function. Priority ordering, error isolation, automatic column alignment, two-tier caching. Install it and every tooltip mod works together — aligned, organized, conflict-free. For Players Install it. If a mod lists TooltipLib as a dependency, install TooltipLib. No configuration. No load order fiddling. No compatibility patches. Toggle individual providers on or off, rebind the detail key (default: Shift). Safe to add mid-save. Safe to remove mid-save. No persistent state. Writes nothing to your save file. Item — Inventory tooltips. The one everyone fights over. Not anymore. Item Slot — Crafting panel slots. Item providers auto-apply here. World Object — Generators, fridges, rain collectors, containers — anything in the world. Skill — Character skill bars. Rich text. Vehicle — Mechanic overlay part tooltips. Rich text. Recipe — Build 42 crafting recipe side panel. All six share the same context method interface. Write a provider once, point it at any surface. One call. No hooking, no metatable juggling, no layout lifecycle. require "TooltipLib/Core" TooltipLib.registerProvider({ id = "MyMod_WeaponStats", target = "item", enabled = TooltipLib.Filters.weapon, cacheable = true, description = "Weapon damage stats", callback = function(ctx) ctx:addKeyValue("Damage:", "+15%", nil, TooltipLib.Colors.GREEN) ctx:addProgress("Mastery:", 0.75, nil, TooltipLib.Colors.GOLD) end, }) The framework handles the hook, the layout, the error handling, and the caching. Your callback adds content. Error isolation. Every callback runs inside pcall. Provider A fails, providers B through Z keep rendering. Circuit breaker benches repeat offenders after 10 consecutive errors. Cleanup phase runs unconditionally — if your preTooltip modified item state and your callback divided by zero, cleanup still fires. Filtering. 14 item filters, 3 world object filters, factory functions for custom cases, combinators (allOf, anyOf, negate). Every filter is pcall-hardened. Context methods. Ten common methods for all surfaces: addLabel addKeyValue addProgress addInteger addFloat addPercentage addSpacer addHeader addDivider addText Layout surfaces (item, itemSlot, object) add texture rendering. Rich text surfaces (skill, vehicle) add line-level formatting. 5-phase lifecycle. preTooltip → callback → textures → postRender → cleanup. In order. Multiplayer Item, skill, vehicle, and recipe surfaces are fully client-side. Zero server traffic. World objects use a request-response pipeline on dedicated servers. Client sends one request per object. Server reads whitelisted methods only — getters and boolean checks. No mutations, no arbitrary invocation. Responses cached client-side. Sandbox option EnableMPSync lets admins disable the pipeline. Singleplayer and listen servers read directly. No network overhead. Compatibility Works alongside mods that hook ISToolTipInv.render directly — deferred mode detects the foreign hook and renders provider content below it. Works with Inventory Tetris, Equipment UI, and other UI-replacing mods. Multiple mods can bundle TooltipLib — version guard ensures newest copy loads, older ones skip silently. Mods Using TooltipLib Sauce Tooltips — 20 providers across all 6 surfaces. Generators, food freshness, farm plants, containers, fridges, stoves, lamps, vehicles, crafting. VorpallySauced — Weapon progression tooltips. Affixes, mastery, kill tracking. Requirements Build 42.13.1+ Safe to add or remove mid-save No persistent state, no save writes Bug reports: TooltipLib Version: Game Version: Mode: [SP / MP Host / Dedicated Server] What happened: Other tooltip mods installed: Workshop ID: 3694097672 Mod ID: TooltipLib Workshop ID: 3694097672 Mod ID: TooltipLib

description: FIRST IN MOD LOAD ORDER Compatibility Notice for Inventory Overhaul Mods Most of this mod will work with other mods as long as Better Pause is loaded early in your mod load order. However, complete inventory overhauls can overwrite vanilla inventory files and may bring the pause restriction back into the inventory context menus. Clean UI Compatibility - Build 42.19+ Clean UI is supported in Build 42.19+ when the Better Pause Clean UI compatibility file is loaded after Clean UI. Recommended load order: 1. TwisTonFire - Better Pause 2. Clean UI 3. Better Pause Clean UI Compatibility File This allows the inventory right-click menus to work while paused, even when Clean UI replaces the inventory menu files. If another mod fully overwrites the inventory system after the compatibility file, that mod may still reintroduce the pause restriction. TwisTonFire - Better Pause This mod removes the pause-related restrictions that Project Zomboid normally enforces. In vanilla, a number of actions are explicitly blocked while Active Pause is enabled. In many cases, the player could otherwise simply queue actions, plan the next step, and continue playing when ready. This mod removes all pause restrictions currently known to me, allowing you to queue actions even while Active Pause is enabled. It also includes an optional Mod Option that can automatically pause the game right after you enter your world. This option is disabled by default and works in Singleplayer only. Important Load Order Information This mod must be placed at the very top of your mod load order, before all other mods. The reason is simple: This mod uses full vanilla file overrides. Those files must load first in order to cleanly replace the original game files. If another mod loads before this one, its changes may not work properly or may not appear in-game at all. Why I made my own version There are already similar mods on the Steam Workshop. However, I do not want to depend on whether another mod is updated or abandoned. Because of that, I created and maintain my own version, so I can make sure it continues to work the way I want. Why this mod can be updated quickly Whenever Project Zomboid receives an update, I only need to run a script on my own PC. That script automatically takes the new vanilla files and removes the pause restrictions for me. This makes it easy for me to update the mod as quickly as possible after a game update, without manually editing every file by hand again. Why full file overrides are necessary Unfortunately, complete file overrides are the only sensible way to remove these restrictions. In most cases, the pause checks are placed very high up inside very long functions. Because of that, they cannot be cleanly removed with lightweight hooks or small compatibility patches. My goal with this mod My goal is to keep this mod updated as quickly as possible whenever the game changes, so the functionality remains available. I also make sure that each version of this mod only patches the exact Project Zomboid version it is intended for. Summary Removes all pause restrictions currently known to me Lets you queue actions while Active Pause is enabled Optional automatic pause after entering your world Auto-pause option is disabled by default Singleplayer-only auto-pause option Must be placed at the very top of the mod load order Uses full vanilla file overrides Designed for fast maintenance after game updates Version-specific patching for the intended Project Zomboid version Is this mod better than X? I cannot say whether this mod is better than another one. What I can say is that this mod is very clear about how it is meant to be used: It must be loaded before all other mods. Nothing breaks when the game updates. The patches only apply to the specific game version this mod was made for. Its translation files also clearly warn that it must be placed at the very top of the load order. 12 current translations of the in-game mod description. Another important difference is how this mod is maintained. It does not simply comment out these restrictions — it removes them entirely. Compatibility FIRST IN MOD LOAD ORDER Your support helps me keep going — thank you very much in advance! Workshop ID: 3696291148 Mod ID: twistbetterpause Mod ID: twistbetterpause_cleanui_compat

description: Meat Expansion (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ*:･ﾟ✧ By Yumi Hi! This is my very first mod. (´｡• ᵕ •｡`) I’m Yumi, a proud meat lover, and I always felt like the game was seriously lacking when it came to animal drops. You’d go through all the effort of hunting or raising animals, and the amount of meat you got just didn’t feel right. So I decided to fix it. (ง •̀_•́)ง When I first posted this mod in its rough early form, it was very much a learning project. It worked, but it was simple, messy in some places, and I still had a lot to learn. Now this mod has received a complete new update with tons of new meats, proper 3D world models, improved cooking behavior, burnt food variations, and better overall meat variety. It took me a lot of time to learn how to work with Blender, 3D models, textures, UVs, scaling, and getting everything to show properly in-game. I broke things, fixed things, broke them again, and somehow survived the meat dimension. (｡•́︿•̀｡) But I am honestly really glad it finally worked out. This mod was inspired by Vanilla Foods Expansion, specifically how pigs drop different kinds of meat. I thought that idea was really cool, and it made me want to try something similar, but on a much more extreme and rewarding level. So I made my own version. This is still my first mod, so please go easy on me. I’m still learning, but I put a lot of time and effort into this. (｡•́︿•̀｡) What This Mod Does (っ◔◡◔)っ This mod reworks and expands animal butchering drops to make hunting feel more rewarding and immersive. Instead of getting small, limited amounts of meat, animals now provide larger and more satisfying yields, along with additional food items depending on the animal. Lard Drop Values (づ｡◕‿‿◕｡)づ Cows → 12 Lard Pigs → 6 Lard Deer → 5 Lard Sheep → 3 Lard Lard is fully integrated into the butchering system and scales based on animal size for balance and realism. (｡•̀ᴗ-)✧ Vanilla Foods Expansion Notice (´｡• ᵕ •｡`) You do not need Vanilla Foods Expansion to use this mod anymore. Meat Expansion now has its own expanded meat drops per animal, so Vanilla Foods Expansion is no longer required. You can use Meat Expansion by itself and still get the full meat expansion experience. If you still want to use Vanilla Foods Expansion alongside this mod, that is totally up to you. Just please understand that both mods add their own animal meat drops. That means if you use both together, you may get a lot more meat than intended, because Vanilla Foods Expansion can drop its meats while Meat Expansion also drops mine. So if your butchered animals suddenly explode into a grocery store worth of meat, that is probably why. (╥﹏╥) If there is another type of meat you would like me to add in the future, feel free to let me know. I may add more later when I have the time and energy. Compatibility (ง •̀_•́)ง Compatible with Build 42.19 Works with most mods Mods that edit animal loot tables may conflict Vanilla Foods Expansion is not required Using Vanilla Foods Expansion with this mod may cause very large meat drops Notes (´• ω •`)ﾉ Please let me know if you run into glitches, missing models, weird textures, cooking issues, compatibility problems, or anything else strange. I’ll look into it as soon as I can. Also, quick heads up: I am a mother of a two-year-old, and I also have a full-time job. I usually play Project Zomboid once I get home, my family is taken care of, and my daughter is asleep. So please bear with me if something is not fixed immediately. I promise I try to get things done as soon as I can when I have the time. Final Thoughts (≧◡≦) This was a huge learning experience for me, and I’m really proud of how it turned out. This update especially took a lot out of me, but I’m happy I pushed through it. Learning Blender, fixing 3D models, making textures work, adding burnt food, and getting everything working was not easy, but seeing everything finally come together made it worth it. If you enjoy it, liking the mod means everything to me. <3 Thanks for checking it out. — Yumi ^v^ Workshop ID: 3700009701 Mod ID: MeatExpansion2.0

Adaptive Wear System A dynamic clothing and equipment degradation system designed to bring realism and long-term survival consequences into your gameplay. This mod introduces a fully immersive wear system where your gear reflects how you play, how you survive, and how much you neglect it. Core Features Dynamic durability system for clothing and backpacks Visual and mechanical degradation tied to real gameplay actions Progressive damage instead of instant condition loss Fully compatible with singleplayer and multiplayer How It Works Your equipment no longer degrades randomly. Instead, it reacts to your behavior: Blood accumulation increases wear over time Repeated washing weakens fabric durability Overused items become fragile and unreliable Environmental interactions affect your gear condition Every action has consequences. Survival is no longer just about staying alive, but maintaining what keeps you alive. New Mechanics Blood Wear System Heavy blood levels gradually damage clothing and backpacks. Washing Degradation Cleaning your clothes repeatedly will slowly reduce their structural integrity. Hole Creation System Items with high wear have a chance to develop holes, reducing protection and effectiveness. Environmental Damage Walking through dense vegetation (trees, bushes) can damage clothing and create tears. Backpack Degradation Backpacks are no longer immune — they wear down just like clothing. Design Philosophy This mod is not about punishing the player. It is about creating meaningful consequences over time. Neglect your gear, and it will fail you when you need it most. Take care of it, and it will last. Why Use This Mod Adds depth to survival gameplay Makes looting and repairing gear more meaningful Encourages strategic decision-making Enhances immersion without breaking vanilla balance Compatibility Works in both Singleplayer and Multiplayer Designed to integrate naturally with vanilla mechanics Safe to add to existing saves It is not compatible with mods that add dirt to the character or clothing/backpack. It is not compatible with mods that clean clothes with rain. description: Advanced Trapping Overhaul (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ*:･ﾟ✧ This is the fourth mod I’ve created and uploaded recently, and out of all of them, this is the one I’m most proud of. This mod was heavily inspired by Trap Everything by RiversideHibbard. It’s an amazing concept, but it hasn’t been updated in quite some time. I completely understand that people have lives and can’t always maintain their mods, so instead of continuing to ask for updates, I decided to take on the challenge myself and build something similar from the ground up. (ง •̀_•́)ง This mod took a lot of time, patience, and trial and error, but I finally got it working properly for Build 42.18. One of the biggest changes compared to older trapping systems is that animals are now caught alive instead of dead. This allows you to actually bring animals back to your base or keep them nearby without needing to travel long distances to farms or specific locations. You can catch both male and female animals, though there are some limitations. Due to how the code behaves, the only baby animals currently supported are baby cows / cow calves. Adult cows presented some technical issues, so baby cows became the stable middle ground for now. All other animals can be caught normally without restriction. Another major difference from the original concept is that traps are no longer limited by time or location. You can catch animals anywhere and at any time of day. There’s no need to place traps in specific zones or wait for certain hours — just set them up and let them work. (｡•̀ᴗ-)✧ The mod has also been updated so traps can work even when the player is nearby, making trapping much smoother and more flexible around your base. Nepenthe’s Nearby Traps is no longer required. That functionality has now been integrated directly into Advanced Trapping Overhaul. This means traps can still catch animals while you are near them, without needing a separate compatibility or support mod. (っ◔◡◔)っ I also want to point out that the bait system wasn’t chosen randomly. description: ﻿ApocalipseBR - Projeto Nemesis Build 42 - Multiplayer Compatible A Resident Evil–inspired boss zombie mod that brings the relentless Nemesis to Project Zomboid. He will find you. What Does This Mod Do? This mod adds a boss-tier zombie wearing the iconic Nemesis outfit that the server automatically spawns near players using an escalating pressure system. The longer you survive without encountering him, the more inevitable his arrival becomes. It works by converting a zombie inside a range to the infamous Nemesis, and he's not like any other zombie: Sprinter - he runs. Always. Superhuman toughness - takes up to 10 hits to bring down (configurable). Hawk vision & pinpoint hearing - he detects you from far away. Long memory & navigation - he remembers where you are and pathfinds toward you. Active redirect - even if distracted, he re-targets the nearest player every few seconds. Doors and barricades - Nemesis does an icreased damage to doors and barricades, there's no stopping him. Also includes the Mr. X outfit as a secondary visual variant. Mr. X is slightly less armored but still uses the same boss module stats. Players cannot equip the Nemesis or Mr. X suits - the mod blocks wearing them from context menus, drag-and-drop, and as a safety net on clothing update events. Pressure Spawn System The server runs a background pressure loop every in-game minute: Pressure increases by a configurable amount each minute (default: +3). When pressure reaches the threshold (default: 30), a spawn roll is attempted. The roll has a configurable success chance (default: 10%). If the roll succeeds, Nemesis spawns 30–45 tiles away from a random eligible player. On spawn or failed roll, pressure resets to zero and the cycle begins again. There is no limit on how much Nemesis can be active at a time - too frequent spawn chances in the sandbox and you may be getting swarmed by Nemesis. With default settings, expect roughly 10 minutes of calm before the first threshold hit, and then it's a dice roll each cycle. Tension builds because you know he's coming - just not exactly when. Sound Design Nemesis has a full 3D positional audio system. All vanilla zombie sounds are suppressed on Nemesis-outfit zombies and replaced with custom ones: Theme music - a looping ambient track audible within 60 tiles. You'll hear him before you see him. "S.T.A.R.S." voice line - plays when Nemesis first detects you (40-tile range). Unmistakable warning. Roars - periodic roars (3 variants) on an 8-second cooldown with a 40% chance per cycle, audible up to 80–100 tiles away. Grunts - plays when Nemesis takes a hit (2 variants, 50% chance), audible within 40 tiles. All sound ranges, cooldowns, and chances are configurable through Sandbox Options. You can tune or mute any layer. Sandbox Options Everything is tunable from the server sandbox settings page: Admin Commands Admins can manually summon a Nemesis or Mr. X at any coordinates (though this fails to summon the zombie sometimes and i couldn't figure out why): /createhorde2 -x 10600 -y 9800 -z 0 -count 1 -outfit Nemesis -health 4.5 /createhorde2 -x 10600 -y 9800 -z 0 -count 1 -outfit MrX -health 2.0 There's one detail about summoning them by hand is that the code that spawns it contains a set of properties that are set to the zombie during the conversion of a normal zombie into nemesis, there is no way for me to hook into the spawn zombie command, use this as a command to test the outfit, but summoning this way will not apply any of the Nemesis actual features like sprinting or the sounds. It is a technical limitation of the engine that would make everything just harder to code. What to Expect A slow-burn tension loop that keeps you on edge throughout your session. Audio cues that let you gauge distance and react - or panic. A genuine threat that forces you to think about escape routes, weapon durability, and positioning. Works on dedicated servers with multiple players - Nemesis picks a random target each spawn. Fully configurable difficulty - dial him up for horror, or tone him down for a manageable challenge. A genuine pure rush of adrenaline, specially when it comes unexpected. Known Issues Nemesis zombies can get stuck attacking doors and windows easily. [FIXED] - He breaks doors and barricades despite roleplay state Nemesis may fail to pathfind correctly when spawned too far away from the target player. [Not something i can fix] - I've limited the maximum range in sandbox to an acceptable value to avoid missconfiguration In roleplay zones where door attacks do not deal damage, zombies attacking doors can still be converted into Nemesis, causing Nemesis to get stuck inside those roleplay areas. [FIXED] - the same fix of Nemesis getting stuck on doors and windows easily apply here No knwon issues are in place anymore, if you have any issue feel free to share! Future planned features Rare items drop table: guns, ammo, armor, etc Credits Original B41 ResidentEvilNemesis assets: Nemeth Workshop ID: 3706463588 Mod ID: ApocalipseBrProjetoNemesis

description: The Ark The Ark is a direct sequel to the Bandits: Week One mod, continuing the story after the dramatic events of the first chapter. You awaken from a coma; disorientated, changed and discover that the world — and your place in it — is no longer the same. Unlike Week One, The Ark delivers a quite different experience. This is a narrative-driven adventure focused on progression, discovery, and atmosphere. The story unfolds step by step, drawing you deeper into a world filled with mystery and unanswered questions. The story will lead you to the answer for the ultimate question about the Knox Infection. Expect rich lore, unexpected twists, and carefully placed surprises as you explore new locations and encounter new events. The mod introduces original gameplay mechanics designed specifically to support the story and immerse you in its themes. Your choices, observations, and persistence matter. The Ark is not just about survival and not about you only — it’s about uncovering the truth, forming connection with other human, and facing moments of challenge. This is a slower, more deliberate journey meant to be experienced, not rushed, but there is also a lot of intense action moments. What is the Ark? The Ark is a SINGLE-PLAYER ONLY mod for Project Zomboid Build 42. It is a total conversion of PZ that revamps the entire map and adds custom elements including NPC's. It is intended to be played through slowly, and offers a story-driven campaign that has probably never been attempted at this scale. This mod cannot be played like vanilla Project Zomboid, it is meant to be explored slowly and methodically. What to expect? This mod is an immersive story that has hundreds of quest lines, where you will explore the ruins of Knox Country, discover the lore of the mysterious Arks, the outbreak of the Knox infection and your place in this apocalypse. But, this story is not just about you: You have others to consider, and their survival is important as your own. This mod is difficult and even the most seasoned PZ players will struggle with some of the changes in the world. Be on your toes at any moment. How to play? This mod requires unstable B42 version of the game as well as [B42] Bandits NPC and [B42] Waterpipes mods to run. It is recommended that you play through this mod without any additional mods, ESPECIALLY mods that will overwrite zombie behaviour, zombies, and survival items such as gas masks/hazmat suits. It is also recommended that you do not change the default settings in Sandbox for your first playthrough. It is recommended that you back up your saves frequently. Death comes knocking at every door and at every opportunity. Copy the files in your X:\Users\YourName\Zomboid\Saves\Sandbox\ARK_vX.XXX_Date-Time to a separate folder. If you die, replace the files in that folder with the backup files and overwrite them. Similar to Week One, you can talk with NPC's by pressing the T key, however you will not be expected to type out what you want to say to other NPC's. You can also interact with other NPC's by holding down the Q key, which will give you commands such as to follow/stay and other opportunities to interact with them. The Ark features a central computer, called NOAH, that gives you information about the situation within the Ark. You can interact with it by right clicking on the terminal. You can exit the interaction window by either walking away from the terminal or by closing the terminal by exiting all of the menus. It is vital that you maintain the Ark. This means keeping it fueled, stocked and functioning to ensure survival deep underground. Things such as generators, decontamination chambers and vents all need maintenance to keep running smoothly. Radiation exposure is a major hazard when travelling out of the Ark. It is essential that you prepare for the nuclear winter that has followed the nuclear detonation. Wearing an intact hazmat suit and a gas mask with working filters is important. If you are exposed to radiation, taking Potassium Iodine pills can help to lower your radiation levels, but it is a gradual process and will not take away radiation right away. Do not eat irradiated items without taking them through decontamination first. Lore documents can be explored by clicking on the arrow buttons at the bottom of the page. Important items will be highlighted once you get close to them. Please do not post spoilers here. I reserve the right to delete them. I ran into an error, what should I do? The Ark has been in testing for months, however errors are expected to come up due to how complex the mod is. If you encounter errors, please report them to Slayer's Discord. Please do not report errors that are due to mod conflicts. Donations If you like my work, be sure to give it a LIKE or: Known Issues Player body or some body parts are invisible - restart the game Emma is stuck - hold Q, select Movement and Follow me, go with her to some other location and then hold Q, select Movement and Don't follow. Enabling Living Skeletons can cause issues with targeting. It is recommended that you do not enable this option. Endure. Music Here is a playlist of all tracks in the mod. description: About this mod: This mod makes your diet actually matter by having a simulated gut health, and adds two of the most basic human needs, urinating and defecating. ------------------------------ FEATURES ------------------------------ Fully simulated gut health that tracks what you eat and drink over a period of time, and either improves or damages your gut health based on what you've eaten. Good gut health gives higher endurance regen and slower fatigue, bad gut health gives the opposite. Food related illnesses. Eating too much greasy/sugary/fat foods or drinking too much soda too fast can cause stomach cramps and heart burn. Consistent bad diet can cause frequent diarrhea or constipation. Bladder and bowels that fills up as you play. Drinking and eating will fill it up faster, with simulated digestion meaning it's not an instant fill when you ingest something, but builds up faster the more you eat. Urinate and defecate in toilets, on trees or bushes, in a fluid container, or on the ground. Where you relieve yourself matters, use toilets to avoid unhappiness, if you can't find one then a tree or bush is better than just out in the open. Make sure to wipe using toilet paper, rags, socks or towels to avoid a mess after. Control system for bladder and bowels. Based on what you eat/drink, your health, traits, and panic level, you have varying control over your bladder and bowels, which makes you more or less likely to have accidents. System for urine and feces getting on clothing. Visible dynamic stains for urine and feces on clothing. Leaving soiled clothing to dry can cause permanent damage to the clothing and the stains won't wash out. System for urine and feces getting on your body. If you don't clean urine or feces from your body in time, then you can get a rash that will turn into an infection. Custom smell system. Soiled clothing, unflushed toilets or urine/feces on the ground will leave a bad smell that attracts nearby zombies. The smell travels realistically in buildings and can be cut off by closing doors. Custom UI as a tab in the health panel. Track your intake, see your current gut status, your control level, any illnesses or statuses. Also take actions like checking your pants and wiping/washing yourself. New items. Medications and supplements to help manage your gut health and illnesses. Custom animations for all actions. Sounds for all actions. New moodles and traits. Fully MP compatible. ---------------------------- MOD INCOMPATIBILITIES ---------------------------- It's FULLY COMPATIBLE with Take a Shower and Bath (just needs a tweak to the moodle positions because we use different moodle frameworks) For Lifestyle: Hobbies do this: 1. description: Expand your vision Project Zomboid hides a lot of what's actually visible to your character behind walls, trees, and floors above. PeekAView extends three rendering passes so your screen catches up with your character's eyes. Three independent features: Wall cutaway: walls are cut away at greater range, so corners and doorways reveal what's behind them earlier as you approach. Tree fade: trees in your view become translucent. Spot zombies behind tree lines where line of sight reaches; safer driving with earlier hazard visibility. Stair view: the upper floor renders while you're climbing, so you see what's upstairs before you reach it. Same rules as vanilla. No X-ray, no see-through walls, no enemy outlines. Your character's line of sight still decides what's actually visible. Settings Each feature is independent. Run all three together, just the one you need, or somewhere in between. Every feature has its own Enable toggle, and the wall and tree fade ranges are tunable in the Options menu. Options → Mods → Peek a View, four sections: Global, Wall cutaway, Tree fade, Stair view. F8 toggles the master Enable in-game (green/red halo confirms; rebindable in Options → Keybind under [PeekAView]). Requirements PZ Build 42.13 or later ZombieBuddy, one-time install for any Java mod Compatibility Safe to add or remove mid-save: no save data touched. Visual effects clear on the next save reload after removing the mod from the mod list. Client-side only: each player who wants the effect needs the mod (and ZombieBuddy) installed. FAQ Does it conflict with the Staircast Workshop mod? No. If both are subscribed, PeekAView detects Staircast at runtime and yields its own stair view so the two can run together. Does it work in multiplayer? Yes, client-side only. Every client also needs ZombieBuddy installed. What does "Fix B42 Wall-Hiding Bug" actually do? The mod's wider cutaway amplifies a vanilla B42 quirk where upper-floor walls vanish next to player-built structures, leaving wall holes from certain angles. The toggle (on by default, outdoor-only) suppresses that. Trade-off: a floor-tile sliver often stays visible on one outer-wall cell, and player-built decks attached to vanilla walls render more visibly at the facade. I picked it as the lesser evil for overall immersion. If your save doesn't have heavy player-built geometry attached to vanilla houses on the camera-facing sides, or if you don't use the wall cutaway feature, you can toggle it off for closer-to-vanilla rendering. I accidentally declined PeekAView in the ZombieBuddy approval prompt. Can I undo it? ZombieBuddy keeps each decision in %USERPROFILE%\.zombie_buddy\mod_approvals.json. Open the file, find the "id": "PeekAView" block(s) where "decision": false, flip false to true, save, restart PZ. If editing JSON sounds risky, just delete those PeekAView blocks instead and ZombieBuddy will re-ask on next save load. Does it affect performance? Several caches keep the runtime cost close to vanilla. Standing still and walking on foot are the cheapest paths. Lower the range sliders if your hardware struggles. Maintenance & Source This mod is feature-complete for my use and no longer actively developed. Last tested against PZ build 42.18. PeekAView is MIT-licensed and fully open source. The patches only touch specific PZ rendering classes. Forks and improvements are welcome and encouraged. If a maintained successor appears, I'll link to it here. PeekAView: github.com/armakupub/PeekAView Issues and PRs will be read but I can't promise response times. If the mod breaks in a future PZ version and I'm not going to fix it, I'll remove it from the Workshop rather than leave a broken version up. Attribution Cutaway-on-stairs idea + FakeFrameState pattern + choice of patched render classes: copiumsawsed/pz-Staircast (MIT, original Workshop mod). Read-path implementation fork: armakupub/staircast-rp (MIT). PeekAView extensions on the staircast-rp foundation: upper-floor zombies stay visible throughout the climb, as long as they're in your character's line of sight. description: Attachment Stats Tooltip Adds auto-generated stat effect lines to weapon-attachment tooltips (scopes, suppressors, muzzle brakes, grips, etc.). What it shows For attachments that declare numeric modifiers on their item script (vanilla pattern), the tooltip gains color-coded lines like: Hit Chance: +10% Aiming Time: -5 (green = lower is better) Recoil Delay: -3 (green) Damage / Max Range / Clip Size deltas Mods supported Any vanilla-pattern firearms mod (modifiers declared on item scripts: HitChanceModifier, AimingTimeModifier, RecoilModifier, etc.). Real Firearms — runtime suppressor sound math is mirrored as a known-effect note (-80% sound radius / volume on RF_*_Suppressor). SWMG-framework mods (Gunworks_gang_framework, used by Guns of Marz and others) — reads the CustomStatsAttachments registry directly and renders multiplier lines (x1.10 Hit Chance, x0.80 Aiming Time, etc.). A shared-state probe wraps StatsFactory.Multiply/Set at load time to capture stat metadata. How it works Client-side only. Wraps ISToolTipInv.render to temporarily replace the WeaponPart's Java DoTooltip method during one render pass, then restores it. The vanilla tooltip is untouched; we just append a tagged "--- Effects ---" section. Compatibility Safe with any mod that doesn't already custom-render WeaponPart tooltips. If you spot an attachment that should show stats but doesn't, message the uploader with the mod name — most likely cause is the mod uses a third stat-dispatch system we haven't probed yet. Changelog v2 — SWMG / Guns of Marz support (registry probe + tooltip-time rendering). v1 — Initial release. Vanilla item-script modifiers + Real Firearms runtime suppressor mirror.

description: EBF Chainsaw Standalone Chainsaw System for Project Zomboid Build 42.19 This mod adds a standalone and fully functional chainsaw system for Project Zomboid Build 42.19. The chainsaw can be equipped, started, turned off, refueled, emptied, used as a weapon, and used to cut trees. It has its own fuel system, chain condition system, radial menu support, context menu actions, custom icons, sounds, animations, and multiplayer-focused behavior. MAIN FEATURES Standalone chainsaw item. Actions to start and turn off the chainsaw. Fuel system with gasoline capacity. Add gasoline using a fuel can. Remove gasoline from the chainsaw. Chain system with install and remove actions. Chain wear when cutting trees and attacking zombies. Broken chains can fall off during use. The chainsaw can still be started without a chain, but it cannot cut properly or deal full damage. Custom radial menu using the V key while holding the chainsaw. Context menu actions with proper icons. Multiplayer-compatible client-side processing. Compatible with saves using Authentic Z, while keeping the EBF chainsaw mechanics independent. CRAFTING The mod includes a manual that teaches the chainsaw recipes: Start Chainsaw Turn Off Chainsaw Remove Chainsaw Chain Install Chainsaw Chain Create Chainsaw Chain Create Heavy Chain Link You can craft chainsaw chains using metalworking tools and materials. Chainsaw chain crafting uses welding animations, welding sound, and requires a valid crafting surface. GAMEPLAY NOTES The chainsaw uses gasoline and chain durability separately. Fuel is consumed during use. The chain wears down when cutting trees or hitting zombies. If the chain breaks, it will be automatically removed from the chainsaw. The chainsaw makes noise while turned on. The chainsaw becomes even louder when cutting trees. CHAIN SYSTEM The chainsaw chain is an important part of the system. Without a chain: The chainsaw can still be started. It cannot cut trees properly. It does not deal full damage. With a chain installed: The chainsaw can cut trees. It can be used more effectively as a weapon. The chain loses condition during use. A damaged chain can break and fall off. COMPATIBILITY Designed for Project Zomboid Build 42.19. Standalone mod. Does not require Authentic Z. Does not require any other chainsaw mod. Designed to work safely alongside Authentic Z. This allows players to use the EBF chainsaw mechanics without depending on other mods. AUTHENTIC Z COMPATIBILITY NOTICE This mod includes compatibility support designed to work alongside Authentic Z variations, while keeping the EBF chainsaw system independent. Compatibility check result: Authentic Z - Current uses AuthenticZClothing.Chainsaw and AuthenticZClothing.ChainsawOff: compatible. Authentic Z - Lite uses AuthenticZLite.Chainsaw and AuthenticZLite.ChainsawOff: compatible. Authentic Z - Backpacks+ does not appear to have an active chainsaw in the Build 42 package, but the old AuthenticZBackpacksPlus.* types are already covered. The Authentic Z 42 chainsaw menu and tooltip scripts are commented out in a block, so they should not compete with the EBF system actions. EBFsawskins does not need adjustment: it depends on EBF recognizing the chainsaw, and the system now also recognizes the Authentic Z Lite chainsaw. Important: EBF Chainsaw does not depend on Authentic Z to work. Compatibility only exists so that players using Authentic Z can also safely use the EBF chainsaw mechanics. MULTIPLAYER SUPPORT This mod was designed with multiplayer compatibility in mind. Chainsaw actions, the fuel system, chain system, sounds, and animations were created to work safely in multiplayer environments. IMPORTANT NOTE This is a standalone EBF chainsaw system. It does not replace the mechanics of other chainsaw mods. It adds its own chainsaw logic, recipes, sounds, animations, and gameplay behavior. description: KR CoreOS The shared core behind all KR mods. KR CoreOS is a backend library required by KR mods. It doesn't add items or gameplay mechanics on its own — it provides the shared infrastructure that powers loot distribution, vehicle spawns, and mod extensibility across the entire KR ecosystem. Install it alongside any KR mod that requires it. No configuration needed. ⚙️ What It Provides Item Distribution API — Registers items into ProceduralDistributions using shared location groups (military, survival, electronics, fridge, kitchen, and more). Dependent mods call a single function — KRCore handles the rest. Vehicle Distribution API — Registers custom vehicles into VehicleZoneDistribution so they spawn naturally across the world in appropriate zones. Care Package Protocol — A lightweight extensibility system that allows future KR mods to register themselves and receive content additions without touching each other's code. 📦 Mods That Use It KR FriOS — Portable fridges, freezers, stoves, solar charger, and the refrigerated FriOS StepVan. KR Solar Charger — Standalone solar charger for vanilla batteries and car batteries. 🔧 Compatibility Build 41 (41.78.7) ✔ Build 42 (42.17.0) ✔ Singleplayer ✔ Multiplayer ✔ No known mod conflicts 🛠️ For Modders KR CoreOS is open to any mod — not just KR mods. If you're a modder and want your items to distribute naturally across the world without writing hundreds of lines of distribution tables, you can declare KR CoreOS as a dependency and register your items through its API with just a few lines of Lua. Call KRCore.dist.add(itemId, groups) to register an item across any combination of location groups. Call KRCore.dist.addVehicle(vehicleId, zones) to register a custom vehicle into world spawn zones. No need to touch ProceduralDistributions or VehicleZoneDistribution directly. Full documentation — including group names, weight guidelines, and a working example — is available in the mod discussion. 🔭 Future Content KR CoreOS is the foundation for all upcoming KR mods. As new mods are released, they will declare KR CoreOS as a dependency and register through its API — no updates to existing mods required. Check out my other mods! BetterPush — The Domino Effect Fully Compatible with : Buttstroke / Gun Stock Attack [B42] MAJOR FIX : Domino Effect should now only trigger on pushing animations, not on weapon swinging or bumping players Turn your shove into a weapon. One push. A whole line falls. Ever wished your character's raw strength actually mattered when you push zombies? BetterPush adds a satisfying chain-reaction mechanic to the shove action. At high strength levels, shoving a zombie has a chance to trigger a domino effect — the zombie you pushed stumbles into the one behind it, which stumbles into the next, and so on. Each zombie falls one after another with a realistic staggered delay, just like real dominoes toppling in a line. Features Dynamic Strength Scaling — As your character gets stronger, you become deadlier. Both the chance to trigger a domino push AND the maximum number of zombies you can knock down dynamically increase as you level up your Strength! Domino Chain Reaction — When triggered, zombies behind your target fall one by one in the direction you pushed. The chain only continues through zombies that are physically close to each other — if there's a gap, the chain breaks. Chance-Based — It's a reward, not a guarantee. Every trigger feels earned. Staggered Knockdown — Zombies don't all drop at once. Each one falls roughly 0.6 seconds after the previous, creating a smooth, cinematic cascade effect. Singleplayer & Multiplayer — Fully compatible with both. In multiplayer, knockdowns are synchronized through the server so all players see the effect. Fully Customizable Sandbox Options — Every parameter is adjustable in-game through the Sandbox Settings menu, complete with hover-over descriptions. Sandbox Options BetterPushMinStrengthLevel — The Strength level where the push effect first becomes possible (0–10, default: 5). BetterPushMaxStrengthLevel — The Strength level where you reach your absolute maximum push potential (0–10, default: 10). BetterPushMinChance — The base chance to trigger a domino push when at minimum strength (0–100%, default: 5%). BetterPushMaxChance — The maximum chance to trigger a domino push when at max strength (0–100%, default: 30%). BetterPushMinZombies — The base maximum number of zombies knocked down in a chain when at minimum strength (1–20, default: 1). BetterPushMaxZombies — The absolute maximum number of zombies knocked down in a chain when at max strength (1–20, default: 4). BetterPushLineDistance — How close zombies must be to each other (front to back) to continue falling in the chain (0.6–5.0 tiles, default: 0.8). BetterPushLineWidth — How wide the lateral tolerance is when finding the next zombie in the chain (0.6–5.0 tiles, default: 0.8). How It Works You shove a zombie (Spacebar). The mod checks your Strength. If you meet the minimum level, it rolls a chance to trigger based on how strong you are. If successful, it calculates how many zombies you can push down (which also scales with Strength) and traces a line from you. It looks for the closest zombie behind the target — they must be nearly touching. That zombie falls. Then the next. Then the next. Each one drops with a slight delay, creating the domino cascade. Compatibility Build 42.17 Unstable Singleplayer ✔ Multiplayer ✔ Should be compatible with most other mods — BetterPush only safely hooks into the OnWeaponHitCharacter event and does not override any vanilla files. Tips Works best against tightly packed hordes — the zombies need to be shoulder-to-shoulder for the chain to connect. Pairs well with traits and mods that boost Strength. One push. Watch them fall. If you would like to support me, I would appreciate it :) <3 Workshop ID: 3715137752 Mod ID: BetterPush

description: Dynamic Horde Events Tired of sitting safely inside your base while absolutely nothing happens? Cleared the neighborhood, boarded the windows, stacked food for three months, and now the apocalypse feels more like a sad farming simulator? Dynamic Horde Events adds highly configurable incoming zombie horde events to Project Zomboid. Sometimes the dead will find you. Sometimes you will hear them before you see them. And sometimes the sky itself will tell you that staying home was a terrible idea. This mod is designed to bring back pressure, danger, and unpredictability without turning every day into a constant zombie flood. 🎲Core Features Random Horde Events At configurable time intervals, a horde can spawn at a distance from the player and begin moving toward them. You can configure: Direct player target minimum and maximum time between horde events horde size spawn radius cooldown between events night-time spawning rules attraction radius and volume The goal is simple: make the world feel dangerous again, even after you cleared your local area. Now you almost have to barricade windows and doors since they can come even at your night sleep 🚶‍♂️🚶🚶‍♀️Wandering Horde Events Wandering Hordes are different from normal horde attacks. Instead of being attracted directly toward the player’s position, a Wandering Horde is spawned on one side of the player and guided toward a point beyond the player’s area. In simple terms: Spawn Side ---> Player Area ---> Exit Direction This means the horde can pass through or near your location instead of directly hunting you. If you stay quiet, hide, and avoid making noise, the horde may pass by. If you shoot, drive, trigger an alarm, use loud tools, or make too much noise, the situation can quickly become your problem. Wandering Hordes are meant to create tense “hold your breath and don’t move” moments. 🔊Survivor Voice Lines Your character can react when a horde is coming. Project Zomboid Needs More Bugs Spawn real-time rendered bugs around outdoor lights Bugs are active in the summer months Bugs are most active when it's warm and not raining Bugs are attracted to active light sources Mod Options control the number and size of bugs Mod Option to toggle if bugs are active all year Mod Option to turn off temperature and rain limited spawn rates Mod Option so bugs can spawn both day and night Includes an "addBug™ function" to add your own bugs Safe to add at any time or remove, but why? For B42 SP & MP Check out JB's Fireflies for even more bugs! Adding your own bugs model: This is the name of the 3D item model used for the bug, like "Base.Plushabug" size: This determines the scale of the 3D item. 1.0 represents the full size of the item, a good range would be 0.05 to 0.8 for bugs speed: This sets the base velocity applied to the bug during movement. A good range is 0.0001 to 0.01, since higher values can cause the bug to move too fast to see yawOffset: This is a degree adjustment used to ensure the "front" of your 3D model faces the actual direction of travel. The range is 0 to 360, and typical values are 0, 90 or 180 depending on how the model was exported crazyFactor: This controls the amount of random "jitter" or "crazy"" added to the bug's velocity every frame. A good range is 0.00001 to 0.02; higher values create frantic, crack-head movement, while lower values looks like a steady drift lightAttraction: This is how strongly the bug is "pulled" toward the light source. A range of 0.001 to 0.5 is good. Higher values make the bugs stick too close to the light source areaOfInterest: This is the radius in squares/tiles around the light source where the bug will spend its life. A good range is 0.1 to 1.5 minFrames and maxFrames: This defines the lifespan of a single bug instance in update ticks before it despawns. A suitable range is 30 to 600, which is roughly 1 to 10 seconds of activity at 60 FPS Example mod put in lua/client: local BugPattern = require("jb_BugPatterns") local bug = { model = "Base.Plushabug", size = 0.06, speed = 0.001, yawOffset = 90, crazyFactor = 0.01, lightAttraction = 0.001, areaOfInterest = 0.5, minFrames = 180, maxFrames = 600, } BugPattern.addBug(bug) Workshop ID: 3717902500 Mod ID: JB_BugsInLights

description: Enjoy a less overwhelming inventory management! We can even Shift+Click afterwards pour transfer the selection! Smart stacking Icons Inventory has its own stacking logic that should feel natural: Small items always stack (two bandages stack, but two baseball bats don't) Over a certain amount, bigger items stack anyways (4 or more by default) These parameters can be configured in options > mods. Feedback on these features and preferred parameters would be appreciated! Fast transfer Shift+Click has been a standard since ages in game inventories. It fits especially well here as we have a lot of stuff to manage! The original multi-select gesture is still possible with Ctrl+Shift+Click. Hybrid view Right-Click the top bar to change the view. You can now switch to a detailed view when you open your base storage! Controller bindings The D-Pad alone can move you through both player and loot windows naturally. However I felt that having a quicker way to switch windows was necessary. So in current design, LB/L1 and RB/R1 have been supercharged: Press and hold + Up/Down to navigate containers Press and hold + Left/Right to switch focus to the other window Tapping is not changed (cycle containers or whatever vanilla decides) In any case I'm very interested in your feedback, especially if you play on controller! Built to last Icons Inventory comprehensively integrates with vanilla to let it manage logic as much as possible, which should avoid breakage in future versions or facilitate upgrades. OVERVIEW Anomalies is a hardcore mod that introduces randomly generated anomalous events, bringing entirely new challenges to your exploration in Knox Country. RADIOACTIVE ANOMALOUS ZONES Toxic: A deadly radioactive zone. Always wear your gas mask and monitor your filters so they don't run out when you need them most. Frost: This anomaly has its own freezing microclimate. Bundle up to stay warm, wear your gas mask, and keep an eye on your filters. Thermal: An area of extreme heat where objects, houses, and zombies will be engulfed in flames. Wear light clothing, keep your gas mask on, and manage your filters carefully. Radioactive anomalous zones do not stay in the same place forever; they dissipate as you move away from them. This means a place that was once radioactive might not be anymore, just as a place that was completely clear can suddenly become radioactive. description: The Director [B42.18 MP and SP] "It's not just spawning zombies. It's deciding what to do about you." A cognitive AI for Project Zomboid. Server-side overseer that watches every move you make, builds a Bayesian model of who you are as a player, and writes a different scenario for every survivor it meets. Inspired by Left 4 Dead's AI Director, but pushed several decades forward in capability. What it actually does Every cycle, an 18-module cognitive pipeline runs end to end: Perceive - events tagged with semantic context (loud, aggressive, vulnerable, at_night, in_storm_phase) Remember - short-term episodic memory consolidates into long-term narrative beats (firefight, hubris, near-death recovery, betrayal) Model you - Bayesian Beta distributions track paranoid, confident, methodical, aggressive, hoarder, explorer, expert beliefs that tighten as evidence accumulates Predict you - a Theory-of-Mind layer models what you think the Director will do next, so it can subvert your expectations Deliberate - generates 5-10 candidate plans, simulates your likely response via Monte Carlo rollout, scores them on 7 competing objectives Learn - a UCB1 multi-armed bandit Q-table records what works on you specifically across 420 state buckets; persists across save/load Reflect - every 30 in-game minutes, the Director self-critiques and adjusts strategy Narrate - procedural taunts reference your actual history ("You came back to that street. Brave. Or stupid.") Action vocabulary The Director picks from 12 tactical levers each cycle, weighted by a learned-reward bandit: spawn_horde - walker / fast_shambler / fake_shambler / sprinter / crawler / mixed. The two new tiers landed in v1.2.0 via B42.18's per-zombie speed API. Tier is gated by belief: fake shamblers (look slow, then run when you commit) are reserved for players who actually scout before engaging - a charger would read them the same as walkers, so the trick has no audience. Fast shamblers fill the buildup band; sprinters are saved for the climax. lure_existing / redirect_zombies - pulls or nudges nearby zombies via a world-sound source siege_phase - sustained multi-cycle pressure at intensity 1-5 ambient_sound / phantom_gunshot / broadcast_static - atmospheric cues that don't spawn anything but make you check the corners meta_event_nudge - bumps a Knox Event helicopter (or similar) at a thematically-fitting moment weather_nudge - pushes weather toward whatever the persona prefers taunt - procedural chat referencing your actual profile and history wait - enforced relax windows (the same trick L4D uses) cull_distant - removes off-screen zombies to make room for fresh pressure Personas Pick the Director's voice in sandbox options: Patient - long lulls, rare big strikes Sadistic - targets your weakest moments (low HP, sleeping, low ammo) Tactical - methodical, consistent pressure Narrator - heavy taunting, theatrical pacing Cross-mod awareness The Director auto-detects every active mod on the server and adapts. Hand-written adapters ship for Warlord, Calm Before The Storm, Here They Come!, Bandits NPC, Helicopter Event Framework, and Hordes Alpha. Mods we've never heard of get conservative defaults via name-keyword detection. Other mod authors can ship their own adapter without forking The Director - drop a ZT_Adapter_YourName.lua file in the Adapters folder and it auto-loads. See the Discussions tab for the adapter protocol. Persistent across sessions Every belief, every Q-value, every narrative beat, every persona drift is saved. Load your save a week later and the Director continues the campaign it was running. Tactician Notes Right-click in the world, "Zombie Tactician", "Open Tactician Notes" for a live, color-coded panel showing the Director thinking in real time. Watch each cycle's perception, beliefs, projected outcomes, decision rationale, and self-reflection scroll by like an LLM monologue. Other admin tools in the same menu: Dump Brain State, Force Cycle Now, Reset Learned Data. Compatibility Build 42.18 unstable Singleplayer and dedicated MP (per-player belief tracking) Pure Lua. No external services, no API keys, no network calls Save-safe: persistence migrates between schema versions automatically A note on what this is This mod is the result of building, from scratch in Lua, what an LLM would have done if Project Zomboid's kahlua sandbox allowed network access. It mimics LLM-style cognition (multi-step reasoning, persistent beliefs, theory-of-mind, reflection) without being one. Every implicit LLM capability is an explicit module. It is also early. Beliefs may drift in unexpected ways. Personas may need tuning. The Tactician Notes panel is your friend - open it, watch the brain reason, and report what feels off. Credits Architecture inspired by Mike Booth (L4D AI Director), Dave Mark (Behavioral Mathematics for Game AI), Jeff Orkin (F.E.A.R. GOAP) Step right up. Support If my mods saved your save (or your sanity), a coffee keeps the late-night debugging going. Every tip funds more time spent reverse-engineering kahlua quirks so you don't have to. Buy me a coffee on Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/grphx Workshop ID: 3720305815 Mod ID: ZombieTactician

description: Please read the description before leaving a comment. This mod adds friendly survivors. There are no hostile survivors. Build a base, gather companions, and create a small community. This is not a detailed life simulation mod for living together with NPCs. It is a compact and intuitive player-support mod designed to make lonely survival a little easier with the help of NPCs. You cannot give NPCs detailed commands, and they do not need food. The available commands are limited to having them defend the base, follow the player and assist in combat, and exchange items. However, each NPC occupation has its own traits. Depending on their occupation, NPCs can support you with things such as vehicle maintenance, farming, water collection, healing, and item gathering. ───── How to Play ───── 1. Set a Base Set a safe location as your Base from the right-click menu. You cannot recruit NPCs until a base has been set. 2. Find and Recruit Survivors NPCs wander around the world. After setting a base, you can recruit them from the right-click menu. Recruited NPCs can either follow you or wait at the base. Following NPCs stay near the player and try to fight nearby enemies. You can also encounter NPCs by consuming a walkie-talkie. 3. Custom NPC You can create one Custom NPC. After setting a base, you can create them from the right-click menu while you are inside the base. 4. Shared Storage Shared Storage is a withdrawal-only container used to receive items collected by NPCs. It can only be opened from the right-click menu while the player is inside the base. NPCs stationed at the base have a low chance to collect items. The collection interval and amount can be adjusted in the sandbox settings. In addition, some occupations may bring back extra items through their base traits, separate from normal collection. 5. NPC Management Tag The NPC Management Tag stored in your key ring is an item that contains NPC records. It is used to restore companions’ names, status, equipment, and inventory. There is an automatic recovery system in case it is lost, but please be careful with it. 6. Base Support Abilities Some occupations have base support abilities such as healing, vehicle maintenance, generator maintenance, crop watering, and item generation. These abilities generally only work while the player is inside the same base. Game balance can be adjusted in the sandbox settings. 7. Guard Patrol System If you set guard points and assign NPCs to guard duty, they will move to the guard points. If there are empty guard points, they will patrol between them. ───── Occupation Abilities ───── Each NPC occupation has different combat traits, follow abilities, and base support abilities. Some abilities work while the NPC is following you, while others work when the NPC is stationed at your base. Fire Officer ・Combat: axe attacks always knock down zombies. ・At base: refills rain barrels. Police Officer ・Combat: firearms may knock down zombies. ・At base: rarely collects ammunition. Park Ranger ・Combat: firearm range +10%. ・Following: improves nearby foraging support. Construction Worker ・Following: increases the player’s carry capacity. Security Guard ・At base: melee damage x1.5. ・At base: improves firearm damage and accuracy. Carpenter ・At base: has a chance to add nails. Burglar ・Following: can help unlock doors and vehicle doors. Chef ・At base: has a chance to add cooked meals. Repairman ・At base: repairs doors, windows, and barricades. Livestock Farmer ・At base: waters crops. ・At base: has a chance to add meat. Crop Farmer ・At base: waters crops. ・At base: has a chance to add vegetables or fruit. Fisherman ・At base: has a chance to add fish. Doctor ・Combat: blade damage x1.5. ・At base: heals the player and NPCs inside the base. Veteran ・Combat: improves firearm damage and accuracy. ・At base: rarely collects ammunition. Nurse ・At base: improves healing if a doctor is at the base. Lumberjack ・Combat: axe damage x1.5. ・At base: has a chance to add planks. Fitness Instructor ・Combat: sports weapon damage x1.5. ・Following: increases the player’s carry capacity. Burger Flipper ・At base: has a chance to add a fast food set. Electrician ・At base: repairs and refuels generators. Engineer ・At base: repairs and refuels generators. Metalworker ・At base: has a chance to add metal materials. Blacksmith ・At base: has a chance to add a katana. Mechanic ・At base: repairs vehicle parts. ・At base: has a chance to add spare vehicle parts. Tailor ・At base: has a chance to add thread or ripped sheets. ───── Player Death ───── By default, even if the player dies, NPCs stationed at the base and the contents of Shared Storage will be preserved. NPCs who were following the player will disappear. ───── Known Issues / Important Notes ───── ・Please back up your save data before using this mod. ・This mod can be added to an existing save, but starting a new game is recommended for better stability. ・NPCs may sometimes attack or kill zombies through walls. ・Animations are still generally unstable. NPCs may sometimes freeze during attack animations, and in many cases the weapon animation and the actual attack hit detection may not match properly. ・You can change NPC clothing and weapons, but the save system is still not fully reliable. ・NPC behavior and combat AI are complex, so performance may vary depending on your environment. ・Using this mod together with other NPC mods is not recommended. ・This is a personal project, and AI tools are used during development. ・I may not be able to handle advanced fixes or complex feature requests. ───── Mod Compatibility ───── ・Various weapon mods Reload speed will use the default calculation unless an additional patch is provided. A patch template is included as “NotAlone_CustomReloadPatch_Template.lua”. ・Inventory Tetris https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=2982070344 Reported as compatible, but not fully tested: ・RV Interior ・Bandits Reported as incompatible: ・Brutal Handwork ・Better Helicopter Rework ・ZRAP ───── Questions ───── Build 42? There are currently no plans to support Build 42. Multiplayer? There are no plans to make this mod multiplayer-compatible. Hostile NPCs? There are no hostile NPCs in this mod. There are currently no plans to add them. It doesn’t work. I cannot investigate the issue with only that information. I need more details, such as the error, the situation where it happened, and your mod list. If an error appears, please close the game and check the following file: C:\Users\<YourWindowsUserName>\Zomboid\console.txt The error is usually near the end of the file. ───── Permissions ───── You do not need to ask for permission to create modified versions of this mod. Translations, adjustments, fixes, and separate versions are allowed. ───── Credits ───── This mod is strongly inspired by “Superb Survivors!” and “Superb Survivors Continued”. I respect and thank the original authors. Please do not insult other mods in the comments. Workshop ID: 3720923377 Mod ID: NotAlone_NPC Mod ID: NotAlone_NPC_InventoryTetris
